الاسم العبري וַיִּקְרָא (Vayyiqrā) يعني: The Hebrew name וַיִּקְרָא (Vayyiqrā) means “And He called,” and it is the opening of the book: “And the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting.” Leviticus, however, is associated with the Levites and matters of worship and priesthood, although the book directs its teaching to the whole community of Israel. The central question is: How can a sinful people live in the presence of the holy God? Reference: Leviticus 1:1.
ينسب التقليد اليهودي والمسيحي السفر إلى: Jewish and Christian tradition attributes the book to Moses, and its chapters present Moses as a mediator who receives the word of the Lord and conveys it to the priests and the congregation. The events take place in the wilderness after the exodus, centering on the tent of meeting before entry into the land of Canaan. The text does not provide an absolute calendar date, and what is established in biblical tradition is that Moses died at the age of one hundred and twenty, according to Deuteronomy 34:7.
العلاقة بسفر الخروج: The Relationship to the Book of Exodus
انتهى الخروج بحلول مجد الرب في المسكن، و: Exodus ended with the glory of the Lord coming to rest in the tabernacle, and Leviticus begins from within this presence. Exodus explains how God saved His people and dwelt in their midst, whereas Leviticus answers how the people may approach this holy God. Freedom after redemption is therefore not independence from all authority, but covenant life before God.

It then consecrates Aaron and his sons to the priesthood, showing that service before the sanctuary is a calling within the covenant order, not an independent human privilege. Leviticus 17:11 explains the centrality of blood in atonement, an important background for understanding New Testament language concerning redemption.
القداسة والطهارة ويوم الكفارة: Holiness, Purity, and the Day of Atonement
لا تساوي النجاسة الطقسية دائمًا الخطية ا: Ritual impurity is not always equivalent to moral sin; many purity laws regulate approach to the sanctuary and distinguish between the holy and the common. In Leviticus 16, the high priest enters the Holy of Holies on the Day of Atonement, bringing together the idea of making atonement for sin and removing it from the congregation. References: Leviticus 10:1-3; 11–16.
قانون القداسة والأعياد واليوبيل: The Holiness Code, Feasts, and Jubilee
تمتد القداسة إلى الدم والعلاقات والعدل و: Holiness extends to blood, relationships, justice, and love of neighbor, and is summarized by the statement: “You shall be holy, for I am holy” (Leviticus 11:44); likewise, the command occurs: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself” (Leviticus 19:18). The feasts build a memory of God's acts, while the Sabbath for the land and the Jubilee declare that the land belongs to the Lord and that ownership and economics cannot be separated from the covenant. References: Leviticus 17–25.
توضح قصة ناداب وأبيهو أن النعمة لا تلغي: The story of Nadab and Abihu makes clear that grace does not abolish God's holiness and that worship is not a sphere in which people may do whatever they please. Conversely, the renewal of the relationship with the congregation is highlighted through the system of atonement and covenant; thus the book's laws are not to be read as rules separated from God's mercy and presence.
يمكن تلخيص الرسالة هكذا: الشعب الذي خلصه: The message may be summarized thus: the people whom God saved and called into covenant must live in holiness before the holy God. The system of sacrifices, priesthood, and atonement provides the framework the New Testament uses to understand Christ as the perfect sacrifice, the great high priest, and the final atonement, without turning every detail into an independent symbol. References: John 1:29; Hebrews 9–10.

الاسم العبري בְּמִדְבַּר (Bemidbar) يعني: The Hebrew name בְּמִדְבַּר (Bemidbar) means “In the wilderness,” and it is taken from the beginning of the book in the wilderness of Sinai. Numbers, or Ἀριθμοί, refers to the censuses, but the census serves the picture of an organized community around the tent of meeting. The two names combine the setting of the events and the organization of the people. Reference: Numbers 1:1-3.
ينسب التقليد اليهودي والمسيحي السفر إلى: Jewish and Christian tradition attributes the book to Moses, who appears as leader, mediator, and prophet. The events begin at Sinai after the exodus and proceed to the plains of Moab opposite Jericho. The book does not specify a calendar year for Moses' birth, and it is established that he died at the age of one hundred and twenty, according to Deuteronomy 34:7.
الغرض والعلاقة بالأسفار السابقة: Purpose and Relationship to the Previous Books
إذا شرح اللاويين كيف يعيش الشعب في حضرة: If Leviticus explains how the people live in God's presence, Numbers explains how this people journeys with God in the wilderness. It organizes the people, reveals the testing of faith, and presents grumbling, rebellion, and judgment, while God's faithfulness to His promise continues. The overall progression is: organization, God's leadership, the testing of faith, then arrival at the boundary of promise.

يضع التعداد الأول الرجال القادرين على ال: The first census registers the men able to go to war, and the tribe of Levi is set apart for the service of the tabernacle. The tribes surround the tent of meeting, so that God's presence becomes the center of the nation's identity. When they set out, the movement of the camp is linked to the cloud, the trumpets, and the Lord's direction; the wilderness is a school in which the people learn that food, water, the way, and protection come from God.
يكشف التذمر والمن والسلوى حنينًا مشوهًا: Grumbling, manna, and quail reveal a distorted longing for Egypt and distrust of God's provision. In the story of the spies, Joshua and Caleb see the land in the light of the promise, while the people believe their fear; God therefore judges the rejecting generation not to enter the land. Then Korah's rebellion shows that religious ambition does not become service merely by drawing near to the sanctuary. References: Numbers 11–14; 16.
ماء الصخرة والحية النحاسية: The Water from the Rock and the Bronze Serpent
عند ماء الصخرة يخطئ موسى حين يضرب الصخرة: At the water from the rock, Moses sins when he strikes the rock instead of speaking to it as the Lord commanded, showing that the leader himself is under the judgment of holiness. In Numbers 21, Moses raises the bronze serpent, and whoever looks at it in obedience and faith lives; Christ connects this image with the lifting up of the Son of Man in John 3. References: Numbers 20:1-13; 21:4-9; John 3:14-15.
يحاول بالاق استخدام بلعام ضد إسرائيل، لك: Balak attempts to use Balaam against Israel, but the curse is turned into a blessing, and Balaam's prophecy presents the image of the star coming forth from Jacob. Then the second census declares the emergence of a new generation, and Joshua is appointed as Moses' successor. The leader changes, but God's promise continues. References: Numbers 22–24; 26–27.
الله أمين لوعده، لكن شعبه مدعو أن يسير م: God is faithful to His promise, but His people are called to walk with Him in faith and obedience. People change, generations die, and leaders pass on, but God's faithfulness does not change. Therefore, the wilderness remains a period between promise and fulfillment and a test of the heart, not the end of God's purpose.

The people stand on the plains of Moab between the memory of the wilderness and the threshold of the promised land. Reference: Deuteronomy 1:1-5.
ينسب التقليد اليهودي والمسيحي السفر إلى: Jewish and Christian tradition attributes the book to Moses, who appears as the principal speaker, covenant mediator, and teacher. The final chapter records his death; therefore, scholars discuss its completion and editing in light of tradition and modern study. Reference: Deuteronomy 34:1-7.

Moses brings together history, law, warning, and hope for the renewal of the covenant and the preparation of the people for life in the land, where matters of worship, property, leadership, and justice will arise. References: Deuteronomy 5:1-3; 29:1.
العلاقة بسفر العدد: The Relationship to the Book of Numbers
ينتهي العدد في سهول موآب، ويبدأ التثنية: Numbers ends on the plains of Moab, and Deuteronomy begins from nearly the same region. In Numbers, we see the people in the wilderness under testing; Deuteronomy places them on the threshold and turns the history of failure into a lesson in obedience. It is therefore the theological threshold between journeying and possession.

«اسمع يا إسرائيل: الرب إلهنا رب واحد. فت: “Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one. You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength” (Deuteronomy 6:4-5). Hearing here leads to love and obedience. The warning against forgetting the Lord after fullness and rest is repeated, because blessing itself may become a test of memory and faithfulness. References: Deuteronomy 6:4-9; 8:10-18.
يطلب السفر عبادة الرب وحده، ويضع حدودًا: The book calls for worship of the Lord alone and sets limits for the king, prophet, priest, and judge, so that all are subject to the word of God. It also cares for the sojourner, orphan, widow, and slave, because Israel was a slave and a sojourner in Egypt; memory that does not produce mercy is incomplete memory. References: Deuteronomy 12:1-14; 16:18-20; 17:14-20; 24:17-22.
يضع موسى أمام الشعب الحياة والموت والبرك: Moses sets before the people life and death, blessing and curse, and calls them to choose life. The text does not present choice as a slogan separate from the covenant, but connects it with loving the Lord, listening to His voice, and keeping His commandments. Reference: Deuteronomy 30:15-20.
يشوع وموت موسى: Joshua and the Death of Moses
يسلم موسى القيادة إلى يشوع ويشجعه، ثم يص: Moses hands leadership to Joshua and encourages him, then ascends Mount Nebo and sees the land without entering it. Moses dies, but the leader changes while God's purpose does not change; the promise continues through the new generation and Joshua's leadership. References: Deuteronomy 31:1-8; 34:1-12.

استشهد المسيح بتثنية 6:5 في الوصية العظم: Christ cited Deuteronomy 6:5 in the greatest commandment, and used texts from Deuteronomy when confronting temptation in the wilderness, including, “Man shall not live by bread alone.” The book of Acts also reads the prophet like Moses in Deuteronomy 18:15 in the light of Christ, while Christ remains greater than Moses. The book addresses the people of Israel and later generations to declare that the land is bound to God's promise to the fathers, and that possession does not remove the responsibility of faithfulness to the covenant.

يتحول وعد الأرض إلى أسماء ومدن وحدود وتو: The promise of the land becomes names, cities, boundaries, and distribution among the tribes, while the cities of refuge and the Levitical cities present the picture of an ordered society rather than merely a military victory. Ruth enters the genealogy of Christ according to Matthew 1:5, while Boaz remains a limited type of the redeemer, not equal to Christ.

Saul begins as a promising figure, but pressure from circumstances leads him to transgress the command, and then to keep what had been devoted to destruction in the Amalekite episode. Therefore, the principle comes: “Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice” (1 Samuel 15:22). References: 1 Samuel 8; 9–15.
يمسح صموئيل داود بن يسى في بيت لحم، ويعل: Samuel anoints David son of Jesse in Bethlehem, and the LORD declares that people look at the eyes, but the LORD looks at the heart. David defeats Goliath not by the strength of weapons alone but by his confidence that the battle belongs to the LORD, then waits for God’s timing and refuses to kill Saul despite the opportunity. References: 1 Samuel 16–17; 24; 26.
داود ملكًا وعهد الله معه: David as King and God's Covenant with Him
بعد موت شاول يُمسح داود في حبرون ثم ملكً: After Saul’s death, David is anointed at Hebron and then as king over all Israel; he makes Jerusalem his capital and brings the ark of the covenant there in the proper manner after the incident of Uzzah. In 2 Samuel 7, God declares a covenant with David, linking house, offspring, and throne with a royal hope that expands in the Psalms and the New Testament. References: 2 Samuel 1–6; 7:1-17.
يأخذ داود بثشبع ويدبر موت أوريا، فيواجهه: David takes Bathsheba and arranges Uriah’s death, and Nathan confronts him, saying: “You are the man.” David confesses, but forgiveness does not remove temporal consequences, and turmoil enters his house. The narrative makes clear that David’s election does not make him a sinless man, but highlights the importance of confession, repentance, and submission to God’s word. References: 2 Samuel 11–12; Psalm 51.
انهيار البيت والرجاء: The Collapse of the House and Hope
تظهر مأساة أمنون وثامار، ثم تمرد أبشالوم: The tragedy of Amnon and Tamar appears, followed by Absalom’s rebellion, David’s flight from Jerusalem, and Absalom’s death; the reader sees how the effects of the king’s sin extend into the family and politics. Yet God’s covenant remains in force; David is a repentant king, not a perfect king. References: 2 Samuel 13–20; 22–23.
تقدم الأسفار داود ملكًا ممسوحًا وراعيًا: The books present David as an anointed king, shepherd, and covenant bearer, but they reveal his limitations and create expectation for the perfect king. In the New Testament, Christ comes as the “Son of David” and fulfills what David could not accomplish: He is without sin, and His kingdom does not end in death. References: 2 Samuel 7:12-16; Matthew 1:1; Luke 1:32-33; Acts 2:29-36.

الملوك الأول والثاني — מְלָכִים — Kings: First and Second Kings — מְלָכִים — Kings
دراسة موحدة للسفرين: الهيكل، انقسام المم: A unified study of the two books: the temple, the division of the kingdom, the prophets, reform, and exile
كان الملوك الأول والثاني سفرًا واحدًا في: First and Second Kings were one book in the Hebrew tradition and were later divided. The name מְלָכִים (Melakhim) means “kings,” but the purpose of the book is not merely to recount names; rather, it evaluates kings in the light of the covenant: did the king do what was right in the eyes of the LORD or what was evil? References: 1 Kings 1–2; 2 Kings 25.
لا يذكر السفر كاتبًا محددًا، ويشير إلى س: The book does not name a particular author, and refers to royal records such as the Book of the Acts of Solomon and the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel and Judah. The final author reads history in light of the principles of Deuteronomy, explaining division, downfall, idolatry, and exile as covenantal realities, not merely political ones.
1 ملوك 1–11: نهاية داود وسليمان والهيكل: 1 Kings 1–11: the end of David, Solomon, the temple, and his apostasy; 12–16: the division of the kingdom; 17–22: Elijah and Ahab. 2 Kings 1–13: Elijah and Elisha; 14–17: the fall of Samaria; 18–20: Hezekiah; 21–23: Manasseh and Josiah; 24–25: the fall of Jerusalem and the exile. References: 1 Kings 1–22; 2 Kings 1–25.
يطلب سليمان قلبًا فهيمًا، ثم يبني الهيكل: Solomon asks for an understanding heart, then builds the temple and dedicates it in Jerusalem. The prayer of dedication affirms that the heavens cannot contain God; the temple is a place God chose to reveal His presence, not a building that confines Him or a talisman that protects a disobedient people. References: 1 Kings 3:5-14; 5–8.
انحراف سليمان وانقسام المملكة: The Apostasy of Solomon and the Division of the Kingdom
تُفتح أبواب السقوط بكثرة النساء والثروة: The gates of downfall open through the abundance of women, wealth, and alliances, as women turned Solomon's heart toward other gods. After his death, Rehoboam rejects wise counsel, and the people divide into the northern kingdom of Israel and the southern kingdom of Judah, and Jeroboam establishes the calves for political reasons that become a religious catastrophe. References: 1 Kings 11–12.
إيليا وأخاب والرب هو الله: Elijah, Ahab, and the LORD is God
يواجه إيليا أخاب وإيزابل وعبادة البعل، و: Elijah confronts Ahab, Jezebel, and the worship of Baal, declaring the name 'YHWH is God' as the heart of his message. On Mount Carmel, fire falls after prayer, then comes rain, but Elijah himself passes through exhaustion and despair and experiences God's presence in stillness. References: 1 Kings 17–19.
تنتقل الخدمة من إيليا إلى أليشع، وتظهر م: The ministry passes from Elijah to Elisha, and miracles appear that touch the poor, the sick, and soldiers. In the healing of Naaman, Elisha asks him to wash in the Jordan, and the commander learns that obedience to the word of God is more important than his expectations about how the miracle would occur. References: 2 Kings 2–5.
تسقط السامرة أمام آشور نحو 722 ق.م. بعد: Samaria falls before Assyria around 722 B.C. after the accumulation of disobedience. As for Hezekiah, he seeks the LORD before the threat of Sennacherib, and Josiah begins a reform when the Law is discovered and he restores Passover. But the corruption of Manasseh and the continuation of disobedience lead to the fall of Jerusalem, the burning of the temple, and Babylonian exile. References: 2 Kings 17; 18–20; 22–25.
الرجاء الداودي والمسيح: The Davidic Hope and the Messiah
يثبت السفر أن الهيكل والازدهار لا يعوضان: The book establishes that the temple and prosperity do not compensate for a heart far from God, and that human kings fail. Yet the promise of God to David remains a door of hope, and the lifting of Jehoiachin from prison at the end of the book indicates that the story is not finished. This repeated failure leads to the expectation of the perfect king from the seed of David. References: 2 Kings 25:27-30; Matthew 1:1; Luke 1:32-33.

أخبار الأيام الأول والثاني — דִּבְרֵי הַ: First and Second Chronicles — דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים — Chronicles
دراسة موحدة للعمل الأصلي: الهوية بعد الس: Unified Study of the Work: Identity After the Exile, David, the Temple, Worship, and Hope
وحدة العمل واسمه: The Unity of the Work and Its Name
كان أخبار الأيام الأول والثاني عملًا واح: First and Second Chronicles were originally a single work and were then divided into two books. The Hebrew name דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים means “matters of the days,” whereas the Greek name Paraleipomena became associated with omitted matters. Yet the work is not merely a historical supplement; it is a theological rereading of Israel’s post-exilic history, centered on identity, worship, and Davidic hope.
لا يذكر النص اسم الكاتب. نسب التقليد الي: The text does not mention the name of the author. Jewish tradition attributed the work to Ezra, while scholarly studies use the expression 'the Chronicler' or 'the Historian' and discuss stages of collection and editing. The genealogies point to a post-exilic community, and many scholars favor the final composition in the Persian period, approximately in the second half of the fifth century B.C., with the precise date remaining a matter of discussion.
تبدأ الأنساب من آدم وتمتد إلى إسرائيل وي: The genealogies begin from Adam and extend to Israel, Judah, and David, affirming that the exile did not erase the people's identity and did not cut off God's work in history. After the death of Saul, the narrative moves to the union of Israel around David, then to Jerusalem and the ark of the covenant and the organization of priests, Levites, singers, and gatekeepers. References: 1 Chronicles 1–10; 11–16; 23–29.
عهد داود والاستعداد للهيكل: The Covenant of David and Preparation for the Temple
يعيد 1 أخبار 17 عرض عهد الله مع داود، وي: 1 Chronicles 17 presents the covenant of God with David again, linking the seed, the throne, and the temple. God does not allow David to build the temple, but he prepares gold, silver, bronze, wood, and stones and the system of service, and the leader learns to lay a foundation for a project he may not see completed. References: 1 Chronicles 17; 22:1-19; 28–29.
أخبار الأيام الثاني: سليمان والهيكل: Second Chronicles: Solomon and the Temple
يبدأ السفر الثاني بسليمان وحكمته وبناء ا: The second book begins with Solomon and his wisdom and the building of the temple and its dedication and the bringing in of the ark and the appearance of the glory of the LORD. Solomon's prayer comes as a forward-looking prayer for sin and drought and war and exile, connecting the temple to repentance and the seeking of God's face, not to the building alone. References: 2 Chronicles 1–7.
يركز أخبار الأيام على ملوك يهوذا والإصلا: Chronicles focuses on the kings of Judah and reform and worship. Jehoshaphat appears in teaching the people, Hezekiah in opening the temple and cleansing it and restoring Passover, Manasseh in humility and return, and Josiah in reform after hearing the Law. These narratives reveal that restoration requires prayer and humility and the word of God. References: 2 Chronicles 17; 29–31; 33:10-20; 34–35.
لا يخفي السفر سقوط أورشليم وحرق الهيكل و: The book does not hide the fall of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple and the exile, but it interprets this in light of the covenant and the Sabbath rest of the land, and then ends the work with the decree of Cyrus, which opens the way for return and the rebuilding of the house of the LORD. Therefore, the writer does not write a tragedy without a way out; the destruction is not the end of the promise. References: 2 Chronicles 36:15-23.
يربط أخبار الأيام بين آدم والأنساب وداود: Chronicles connects Adam and the genealogies and David and the temple and worship, then reveals that even the best kings die and do not achieve perfection. The question remains about the king whose kingdom has no end, and the New Covenant comes to proclaim Jesus, the Son of David, with the meaning of God's presence moving to a greater level in Christ. References: 1 Chronicles 17:11-14; Matthew 1:1; Luke 1:32-33.

«فأرى الدم وأعبر عنكم، فلا يكون عليكم ضر: “And when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and there shall no plague be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.”

الحكم والدينونة من جهة، والنجاة والحياة: judgment and condemnation on the one hand, and deliverance and life on the other.

Divine work leads to fruit and expansion.

The harvest turns into communal joy before the Lord.

في أعمال 2 يصبح يوم الخمسين نقطة تحول في: In Acts 2, the Day of Pentecost becomes a turning point in the proclamation of the gospel.
The message moves on to many peoples and languages.
عيد الأسابيع ليس مجرد عيد زراعي. الزراعة: The Feast of Weeks is not merely an agricultural feast. Agriculture is the framework through which Scripture reveals humanity's relationship with God: God gives the land, the rain, the growth, and the harvest; and humanity acknowledges this through the offering and rejoicing.
ثم يأتي مفهوم العد ليكشف أن بين الباكورة: Then comes the concept of counting to reveal that between the firstfruits and the fullness there is a time that carries meaning. And in the New Testament, we see that the Day of Pentecost becomes a day of being filled with the Holy Spirit and the launch of witness.
وهكذا يمكن تتبع خط لاهوتي متماسك:: Thus, a coherent theological line can be traced:
الباكورة ← الانتظار ← سبعة أسابيع ← اليو: Firstfruits ← Waiting ← Seven Weeks ← The Fiftieth Day ← Harvest ← Fullness ← Witness ← The Nations

عند دراسة هيكل هيرودس، من الخطأ التعامل: When studying Herod's Temple, it is a mistake to treat the word "Temple" as though it always refers to the sacred building alone. For the Temple complex was a vast system of walls, courts, entrances, passageways, and buildings, and the sacred building was located in the innermost part of this system.

تبدأ الرسالة بكنيسة غنية بالمواهب لكنها: The epistle begins with a church rich in gifts but suffering from division. Paul redirects its attention to Christ crucified as the wisdom of God and the power of God, then reveals that partisan allegiance to ministers destroys the unity of the body and that the church is God’s temple. He subsequently confronts moral sins, disputes, and the misuse of freedom, affirming that the believer’s body belongs to Christ and that freedom must be subject to love and edification. He then returns to Israel’s history to warn the church against idolatry and apostasy, and organizes its understanding of marriage, celibacy, food, and conscience before correcting its practices of worship and the Lord’s Supper. After that, he explains the diversity of gifts, the unity of their source and purpose, and places love above every gift as the way that gives ministry its meaning. Finally, he arrives at the resurrection, declaring that Christ truly rose, that his resurrection is the firstfruits of the resurrection of believers, and that death will not have the final word. Thus, the epistle moves from a divided church to a church returning to Christ, from individual freedom to love and edification, and from present problems to the hope of resurrection and the coming glory.

Instead, he brings every problem back to a theological truth: you belong to Christ, you are Christ’s body, your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, every gift must be used to build up the body, love is the better way, and the resurrection is the foundation of hope and work. تُعرف باسم الرسالة الأولى ليوحنا، وهي أو: It is known as the First Epistle of John, and it is the first of the three epistles traditionally attributed to the apostle John. The name “John” means “the Lord is gracious” or “the Lord shows mercy.” The epistle is distinctive in that it does not begin with the customary apostolic formula containing the name of the writer and the recipient; instead, it enters directly into its subject by announcing the Word who was from the beginning and the apostolic testimony concerning Christ, whom the apostles heard, saw, and touched. For this reason, the epistle appears more like a profound pastoral and theological testimony intended to establish believers in the truth, protect them from false teaching, and give them assurance of eternal life.
تنسب الرسالة تقليديًا إلى يوحنا الرسول،: The epistle is traditionally attributed to the apostle John, the son of Zebedee and one of the Twelve, the disciple whose name was closely associated with the Gospel of John. Although the epistle does not explicitly mention the writer’s name, the substantial similarity in language and concepts between it and the Gospel of John is especially clear in the themes of light and darkness, love, life, truth, knowledge of God, and abiding in Christ. The writer appears as an apostolic witness speaking from the position of one who knew Christ directly, not as a philosopher presenting a theory about Christ. Therefore, he says: “That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have observed, and our hands have touched, concerning the Word of life” (1 John 1: 1).
لا تذكر الرسالة اسم كنيسة أو مدينة معينة: The epistle does not mention the name of any particular church or city, and is therefore usually understood as a letter addressed to Christian communities known to the writer or to a wider circle of believers. He addresses them in an intimate pastoral manner, using expressions such as “my little children,” “beloved,” and “children.” It appears that the readers were facing deviant teaching concerning the person of Christ, the nature of sin, and the Christian life. The epistle therefore came to bring them back to the apostolic foundation: the true Christ, right faith, obedience, love, and steadfastness.
يعلن يوحنا هدفًا واضحًا جدًا في نهاية ال: John declares a very clear purpose at the end of the epistle: “I have written these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life, and so that you may believe in the name of the Son of God” (1 John 5: 13). The epistle aims at assurance of salvation, but at the same time establishes practical tests of that assurance: How does the believer live? Does he keep God’s commandments? Does he love his brothers and sisters? Does he confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh? Does he live in the light or in darkness? Thus, John does not base assurance on feelings alone, but on true faith that produces a true life.

Whoever believes in Christ as the apostles proclaimed him, walks in the light, keeps God’s commandments, and loves his brothers and sisters can live in the assurance of fellowship with God.

54. الروح القدس في الرسالة: 54. The Holy Spirit in the Epistle

رغم أن الرسالة لا تقتبس من العهد القديم: Although the epistle does not quote the Old Testament in the extensive manner found in some of Paul's epistles, its concepts are deeply rooted in the Old Testament: God is light; holiness, justice, love, righteousness, and the distinction between the children of God and the children of evil are all themes with a clear covenantal background. John recalls the story of Cain and Abel in Genesis 4 to explain the nature of hatred. Likewise, the concept of walking in the light extends the Old Testament language of God as light and holy, while the concept of knowing God is connected with God's covenant with His people and the call to know the Lord and walk in His ways.
56. العلاقة بين الرسالة الأولى وإنجيل يو: 56. The Relationship Between First John and the Gospel of John
العلاقة بين الرسالة الأولى وإنجيل يوحنا: The relationship between First John and the Gospel of John is very close linguistically and theologically; both speak of life, light, darkness, love, truth, the world, the Son, faith, and knowing God. The Gospel begins with the declaration of the Word who was in the beginning, whereas the epistle begins with testimony concerning Him who was from the beginning. The Gospel declares that life was in the Word, whereas the epistle affirms that eternal life was manifested in Christ. Therefore, First John may be read as a pastoral and practical confirmation of many truths proclaimed by the Gospel of John.
57. الاختبارات الثلاثة للحياة المسيحية: 57. The Three Tests of Christian Life
يمكن تلخيص منهج الرسالة في ثلاثة اختبارا: The method of the epistle may be summarized in three interconnected tests: a doctrinal test concerning right faith in Jesus Christ, especially the confession that He came in the flesh and that He is the Son of God; a moral test concerning walking in the light, obedience, and rejecting a sinful pattern of life; and a fraternal test concerning the believer's love for his brothers. These tests do not mean that a person is saved by works, but reveal that true faith produces sound doctrine, holy conduct, and genuine love.
58. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 58. The Major Movement of the Epistle
تبدأ الرسالة من المسيح الذي كان من البدء: The epistle begins with Christ, who was from the beginning, whom the apostles heard, saw, and touched. It then declares that this eternal life was manifested so that believers might enter into fellowship with the Father and the Son. From there, John moves to walking in the light, confessing sin, and confidence in Christ's advocacy and propitiation; then to obedience, love, and rejecting love for the world. After that, he addresses the appearance of antichrists and the denial of the Son, and affirms the necessity of abiding in the truth and in the anointing from the Holy One. He then moves to the believer's identity as a child of God, the hope of Christ's appearing, and the necessity of purification, and sets before the church the moral test and brotherly love. In the fourth chapter, he calls for testing the spirits and rejecting the spirit of error, then declares that God is love and that God's love was manifested in the sending of His Son. Finally, he reaches faith that overcomes the world, God's testimony to the Son, eternal life, assurance, and prayer; then he concludes by declaring that the Son of God has come and given us understanding to know the truth, and with the final warning: “Keep yourselves from idols.”
أعظم ما تؤكده الرسالة الأولى ليوحنا هو أ: The greatest emphasis of First John is that faith in Christ cannot be separated from knowing God and new life. It is not enough for a person to say that he knows God; the effect of this knowledge must be evident in his conduct. It is not enough to speak of love; it must be practiced. It is not enough to confess the name of Christ; one must confess Christ as the church received Him from apostolic testimony. Nor is it enough to speak of eternal life; one must now live in fellowship with God and in the light of Christ.
الرسالة الأولى ليوحنا هي رسالة اليقين وا: First John is an epistle of assurance, truth, love, and eternal life. It begins with apostolic testimony concerning Christ, who was from the beginning and was manifested in the flesh, and declares that the purpose of this testimony is to bring believers into fellowship with the Father and the Son and to grant them complete joy. It then sets forth the path of Christian life in the light, with confession of sin and confidence in Christ as Advocate and propitiation, and presents obedience and love as two marks of true knowledge of God. It strongly warns against denying Christ, false teachers, and antichrists, and affirms the necessity of testing the spirits and holding fast to apostolic teaching. At the heart of the epistle, John declares that God is love, and that this love was manifested practically when the Father sent His Son so that we might live through Him. Therefore, a person cannot claim to love God while hating his brother. The epistle concludes with assurance: the believer has eternal life in the Son, and the Son of God came to give him knowledge of the truth; in the Son are the true God and eternal life. Thus, John moves from testimony to fellowship, from fellowship to light, from light to obedience, from obedience to love, and from love to assurance, all centered on one person: Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

53. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 53. The Major Movement of the Epistle
تبدأ الرسالة بإعلان الولادة الجديدة والر: The epistle begins by proclaiming the new birth and the living hope resulting from Christ's resurrection, then moves to the heavenly inheritance and faith tested by fire. From this salvation, Peter proceeds to call believers to holiness, explaining that their redemption was accomplished through the blood of Christ, the spotless Lamb. He then moves to the identity of the church as a chosen people, a royal priesthood, and a holy nation, calling it to proclaim the excellencies of God. After that, he explains how the believer lives amid a society that does not share his faith, and how his conduct becomes a witness to Christ. The epistle reaches its climax in the suffering Christ, who committed no sin, yet bore human sins on the tree, leaving believers an example that they should follow in his steps. It then turns to marital and ecclesial relationships, the defense of hope, prayer, love, and the endurance of suffering. Finally, it addresses the elders and the church, calling them to shepherding, humility, vigilance, and resistance to the devil, and concludes with the God of all grace who, after suffering, perfects, establishes, strengthens, and enables the believer.
الرسالة الأولى لبطرس هي رسالة الرجاء وال: First Peter is an epistle of hope and holiness amid suffering. It begins with Christ's resurrection, which gives the believer a living hope and an imperishable inheritance, then reveals that faith may pass through fire in order to be tested and to show its genuineness. From this hope arises the call to holiness, because he who called believers is holy. At the heart of the epistle appears Christ: the spotless Lamb, the living stone, the cornerstone, the suffering servant, the bearer of sins, the shepherd of souls, and the chief Shepherd. Therefore, Christian suffering is not viewed as defeat, but as a path on which the believer follows Christ while awaiting glory. The epistle affirms that the church is not a community fleeing from the world, but a people living in the world as witnesses to Christ; its weapons are holiness, good conduct, love for others, gentleness, hope, and prayer. At its conclusion, suffering is transformed from the question, “Why does this happen?” into a certainty: the God of all grace is the one who perfects, establishes, and strengthens, and eternal glory in Christ is the end.

42. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 42. The Major Movement of the Epistle
تبدأ الرسالة بالشكر من أجل إيمان تسالوني: The epistle begins with thanksgiving for the Thessalonians' faith, love, and hope; it then recounts how they received the gospel amid much affliction, turned from idols to worship the living God, and awaited his Son from heaven. Paul then reveals his pastoral heart, explaining his faithfulness in ministry and his longing for the church; he sends Timothy to strengthen them in faith and rejoices when he hears of their steadfastness. The epistle then moves to practical life, calling for holiness, purity, love, and quiet work, before arriving at the great question concerning believers who have fallen asleep. Here Paul presents the hope of resurrection and the coming of the Lord, affirming that the sleeping will rise and that the living will be gathered with them to meet the Lord, and that the final goal is to be always with the Lord. He then moves from the hope of the coming to readiness for it, calling believers to watchfulness because the Day of the Lord comes suddenly, and to live as children of light, armed with faith, love, and the hope of salvation. Finally, he offers a series of communal exhortations concerning encouragement, prayer, joy, thanksgiving, discernment, and sanctification, and concludes with prayer for the sanctification of the whole person and preservation blameless until the coming of Christ. Thus, the epistle moves from faith, love, and hope, to steadfastness in affliction, to holiness, to the resurrection of the sleeping, to the coming of Christ, and then to a life of readiness and hope.
رسالة تسالونيكي الأولى هي رسالة الإيمان: First Thessalonians is an epistle of faith that stands firm, love that serves, and hope that awaits Christ. It presents a model of a church newly established in faith that was able to receive the gospel amid persecution, abandon idols, worship the living God, and await his Son from heaven. At the heart of the epistle stands the hope of the Second Coming: Christ, who died and rose again, will come; those who have fallen asleep in Christ will rise; the living will be gathered with them to meet the Lord; and the goal is not merely an eschatological event, but that Christ's people may always be with the Lord. Therefore, hope becomes a motive for holiness, love a motive for service, and faith a source of steadfastness. The epistle concludes with a complete portrait of the person who awaits Christ: rejoicing always, praying without ceasing, giving thanks in everything, living in the light, and being wholly sanctified in anticipation of the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ.

تبدأ الرسالة بتكليف تيموثاوس أن يحفظ الت: The epistle begins with the commission to Timothy to preserve sound teaching and confront misguided teachers. Paul then presents himself as a witness to the grace of Christ that saved him despite his past. It subsequently turns to the life of the church, speaking of prayer for all people and of Christ as the one mediator and ransom for humanity. It then lays down the foundations of church leadership and the qualifications of bishops and deacons, and declares the church to be the house of God and the pillar and foundation of the truth. From this point, it moves to a warning against apostasy and demonic teaching, and calls Timothy to godliness, exemplary conduct, reading, teaching, and not neglecting his gift. It then regulates relationships within the church, the care of widows, the honoring of servants, and dealings with elders, slaves, and the wealthy, until it reaches its warning against the love of money and its call to fight the good fight of faith. The epistle concludes with the prospect of Christ’s appearing, so that every ordering of the church, every teaching, every practice, and every struggle is connected to a higher goal: that the church may preserve the faith, live in godliness, and await the appearing of the Lord Jesus Christ.
رسالة تيموثاوس الأولى هي رسالة حفظ الإيم: First Timothy is an epistle concerning the preservation of the faith, the ordering of the church, and the formation of a servant worthy of the house of God. It confronts strange teaching with the love that proceeds from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith, and sets before the church a model of leadership founded on godliness, maturity, exemplary conduct, and teaching. At its center stands Christ as the one mediator between God and humanity, who gave Himself as a ransom, who was manifested in the flesh, preached among the nations, and taken up in glory. The mission of the church flows from Christ; therefore, the church must be the house of God and the pillar and foundation of the truth. The epistle connects doctrine and conduct, calling the servant to be an example, believers to love and purity, the wealthy to generosity, and all people to prayer and godliness. Finally, it presents the warning against the love of money and apostasy alongside the call to fight the good fight of faith, hold fast to eternal life, and await the Lord’s appearing. Thus, the epistle presents an integrated model of a church that preserves the truth, lives in godliness, shepherds the people of God, serves the world, and awaits the appearing of Christ.

30. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 30. The major movement of the epistle
تبدأ الرسالة بإله التعزية الذي يسند بولس: The epistle begins with the God of all comfort, who sustains Paul amid affliction. It then reveals that suffering does not conflict with the message, but can become a means of displaying the life of Christ in the servant. Paul then moves to explain the glory of the New Covenant and the work of the Spirit, who removes the veil and transforms the believer into the image of Christ. He further explains that the divine treasure is placed in earthen vessels so that the power of God, rather than of humanity, may be displayed. From there, he arrives at the heart of the gospel: God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, and gave the church the ministry of reconciliation, because Christ, who knew no sin, became sin for us so that we might become the righteousness of God in Him. Paul then explains the nature of apostolic ministry and confronts the false apostles, who measure ministry by appearance and human strength, while he presents his sufferings and weakness as evidence that true power comes from Christ. In the section on giving, grace appears in practical form: the believer who has experienced the riches of Christ learns to give generously to others. Finally, the epistle reaches its climax in the “thorn in the flesh,” where Paul learns that the grace of Christ is sufficient and that the power of God is made perfect in weakness. Thus, the epistle moves from affliction to comfort, from weakness to strength, from the cross to ministry, from reconciliation with God to reconciliation with others, and from the grace of Christ to a life of giving.
تستند الرسالة إلى خلفية العهد القديم خصو: The epistle rests upon an Old Testament background, especially in its discussion of Moses, the veil, and the glory of the covenant. It uses the language of “covenant,” “Spirit,” and “glory” to explain the transition from a covenant written on tablets to a covenant that works in hearts.
كما أن مفهوم المجد، والبر، والهيكل، والق: The concepts of glory, righteousness, temple, holiness, people, and promises likewise extend in the epistle from their Old Testament background to their fulfillment in Christ.
تكشف كورنثوس الثانية الجانب الذي لا يظهر: Second Corinthians reveals the aspect not easily seen in the outward appearance of ministry: the servant himself must be shaped by the cross. Paul does not present the Christian message as a path to personal glory, but as a path on which the servant bears the sufferings of Christ, experiences His comfort, and proclaims the power of His grace. At the heart of the epistle, Christ appears as the foundation of reconciliation, the Spirit as the source of transformation, grace as the power that sustains the weak, and love as the foundation of giving and ministry. Therefore, the greatest paradox in the epistle is that human weakness does not mark the end of God's work, but can become the place where God's power is displayed most clearly.

تُعرف باسم الرسالة الثانية ليوحنا، وهي أ: It is known as the Second Epistle of John, and it is approximately the shortest book of the New Testament. Yet it carries a concentrated theological and pastoral content that brings together truth, love, obedience, and protection from deceptive teaching. The epistle is traditionally associated with John the Apostle and presents itself through the title “the Elder,” a title that reflects the writer's spiritual standing and pastoral authority. The epistle centers on the necessity for believers to live in love, but within the boundaries of apostolic truth, so that love does not become acceptance of teaching that denies the reality of Jesus Christ.
يقدم الكاتب نفسه في بداية الرسالة باسم «: At the beginning of the epistle, the writer identifies himself as “the Elder,” saying: “The Elder, to the elect lady and her children” (2 John 1: 1). Christian tradition has understood this “Elder” to be John the Apostle, an interpretation supported by the strong connection between the language and theology of the epistle and the Gospel of John and the First Epistle of John. The writer appears as a shepherd responsible for protecting the community from distorted teaching, yet at the same time he writes with a fatherly spirit that combines doctrinal firmness with pastoral love.
3. إلى من كُتبت الرسالة؟: 3. To whom was the epistle written?
يوجه يوحنا الرسالة إلى «كيرية المختارة و: John addresses the epistle to “the elect lady and her children.” The expression has been understood in two principal ways: either it refers to a Christian woman and her children, or it is a symbolic expression for a Christian community and its members. The text does not decisively settle which interpretation is intended. What matters, however, is that the epistle is addressed to a community of believers who know the truth and walk in it, and who face the danger of people bearing distorted teaching about Christ.
الهدف المباشر هو تشجيع المؤمنين على الثب: The immediate aim is to encourage believers to remain steadfast in truth, love, and obedience, while warning them against teachers who deny the reality of Christ's incarnation. John says: “For many deceivers have entered into the world, who do not confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh” (2 John 1: 7). Therefore, the epistle is not merely a personal letter of love, but a pastoral document for defending apostolic Christian faith.

The text provides no specific date; therefore, determining the time of writing remains a historical estimate. The epistle seems to belong to a period in which the church faced the spread of teachings that denied certain truths concerning the person of Christ and His incarnation.

The believer is called to love, but cannot separate love from truth; is called to receive others, but cannot accept teaching that destroys the foundation of faith; and is called to fellowship, but must distinguish between Christian fellowship and support for deceptive teaching.
تتكرر كلمة «الحق» بصورة بارزة منذ افتتاح: The word “truth” recurs prominently from the opening of the epistle: “Because of the truth which abides in us and will be with us forever” (2 John 1: 2). For John, truth is not a collection of abstract doctrinal information, but a divine reality that dwells in the believer and continues with him. The context of the epistle shows that this truth is directly connected with the person of Christ and with the apostolic faith received by the church.
يقول يوحنا: «أَنْ تَكُونَ مَعَنَا نِعْمَ: John says: “Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love” (2 John 1: 3). John places truth and love side by side: Christian love does not function outside truth, and Christian truth is not lived in a spirit of hatred. Here an especially important balance in pastoral theology appears: truth without love becomes harshness, and love without truth becomes tolerance of error.

15. الثبات في تعليم المسيح: 15. Abiding in the teaching of Christ
يقول يوحنا: «كُلُّ مَنْ تَعَدَّى وَلَمْ: John says: “Whoever transgresses and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God. Whoever abides in the teaching of Christ has both the Father and the Son” (2 John 1: 9).
وهذه الآية من أهم مفاتيح الرسالة؛ فالعلا: This verse is one of the most important keys to the epistle; relationship with God is connected to abiding in the teaching of Christ. Knowledge of the Father cannot be separated from a proper confession of the Son.

وهذه العبارة تحتاج إلى فهمها في سياقها ا: This statement must be understood in its historical context; the “house” could be a place of welcome and hospitality for itinerant teachers, and thus receiving a teacher practically meant supporting him and giving him a platform to spread his teaching. This is a direct continuation of Johannine theology in his First Epistle and Gospel; Christ is not merely a teaching mediator who may be bypassed in reaching God, but knowledge of the Father is connected to proper faith in the Son.
20. خطر فقدان ما عمله المؤمن: 20. The Danger of Losing What the Believer Has Accomplished
يقول يوحنا: «لِئَلاَّ نُضَيِّعَ مَا عَمِ: John says: “that we do not lose what we have accomplished” (2 John 1: 8). In the pastoral context, this points to the importance of steadfastness and not departing from the truth that believers have received. Christian life is not merely a moment of beginning, but a journey of steadfastness to the end.
يظهر في الرسالة أن الخطر قد يأتي من أشخا: The epistle shows that danger may come from people who speak Christian language and appear as spiritual teachers, yet carry teaching that rejects the truth of Christ. Therefore, teaching should not be evaluated by appearance, eloquence, or spiritual claims, but by its conformity with the apostolic teaching concerning Christ.
22. العلاقة بين 2 يوحنا و1 يوحنا: 22. The Relationship Between 2 John and 1 John
الرسالتان الأولى والثانية ليوحنا ترتبطان: The First and Second Epistles of John are closely related; both speak of truth and love, walking in God’s commandments, Christ coming in the flesh, deceivers, and the antichrist. But the First Epistle offers a broader presentation of spiritual tests, assurance, and eternal life, whereas the Second Epistle condenses these principles into practical pastoral instruction concerning how the church should deal with false teachers.
23. العلاقة مع إنجيل يوحنا: 23. The Relationship with the Gospel of John
هناك صدى واضح بين الرسالة الثانية وإنجيل: There is a clear echo between the Second Epistle and the Gospel of John; the Gospel declares that the Word became flesh, and the Second Epistle warns against those who do not confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. The Gospel focuses on Christ’s commandment of love, and the Second Epistle confirms that love is manifested by walking according to God’s commandments. Thus, the epistle moves from theological proclamation in the Gospel to pastoral protection of this proclamation within the church.
24. الحق ليس منفصلًا عن شخص المسيح: 24. Truth Is Not Separate from the Person of Christ
الحق في الرسالة ليس مجرد نظام فكري مستقل: Truth in the epistle is not merely an independent intellectual system; the epistle connects it directly with Christ and his teaching. Therefore, defending the truth essentially means defending the truth of Christ as the church received it from the apostles.
25. الكنيسة بين المحبة والتمييز: 25. The Church Between Love and Discernment
تضع الرسالة أمام الكنيسة توازنًا بالغ ال: The epistle presents the church with a profoundly important balance: it must be a loving, hospitable, compassionate community concerned for others, but at the same time it must be a community of doctrinal discernment. Not every call to unity is Christian unity, and not every call to love is biblical love; true unity is founded on the truth in Christ.
26. البعد الرعوي للرسالة: 26. The Pastoral Dimension of the Epistle
رغم أن الرسالة قصيرة جدًا، فإنها تكشف قل: Although the epistle is very short, it reveals the heart of a shepherd who desires to protect his people from danger. It begins with love and joy at walking in truth, then offers warning, and concludes with the desire for a personal meeting: “Although I have much to write to you, I did not wish to write with paper and ink, for I hope to come to you and speak face to face, that our joy may be complete” (2 John 1: 12). Here we see that written teaching does not eliminate personal pastoral relationship.
يرتبط الفرح عند يوحنا بالحق والشركة؛ فهد: For John, joy is connected with truth and fellowship; the goal of teaching is not merely victory in a doctrinal debate, but attaining complete joy in the fellowship of believers together. This agrees with the opening of the First Epistle, which connects the proclamation of Christ with fellowship and joy.
إذا أخذنا «كيرية المختارة» بمعناها الحرف: If “the chosen lady” is understood literally, the epistle reveals clear respect for the role of the believing woman and her children within the Christian community. If the expression is understood symbolically as referring to a Christian community, the “children” represent the members of the community. In both interpretations, the primary meaning remains a believing community living in truth and needing protection from deceptive teaching.
تستند الرسالة بصورة غير مباشرة إلى مبادئ: The epistle is indirectly founded on ancient covenantal principles; love for God and obedience to his commandments, caution against false prophets and distorted teaching, and preserving the covenant community from pagan influences all extend from the Old Testament into Christian teaching. Yet John refocuses these principles around Jesus Christ as the Son who came in the flesh.
تبدأ الرسالة بإعلان الحق والمحبة، ثم تفر: The epistle begins by proclaiming truth and love, then rejoices in believers’ walking in truth, reminds them of the fundamental commandment to love one another, and reveals that true love is connected with obedience. It then turns sharply to warning against deceivers who deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh, and calls believers to caution and steadfastness in the teaching of Christ. It establishes clear boundaries against giving false teachers support or a platform, and concludes with the writer’s desire for a personal meeting and the completion of fellowship and joy.
أهم رسالة في 2 يوحنا هي أن المحبة المسيح: The most important message in 2 John is that Christian love cannot be separated from Christian truth. The church is called to love, but it is not called to accept every teaching in the name of love; it is called to hospitality, but it is not called to support those who use hospitality to spread another gospel; it is called to unity, but true unity cannot be founded on denying the person of Christ. Thus, the epistle brings together love, truth, discernment, and steadfastness in a very small space.
الرسالة الثانية ليوحنا هي رسالة قصيرة في: The Second Epistle of John is short in length but profound in content, and it presents a balanced model for church life. It begins with the truth that abides in believers and connects it with love, grace, and peace; then it rejoices in the children of God walking in truth and affirms that true love is manifested in keeping God’s commandments. At the heart of the epistle is a warning against deceivers who deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh, because denying the incarnation strikes at the essence of Christian faith. Therefore, John calls believers to abide in the teaching of Christ, to distinguish between love and uncontrolled acceptance, and not to grant false teaching support or legitimacy within the community. The epistle ends with a warm pastoral spirit, as the writer longs to meet believers face to face so that joy may be complete. Thus, the entire epistle may be summarized in this principle: we love in truth, walk in truth, abide in the teaching of Christ, and protect the church from every teaching that denies the truth of Christ incarnate.

تُعرف باسم الرسالة الثانية لبطرس، وهي إح: It is known as the Second Epistle of Peter and is one of the General Epistles in the New Testament. The name “Peter” is the name that the Lord Jesus gave to Simon son of Jonah, and its meaning is connected with a stone or rock. The nature of this epistle differs from the First Epistle; the first emphasizes hope and endurance amid suffering, whereas the second places strong emphasis on growth in the knowledge of Christ, steadfastness in truth, warning against false teachers, and awaiting the Lord’s coming and judgment. Therefore, it may be viewed as an epistle protecting the church from doctrinal and moral deviation and from losing hope in Christ’s coming.
يفتتح الكاتب الرسالة بقوله: «سِمْعَانُ ب: The writer opens the epistle by saying: “Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained with us an equally precious faith through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ” (2 Peter 1: 1). Here he presents himself by the name “Simon Peter,” combining his former name with the apostolic name Christ gave him. His identity also appears in the reference to his approaching death, as he says: “knowing that the putting off of my tent is near, as our Lord Jesus Christ has also made known to me” (2 Peter 1: 14). This makes the epistle appear as though it were a final spiritual testament from an apostle who wishes to leave the church steadfast in truth after his departure.
لا يحدد بطرس في الرسالة الثانية المناطق: In the Second Epistle, Peter does not identify the regions in which the readers live as he did in the First Epistle, but he addresses believers who share Christian faith with him. In chapter three, he says: “This is now the second epistle I write to you, beloved” (2 Peter 3: 1), indicating that the Second Epistle is directed to an audience that had previously received his teaching. Therefore, its purpose is not to establish faith from the beginning, but to remind believers of what they knew and protect them from forgetfulness, deception, and deviation.
السبب الرئيسي للرسالة هو تثبيت المؤمنين: The main reason for the epistle is to establish believers in sound faith and warn them against false teachers who will enter among God’s people, in addition to addressing the question concerning the delay of Christ’s coming. Peter warns that some will say: “Where is the promise of his coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation” (2 Peter 3: 4). Therefore, the epistle combines safeguarding doctrine, holiness of conduct, expectation of the coming, and confidence in God’s promises.
يربط الكاتب الرسالة بمرحلة متقدمة من خدم: The writer connects the epistle with an advanced stage of his ministry and refers to his approaching death; therefore, it is generally understood as one of his final writings. Scholars differ concerning the precise date and the historical attribution of the epistle to Peter, but traditional Christian reading attributes it to the apostle Peter, while critical studies discuss questions of style, language, and historical circumstances. From an encyclopedic perspective, a distinction should be made between what the text itself states and the historical conclusions over which studies differ.
الموضوع المركزي في الرسالة هو: الثبات في: The central theme of the epistle is steadfastness in the knowledge of Christ and truth, spiritual growth, holy living, resistance to false teaching, and expectation of the day of the Lord. Therefore, the epistle begins with growth and ends with expectation of Christ’s coming; between its beginning and end, Peter warns against everything that may cause the believer to fall away from truth, whether fleshly desire, distorted teaching, or doubt concerning God’s promises.
7. النعمة والسلام ومعرفة الله: 7. Grace, Peace, and the Knowledge of God
يقول بطرس: «لِتَكْثُرْ لَكُمُ النِّعْمَة: Peter says: “May grace and peace be multiplied to you in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord” (2 Peter 1: 2). From the beginning, he places knowledge at the center of Christian life, but he does not mean merely theological information; rather, he means a living knowledge of God and Christ that affects conduct. Therefore, true knowledge in the epistle is not separate from holiness, but leads to it.
8. القوة الإلهية وكل ما للحياة والتقوى: 8. Divine Power and Everything for Life and Godliness

ولا تعني عبارة «شركاء الطبيعة الإلهية» أ: The expression “partakers of the divine nature” does not mean that a human being becomes God in essence; rather, it refers to the believer’s participation in God’s life, grace, and holiness, and separation from the world’s corruption.
«وَلِهذَا عَيْنِهِ وَأَنْتُمْ بَاذِلُونَ: “But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, to knowledge self-control, to self-control perseverance, to perseverance godliness, to godliness brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness love” (2 Peter 1: 5-7).

يقول بطرس إن هذه الصفات إذا وُجدت وتزايد: Peter says that if these qualities are present and increasing, they make the believer:

يقول عن الذي لا توجد فيه هذه الصفات:: He says concerning the one in whom these qualities are absent:

فالخطر ليس فقط الجهل، بل نسيان ما فعله ا: The danger is not merely ignorance, but forgetting what God has done in Christ. When the believer forgets the grace of forgiveness, he becomes more vulnerable to returning to his former life.
«لِذلِكَ بِالأَكْثَرِ أَيُّهَا الإِخْوَة: “Therefore, brethren, be even more diligent to make your calling and election sure, for if you do these things you will never stumble”
لا يقدم بطرس الاجتهاد كوسيلة لشراء الخلا: Peter does not present diligence as a means of purchasing salvation, but as a call to demonstrate the reality of faith in a steadfast practical life.
«لأَنَّهُ هكَذَا يُقَدَّمُ لَكُمْ بِسَعَ: “For so an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be abundantly provided for you.”

15. بطرس كخادم يذكّر الكنيسة: 15. Peter as a Servant Who Reminds the Church
يكرر بطرس فكرة التذكير بصورة واضحة: «لِذ: Peter clearly repeats the idea of reminder: “Therefore I will not neglect to remind you always of these things, though you know them and are established in the present truth” (2 Peter 1: 12). This is an important point in apostolic ministry; Christian teaching does not always require new information, but also continual reminder of known truth, lest the believer forget it.
«عَالِمًا أَنَّ خَلْعَ مَسْكَنِي قَرِيبٌ: “Knowing that the putting off of my tent is near, as our Lord Jesus Christ also made known to me.”
وهذا يعطي الرسالة طابعًا وصائيًا قويًا؛: This gives the epistle a powerful testamentary character; Peter knows that his earthly ministry is approaching its end, and therefore he wishes to leave behind a faith firmly grounded in the word of God and not dependent solely on his personal presence.
17. لسنا نتبع خرافات مصنعة: 17. We Do Not Follow Cleverly Devised Myths
«لأَنَّنَا لَمْ نَكُنْ قَدْ أَعْلَمْنَاك: “For we did not make known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ by following cleverly devised myths, but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.”
وهنا يواجه بطرس احتمال اتهام الرسالة الم: Here Peter addresses the possibility of the Christian message being accused of being a religious myth; he affirms that the apostles did not build their faith upon cleverly devised myths, but upon testimony and eyewitness observation.
يشير بطرس بصورة واضحة إلى حادثة التجلي،: Peter clearly refers to the event of the Transfiguration, when he was with Christ, James, and John, and says:

وهنا يربط بطرس بين الشهادة الرسولية والك: Here Peter connects apostolic testimony with the prophetic word, presenting the word of God as a lamp that shines amid darkness.

وهذا أحد النصوص الأساسية في دراسة وحي ال: This is one of the foundational texts in the study of biblical inspiration; the epistle affirms that the ultimate source of prophecy is not human will, but the work of the Holy Spirit in the prophets.

الخطر هنا لا يأتي من الخارج فقط؛ فقد يظه: The danger does not come only from outside; it may arise within the religious community itself through teaching that appears Christian but carries destructive deviation.
22. إنكار السيد الذي اشتراهم: 22. Denying the Master Who Bought Them
«وَهُمْ فِي طَمَعٍ يَتَّجِرُونَ بِكُمْ ب: “And in their greed they will exploit you with fabricated words.”

يستخدم بطرس أمثلة من تاريخ الكتاب المقدس: Peter uses examples from biblical history to demonstrate that God does not overlook evil: the angels who sinned, the ancient world in the days of Noah, and Sodom and Gomorrah. The purpose is to show that God is able to preserve and rescue the godly while at the same time judging the wicked.
ويتحدث عن لوط الذي كان يتعذب بسبب فساد س: He also speaks of Lot, who was tormented by the corruption of Sodom. Through these 2 figures, Peter presents a clear principle: God knows how to rescue the godly from temptation and to keep the unrighteous until the day of judgment (Second Peter 2: 9).
25. خطورة الشهوة والفساد: 25. The Danger of Lust and Corruption
يربط بطرس التعليم الكاذب بالانحلال الأخل: Peter connects false teaching with moral dissipation, warning of people:

وهذا يؤكد أن العقيدة والأخلاق مرتبطتان؛: This confirms that doctrine and ethics are connected; deviation in the knowledge of God can produce deviation in life.
يستحضر بطرس شخصية بلعام، الذي عرف إرادة: Peter recalls the figure of Balaam, who knew the will of God but went astray because of greed, and says that the false teachers:

«إِذْ هُمْ يَعِدُونَهُمْ بِالْحُرِّيَّةِ: “While they promise them freedom, they themselves are slaves of corruption.”
فالحرية الحقيقية في الكتاب المقدس ليست أ: True freedom in the Bible is not that a person does everything he desires, but that he is freed from the dominion of sin in order to live for God.
يقدم بطرس صورة شديدة القوة:: Peter presents a most powerful image:
«قَدْ أَصَابَهُمْ مَا فِي الْمَثَلِ الصّ: “What happened to them is according to the true proverb: ‘A dog has returned to its own vomit,’ and, ‘A washed sow to wallowing in the mire.’”
الصورة تؤكد بشاعة الرجوع إلى الفساد بعد: The image emphasizes the ugliness of returning to corruption after knowing the way of righteousness, and reveals the danger of dealing superficially with faith.
29. الأصحاح الثالث والمجيء الثاني: 29. Chapter Three and the Second Coming
يبدأ بطرس الأصحاح الثالث بتذكير المؤمنين: Peter begins the third chapter by reminding believers that the prophets and apostles spoke about the coming of the Lord, because the fundamental problem believers will face is mockery of the promise of His coming.

31. الله لا يتباطأ عن الموعد: 31. God Is Not Slow Concerning the Promise

هذه من أهم الآيات في فهم تأخر المجيء؛ فا: This is among the most important verses for understanding the delay of the coming; the apparent delay is neither inability nor forgetfulness, but is related to God’s patience and the granting of opportunity for repentance.
«وَلَكِنْ سَيَأْتِي كَلِصٍّ فِي اللَّيْل: “But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, the elements will melt with fervent heat, and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.”
فالمجيء ليس مجرد حدث عاطفي للمؤمنين، بل: Thus, the coming is not merely an emotional event for believers, but is also connected with cosmic judgment and the declaration of God’s ultimate sovereignty.
33. انتظار سماوات جديدة وأرض جديدة: 33. Awaiting New Heavens and a New Earth

وهذه هي النهاية الإيجابية للرؤية الأخروي: This is the positive conclusion of the eschatological vision: a world in which righteousness dwells.
34. ماذا ينبغي أن تكون عليه حياة المؤمن؟: 34. What should the believer's life be like?
«فَبِمَا أَنَّ هذِهِ كُلَّهَا تَنْحَلُّ،: “Since all these things are to be dissolved, what sort of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness?”
هذه الآية تكشف العلاقة بين الأخرويات وال: This verse reveals the relationship between eschatology and ethics: knowledge of the future must transform the present.
فالمؤمن الذي ينتظر مجيء المسيح لا يعيش ب: The believer who awaits Christ's coming does not live indifferently, but lives in holiness and godliness.
35. انتظار يوم الله وتعجيله: 35. Awaiting and hastening the Day of God

فالنبوة الكتابية لا تهدف إلى إشباع الفضو: Biblical prophecy does not aim to satisfy curiosity about history as much as it aims to form a people prepared to meet the Lord.
«وَاحْسِبُوا أَنَاةَ رَبِّنَا خَلاَصًا،: “Consider the patience of our Lord as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him.”
وهذا رابط مهم بين خدمة بطرس وخدمة بولس،: This is an important link between Peter's ministry and Paul's ministry, and it provides early testimony to the esteem in which Paul's teaching and writings were held.
يشير بطرس إلى أن في رسائل بولس أمورًا:: Peter indicates that there are matters in Paul's letters:

«فَأَنْتُمْ أَيُّهَا الأَحِبَّاءُ، إِذْ: “Therefore, beloved, since you know this beforehand, beware lest you be carried away by the error of the wicked and fall from your steadfastness.”
المعرفة السابقة ليست ضمانًا للامبالاة؛ ب: Prior knowledge is not a guarantee of indifference; rather, it makes the believer responsible for caution and steadfastness.
تختم الرسالة بأحد أهم ملخصاتها:: The epistle concludes with one of its most important summaries:
«لَكِنِ انْمُوا فِي النِّعْمَةِ وَفِي مَ: “But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory now and to the day of eternity. Amen.”
بدأت الرسالة بالمعرفة والنمو، وتنتهي بال: The epistle began with knowledge and growth, and it ends with growth in grace and knowledge; it is as though Peter sets before the church the positive remedy for every danger against which he warned: do not remain stagnant, but grow in Christ.
40. المسيح في الرسالة الثانية لبطرس: 40. Christ in the Second Epistle of Peter
المسيح هو مركز الرسالة كلها؛ فهو ربنا وم: Christ is the center of the entire epistle; He is our Lord and Savior, the possessor of glory, who will come again, and whose coming is associated with judgment and the renewal of creation. Christ appears at the beginning of the epistle as the source of grace and peace, at the Transfiguration as the beloved Son whose glory the Father proclaimed, and at the end of the epistle as the coming Lord whose arrival the church awaits and in whose knowledge believers must grow. Therefore, the epistle does not separate Christ who saved, Christ who sanctifies, and Christ who will come.
تعتمد الرسالة الثانية لبطرس على خلفية عه: The Second Epistle of Peter rests on a clear Old Testament background, especially in its discussion of creation, the waters, the Flood, Noah, judgment, Sodom and Gomorrah, Balaam, the Day of the Lord, the new heavens, and the new earth. The Flood in particular appears as historical and theological evidence that God is able to preserve the godly and judge the wicked world, while the image of the new heavens and new earth becomes an extension of the prophetic hope for the restoration of creation and the establishment of righteousness.
42. العلاقة بين الرسالتين الأولى والثاني: 42. The relationship between the First and Second Epistles of Peter
يمكن ملاحظة تكامل واضح بين الرسالتين. ال: A clear complementarity can be observed between the two epistles. The first confronts suffering and persecution from without and teaches the believer how to follow the suffering Christ in hope and holiness, whereas the second confronts danger from within: false teaching, moral corruption, and doubt concerning the coming. In the first, the believer awaits glory after suffering; in the second, he awaits the Day of the Lord and the new heavens and new earth. Thus, the two epistles together concern the life of the church in the world: steadfastness under external pressure and steadfastness in the face of internal deviation.
43. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 43. The major movement of the epistle
تبدأ الرسالة بالإيمان الذي يمنحه الله وب: The epistle begins with the faith God grants and the call to grow in virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, and love. It then affirms that the believer is called to confirm his calling and election and avoid spiritual barrenness. After this, Peter presents his apostolic testimony concerning Christ and His glory at the Transfiguration, and affirms the certainty of the prophetic word and its inspiration by the Holy Spirit. The discourse then turns to warning against false teachers who distort the truth, exploit believers, and turn freedom into an avenue for corruption, citing the judgment of angels, the ancient world, Sodom and Gomorrah, and the example of Balaam. In the third chapter, Peter moves to the crisis of doubt concerning Christ's coming, explaining that God is not slow but patient, and that the Day of the Lord will certainly come. He then lifts the church's eyes to the end: new heavens and a new earth in which righteousness dwells, and transforms the expectation of the future into a practical call to holiness, before concluding with the comprehensive exhortation: “Grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.”
الرسالة الثانية لبطرس هي رسالة الثبات وا: The Second Epistle of Peter is an epistle of steadfastness, growth, discernment, and eschatological hope. It teaches that true faith does not remain stagnant, but grows in virtue, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, and love. It strongly warns against false teachers who distort doctrine, exploit believers, and turn freedom into an opportunity for corruption. At the same time, the epistle addresses one of the earliest objections to the Christian faith, namely the question of the delay of Christ's coming, declaring that the delay of the appointed time is not forgetfulness on God's part, but patience, mercy, and a call to repentance. Nevertheless, the Day of the Lord is certainly coming, judgment will come, and, according to God's promise, new heavens and a new earth in which righteousness dwells will appear. Therefore, the epistle does not call the believer to determine the time of the coming, but to be prepared for it, to live in holiness and godliness, to beware of error, and to remain steadfast in the truth. The epistle ends where the whole life of the believer should begin and end: in Christ, growing in His grace and knowledge, and giving glory to Him now and to the day of eternity.

تبدأ الرسالة بالشكر من أجل نمو الإيمان و: The epistle begins with thanksgiving for the growth of faith, the increase of love, and the steadfastness of believers amid persecution. It then offers them consolation that God is righteous and that Christ will come in His glory to repay those who afflict His people and grant rest to believers. The epistle then turns to correct a serious disturbance concerning the day of Christ, explaining that the coming of that day is connected with preceding events and that evil is active in history but does not escape God's authority. The “man of sin,” the mystery of lawlessness, and deception appear, but the end is settled: the Lord Jesus will destroy the lawless one by the appearing of His coming. Paul then returns to the believers to affirm God's choice and their calling to salvation, and he calls them to stand firm in apostolic teaching. In the final section, the epistle moves from eschatology to daily life, requesting prayer, the spread of the word, faithfulness, and work, while warning against idleness and disorder resulting from a misunderstanding of the expectation of Christ's coming. Thus, the epistle moves from persecution to consolation, from eschatological disturbance to biblical truth, from the exposure of evil to Christ's victory, and from awaiting the future to the believer's faithfulness in the present.
رسالة تسالونيكي الثانية هي رسالة الثبات: Second Thessalonians is an epistle of steadfastness amid affliction, discernment amid disturbance, and hope in Christ's victory. It affirms that God is righteous, that believers' sufferings are not meaningless, and that the Lord Jesus will be revealed from heaven in His glory, bringing judgment upon those who reject the gospel and rest to His people. At the same time, the epistle corrects every conception that makes Christ's coming a cause for panic or disorder, declaring that there are events connected with the day of the Lord, that the mystery of lawlessness is already at work but is limited by God's authority, and that the end does not belong to evil but to Christ, who will destroy the lawless one by the appearing of His coming. The epistle then joins doctrine to life: whoever awaits Christ must stand firm in teaching, pray, work, and not grow weary in doing good. Thus, the epistle presents a balanced vision of the Second Coming: hope for the saints, judgment for evil, victory for Christ, and a call for the church to live faithfully until the Lord comes.
