📖 مقدمة سفر عاموس: 📖 Introduction to the Book of Amos
الفكرة المركزية للسفر: سفر عاموس هو سفر: The central idea of the book: the Book of Amos is the book of God's justice, exposing formal religion, defending the right, condemning the exploitation of the poor, and proclaiming that worship of God cannot be separated from righteousness in everyday life. Amos came from Tekoa, a rural area in Judah, but he was sent to the northern kingdom of Israel at a time when the land was enjoying economic prosperity and political strength, while poverty, injustice, and exploitation were eating away at society from within. Therefore, Amos proclaims that the problem is not the absence of religion, but the presence of religion without righteousness, worship without holiness, sacrifices without mercy, and a temple without a sincere heart. Although the book ends with severe judgments, it also concludes with the promise of restoration for the house of David and the establishment of God's people, declaring that judgment is not the end of God's purpose, but that righteousness is the path to restoration.
1. اسم السفر ومعنى الاسم: 1. Name of the book and its meaning
اسم السفر هو عاموس — עָמוֹס — ʿĀmôs، وير: The name of the book is Amos — עָמוֹס — ʿĀmôs, and in Hebrew it is connected to a root that carries the meaning of burden or carrying on the shoulder. Therefore, the name is traditionally understood in the sense of 'the bearer' or 'one who bears the burden,' a meaning that fits strikingly with the prophet's personality, who carried in his heart a heavy message against corruption and injustice. The prophet did not carry a comforting message that pleased his hearers, but a divine proclamation that set the sins of the nation before its eyes, regardless of its political or religious standing.
كان عاموس من تقوع في يهوذا، ويصف نفسه بأ: Amos was from Tekoa in Judah, and he describes himself as a shepherd and a tender of sycamore figs, meaning that he did not come from a royal prophetic school or from a prominent priestly class. The Lord called him from his work and sent him to Israel to proclaim the word of God. Therefore, Amos's character presents an important example that the authority of the prophetic message does not depend on the prophet's social position, but on God's call and proclamation.
3. سنة ميلاد عاموس ووفاته: 3. Amos's year of birth and death
لا يسجل الكتاب المقدس سنة ميلاد عاموس أو: The Bible does not record the year of Amos's birth or the year of his death, and therefore they cannot be determined precisely. However, the book itself dates the period of his ministry as being 'in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.' From this dating, his ministry can be placed in the eighth century BCE, approximately in the middle of the eighth century B.C.
ارتبطت خدمة عاموس بفترة حكم يربعام الثان: Amos's ministry was associated with the reign of Jeroboam II in the northern kingdom, a period that saw political expansion and economic prosperity for Israel. Yet this prosperity was not distributed justly among the social classes, and so Amos saw behind the flourishing appearance a serious moral and spiritual crisis. His ministry preceded the fall of the northern kingdom by many years, but it came at a time when the signs of moral and political collapse were beginning to appear clearly.
كان عاموس من يهوذا، لكنه أُرسل أساسًا إل: Amos was from Judah, but he was sent primarily to the northern kingdom of Israel, especially to the religious and political centers such as Bethel and Samaria. He was speaking to a community that enjoyed strength and prosperity and believed that its religious relationship to God guaranteed its protection. Therefore, his message came as a shock: election does not exempt one from judgment, and worship does not protect a person if he lives in injustice.
كتب عاموس ليعلن أن الله يرى الظلم الاجتم: Amos wrote to proclaim that God sees social injustice, judicial corruption, and the exploitation of the poor, and that these sins cannot be covered by sacrifices, festivals, and hymns. He also proclaimed that Israel, even though it was the covenant people, was not above accountability, because its privilege made its responsibility greater. Therefore, the Book of Amos strongly links covenant theology, ethics, and social justice.
7. تقسيم سفر عاموس: 7. Division of the Book of Amos
The book can be divided into four main sections. Chapters 1–2 present judgments against the nations and then direct judgment against Judah and Israel; chapters 3–6 then offer prophetic sermons that expose Israel's sins and declare the nearness of judgment. After that come chapters 7–9:10 in the form of prophetic visions, such as the locusts, the fire, the plumb line, and the basket full of summer fruit; then the book ends in 9:11–15 with a promise of restoration and the raising up of 'the fallen tent of David.'
يبدأ السفر بإعلان أن الرب يزمجر من صهيون: The book begins with the proclamation that the Lord roars from Zion, a very powerful image of God's presence as judge. Then Amos begins to condemn the nations surrounding Israel, such as Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, and Moab. This arrangement has a clever literary and theological effect, because the Israelite listener may easily agree with the judgment against his enemies, and then discover that judgment will also turn toward him.
9. لماذا بدأ عاموس بالأمم؟: 9. Why did Amos begin with the nations?
كان إسرائيل يرى نفسه شعبًا مميزًا، وربما: Israel saw itself as a special people, and perhaps felt that the nations were deserving of judgment while it was secure. Therefore, Amos makes the people first agree with God's judgments against others, then gradually turns the message toward Judah and Israel. Here one of the strongest techniques of the book appears: God does not require a person to see the sin of others before he allows him to see his own sin.
كانت الجرائم المذكورة ضد الأمم تتعلق بال: The crimes mentioned against the nations involved violence, human trafficking, betrayal, revenge, and brutality. This reveals that God is not concerned only with the way his people worship, but also judges the nations for moral and human evil. Divine justice transcends national boundaries, and no state or people can consider itself outside the sphere of God's authority.
بعد الأمم، ينتقل عاموس إلى يهوذا ثم إسرا: After the nations, Amos moves on to Judah and then to Israel. This means that possessing the law, the temple, and knowledge does not exempt one from responsibility. Rather, the more a person knows God, the greater his moral responsibility becomes; therefore, Israel's judgment was severe because the people knew the Lord but lived against him.
12. «أما أنتم فقد عكستم الطريق»: 12. 'But you have turned aside from the way'
يبرز السفر خطايا إسرائيل بطريقة شديدة ال: The book highlights Israel's sins with striking clarity: selling the righteous for silver, the needy for a pair of sandals, trampling the heads of the poor, and exploiting the weak. These are not merely individual mistakes, but a social and economic system that made power and wealth a means of humiliating people. Therefore, Amos becomes one of the most important books for the study of social justice in the Bible.
تظهر في عاموس صورة مجتمع أصبحت فيه قيمة: In Amos appears the image of a society in which the value of the human person has fallen below money. The righteous are sold for profit, the poor are treated as merchandise, and justice can be influenced by bribery and self-interest. Therefore, the book declares that God does not view economics as a realm separate from faith, because the way a person deals with money reveals the truth of his relationship to God.
«اطلبوا الخير لا الشر لكي تحيوا، فيكون ا: 'Seek good and not evil so that you may live, and the Lord God of hosts may be with you as you have said.'
هذه دعوة مباشرة إلى التغيير، وهي تؤكد أن: This is a direct call to change, and it emphasizes that repentance in the book is not merely religious feeling. What is required is a change in moral direction itself, because anyone who seeks God must seek good, justice, and righteousness in the community. Therefore, Amos links seeking God with seeking good.
من أشهر نصوص السفر:: One of the best-known texts of the book is:
«ولكن ليجر الحق كالمياه والبر كنهر دائم»: 'But let justice roll like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.'
الصورة هنا مأخوذة من عالم الماء الجاري،: The imagery is taken from the world of running water, where a river is not merely a series of isolated drops but a continuous flow. Therefore, God does not want seasonal justice that appears on religious occasions, but righteousness and justice as a continual life in the community. This verse summarizes in an astonishing way Amos's social and spiritual message.
يقدم عاموس واحدًا من أقوى الانتقادات للع: Amos offers one of the strongest criticisms of formal worship:
«إني أبغض أعيادكم وأرذلها، ولست ألتذ باع: 'I hate your festivals and despise them; I do not delight in your solemn assemblies.'
«ابعد عني ضجة أغانيك، ونغم ربابك لا أسمع: 'Take away from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps.'
المشكلة ليست أن الله يكره الأعياد أو الت: The problem is not that God hates festivals or praise in themselves, for worship is essential in Scripture; the problem is that the people were offering worship while practicing injustice. Therefore, Amos declares that worship separated from righteousness becomes an insult rather than an act of honor.
هذه الآية ليست مجرد شعار اجتماعي، بل نتي: This verse is not merely a social slogan, but a direct result of understanding God as a holy and just God. If God is just, then his people are called to reflect his justice in judgment, economics, and relationships. Thus Amos presents a comprehensive concept of worship: an altar without justice does not please God, and a hymn without righteousness does not compensate for injustice.
18. «هل يسير اثنان معًا إن لم يتواعدا؟»: 18. 'Can two walk together unless they have agreed to do so?'
في الأصحاح الثالث يستخدم عاموس سلسلة من: In the third chapter, Amos uses a series of short questions that lead to a single conclusion. If the lion roars, there is a reason; and if something happens in the city, there is a reason; and if the Lord speaks, then the prophet must speak. Here Amos defends the necessity of prophecy: the prophet does not speak on his own initiative, but because he has heard the word of the Lord.
من أهم مبادئ عاموس:: One of Amos's most important principles is:
«إياكم فقط عرفت من جميع قبائل الأرض، لذل: 'You only have I known among all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your sins.'
هذه الآية تقلب مفهوم الاختيار رأسًا على: This verse turns the concept of election upside down. Knowledge and election are not guarantees against discipline, but make responsibility greater. Therefore, the people of God cannot say, 'We are chosen, therefore we are safe no matter what we do.'
كانت السامرة العاصمة السياسية للمملكة ال: Samaria was the political capital of the northern kingdom and had become a symbol of prosperity, the wealthy class, and political power. But Amos sees behind the palaces social corruption and exploitation of the poor. Therefore, Samaria becomes an example of a society that may appear strong from the outside, but is morally collapsing from within.
يستخدم عاموس تعبيرًا شديد اللهجة:: Amos uses a very sharp expression:
«اسمعي هذا القول يا بقرات باشان التي في: 'Hear this word, you cows of Bashan who are on Mount Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy,'
لا يقصد مجرد إهانة لفظية، بل يستخدم صورة: He does not mean mere verbal insult, but uses the image of large, luxurious animals to describe a class that lives in comfort while the poor are crushed. Here he declares that wealth built on injustice is not a blessing, but a charge of accusation before God.
22. يوم الرب في عاموس: 22. The day of the Lord in Amos
كان الشعب يتوقع أن يكون يوم الرب يوم انت: The people expected the day of the Lord to be a day of victory for Israel over her enemies. But Amos turns that expectation completely upside down:
«ويل للذين يشتهون يوم الرب! لماذا لكم يو: 'Woe to you who long for the day of the Lord! Why do you desire the day of the Lord? It is darkness, not light.'
وهذا من أعظم إسهامات السفر في مفهوم يوم: This is one of the greatest contributions of the book to the concept of the day of the Lord, because a person may long for God's intervention when he thinks it will be to his advantage, but he forgets that God will judge everyone, including his own people.
23. «كما لو هرب إنسان من أسد»: 23. 'As if a man fled from a lion'
يصف عاموس يوم الرب بصورة مظلمة: يهرب الإ: Amos describes the day of the Lord in dark imagery: a person flees from a lion and meets a bear, then enters the house and leans against the wall and is bitten by a snake. The image expresses the impossibility of escaping judgment when its time comes. This is not to produce despair, but to remove the illusion that rituals, place, or national affiliation can protect a person from God's justice.
في الأصحاحات 7–9 يستخدم الله سلسلة من ال: In chapters 7–9, God uses a series of visions to clarify judgment. Amos sees the locusts, then fire, then the plumb line, then the basket full of summer fruit, and finally a scene of judgment at the altar. These visions move the message from general speech to concentrated symbolic images that reveal that judgment is drawing near.
في الرؤيا الأولى يرى عاموس الجراد يأكل ن: In the first vision Amos sees locusts eating the plants of the earth. The prophet cries out:
«أيها السيد الرب، اصْفَح! كيف يقوم يعقوب: 'Lord God, forgive! How can Jacob stand, for he is small?'
ويستجيب الرب ويتراجع عن تنفيذ الحكم في ت: And the Lord responds and relents from carrying out judgment in that vision. This reveals that the prophet is not merely a cold transmitter of judgment, but participates in intercession for his people.
يرى عاموس نارًا تلتهم الغمر العظيم وتأكل: Amos sees fire consuming the great deep and eating up the inheritance. Again the prophet intercedes, and again the Lord responds. This reveals that intercession is at the heart of prophetic work, and that the proclamation of judgment does not eliminate the possibility of mercy.
في الرؤيا الثالثة يرى عاموس الرب قائمًا: In the third vision Amos sees the Lord standing beside a wall with a plumb line in his hand. The plumb line is an instrument used to measure the straightness of a structure, and so the image becomes clear: God does not measure Israel by comparison with the nations or by its former level, but by the standard of his justice. When deviation appears, neither the temple, nor history, nor privilege can hide it.
28. السلة المملوءة من الثمر الصيفي: 28. The basket full of summer fruit
في الرؤيا الرابعة يرى عاموس سلة من الثمر: In the fourth vision, Amos sees a basket of summer fruit, and the Lord uses a wordplay in Hebrew between the word related to summer fruit and the announcement that the end has come upon his people. Here the image of fruit indicating the end of the season transforms into a symbol for the end of Israel's phase. The message is that the time of waiting has come to an end.
يظهر أمصيا كاهن بيت إيل ويطلب من عاموس أ: Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, appears and asks Amos to flee to the land of Judah and prophesy there. This confrontation reveals the conflict between true prophecy and the religious institution connected to power. Amos responds that he was not a professional prophet, but was a shepherd, and the Lord took him from behind the flock and said to him: "Go, prophesy to my people Israel."
كانت بيت إيل مركزًا دينيًا مهمًا في المم: Bethel was an important religious center in the northern kingdom, but it had been connected since the days of Jeroboam the First with the system of the golden calves. Therefore, Amos stands in a place that is sacred religiously with a long history, but he declares that the sacred place cannot protect a people living in evil. The place may be sacred in memory, but worship needs a sacred heart in the present.
31. «لست أنا نبيًا ولا أنا ابن نبي»: 31. "I am not a prophet nor am I a son of a prophet"
هذه العبارة من أشهر عبارات عاموس:: This phrase is one of the most famous phrases of Amos:
«لست أنا نبيًا ولا أنا ابن نبي، بل أنا ر: "I am not a prophet nor am I a son of a prophet, but I am a shepherd and a tender of sycamore figs."
لا يقصد عاموس إنكار أن الله دعاه نبيًا،: Amos does not mean denying that God called him a prophet, but he affirms that he was not a member of a professional prophetic institution. The authority of his message does not come from his office, but from the fact that the Lord took him and sent him. And this idea is very important in the study of the nature of the prophetic calling.
يربط السفر زمن خدمته بزلزلة كبيرة، ثم تش: The book connects the time of his ministry to a great earthquake, and then the prophecy points to a natural disaster that occurred in that period. This also appears in Zechariah 14:5, which recalls the historical earthquake in the days of Uzziah. Therefore, the book presents an important point for studying the relationship between historical events and prophetic memory.
رغم أن عاموس لم يكن يشهد بعد سقوط السامر: Although Amos did not yet witness the final fall of Samaria, his book clearly points to the announcement that the northern kingdom will face the fall because of its sins. Economic and political prosperity cannot cancel judgment when society transforms into a system of injustice. And within a few decades the fall of Samaria to Assyria in the year 722 B.C. (approximately) was fulfilled, which gives Amos's warnings great historical weight.
Here comes the great surprise at the end of the book. After a long series of judgments, Amos does not end with the word "destruction," but with a promise:
"In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen."
وهذا يعني أن الدينونة ليست إلغاءً لقصد ا: And this means that judgment is not a cancellation of God's salvific purpose. God demolishes what has been corrupted, but he can build again, and restore what has collapsed according to his purpose.
35. «خيمة داود الساقطة»: 35. "The Tabernacle of David That Is Fallen"
خيمة داود تشير إلى بيت داود والملكوت الد: The tabernacle of David refers to the house of David and the Davidic kingdom, which had entered a state of weakness and division. And Amos declares that God will raise it up again. And for this reason this text became very important in the New Testament, where James uses it in Acts 15:15–17 in the context of the nations entering into God's people.
يظهر سفر عاموس في العهد الجديد بصورة واض: The book of Amos appears in the New Testament clearly in Acts 15, when the apostles discussed the issue of accepting the nations. James cites the text of Amos about the raising up of the tabernacle of David, and he sees in it a prophetic framework that is consistent with the entry of the nations into the sphere of salvation. And thus the book that was speaking of the recovery of Israel and the house of David moves to a broader horizon in God's plan for salvation.
37. أهم الأشخاص في السفر: 37. The Most Important Figures in the Book
النبي القادم من تقوع في يهوذا، الذي أرسل: The prophet who came from Tekoa in Judah, whom God sent to the northern kingdom to announce justice, judgment, and repentance.
ملك يهوذا الذي كان يحكم في زمن خدمة عامو: The king of Judah who was ruling at the time of Amos's ministry.
ملك إسرائيل الذي حكم في فترة ازدهار المم: The king of Israel who ruled during the period of prosperity of the northern kingdom during Amos's ministry.
كاهن بيت إيل الذي قاوم رسالة عاموس وحاول: The priest of Bethel who opposed Amos's message and tried to remove him from Israel.
ليسوا أشخاصًا محددين بالاسم، لكنهم يمثلو: They are not specific individuals by name, but they represent the group in whom Amos revealed the injustice of society falling upon them.
38. أهم الأحداث في السفر: 38. The Most Important Events in the Book
إعلان الأحكام على الأمم، الحكم على يهوذا: The announcement of judgments on the nations, the judgment on Judah, the condemnation of Israel, the revelation of the selling of the poor and their exploitation, the condemnation of the wealthy class, the announcement that worship without justice is rejected, the warning of the day of the Lord, the announcement of the necessity of seeking the good and justice, the vision of the locusts, the vision of the fire, the vision of the plumb line, the vision of the basket filled with summer fruit, the confrontation with Amaziah, the announcement of the fall of Israel, and then the promise of the raising up of the tabernacle of David that is fallen and the recovery of the people and the land.
39. أهم رسالة يقدمها السفر: 39. The Most Important Message the Book Presents
الله لا يقبل عبادة تُرفع إليه بينما يُسح: God does not accept worship raised up to him while humans are crushed on the way to the temple; justice, mercy, and truth are not social additions to faith, but part of the very essence of worship itself, and therefore the people who multiply sacrifices and festivals without living righteousness cannot hide behind religion, because God measures his people with the plumb line of truth, and yet the door of recovery remains open, because God who judges the fallen tabernacle can raise up the tabernacle of David again.
40. ماذا يشير لنا سفر عاموس؟: 40. What Does the Book of Amos Point Us to?
يشير السفر إلى أن الله يهتم بالإنسان الذ: The book points out that God cares for the human being who is oppressed just as he cares for the altar on which worship is offered. And it announces that faith that does not produce justice and mercy is faith distorted, and that the church and believers cannot separate worship from conduct. It also warns of the danger of economic success transforming into a false sense of security, because prosperity does not necessarily mean God's pleasure. And finally it announces that God is capable of recovering what has fallen and raising up what has been demolished when return is made to his ways.
يُعد عاموس من أهم الأسفار الكتابية لدراس: Amos is considered one of the most important biblical books for the study of social justice, because it rejects the separation between spiritual life and economic and judicial life. The unjust scale, bribery, the exploitation of the poor, and the selling of humans for money, are all issues that God sees as spiritual issues and not merely civil issues. Therefore, the message of Amos says to the researcher: test your faith not only by what you say in the church, but by what you do when you have power or money or authority.
لا يريد عاموس إلغاء العبادة، بل يريد إعا: Amos does not want to abolish worship, but he wants to restore it to its reality. The hymn, the sacrifice, the fast, and the celebration can be sacred things when they come from an upright heart, but they become rejected when used as a cover for the oppression of others. And from here comes the importance of the verse: "Let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream," because true worship must appear in life.
43. عاموس ويوم الرب: 43. Amos and the Day of the Lord
يعلمنا عاموس أن انتظار تدخل الله يجب ألا: Amos teaches us that waiting for God's intervention should not transform into a false confidence that God will always stand on our side no matter how our lives are. The day of the Lord is a day of justice before it is a day of national victory. Therefore, the real question is not: "Will God come?" but: "How will God find me when he comes?"
يصل خط عاموس المسياني بصورة خاصة من خلال: The messianic line of Amos reaches specifically through the tabernacle of David that is fallen. In Acts 15, James uses the text of Amos in interpreting God's work among the nations, and connects the raising up of the tabernacle of David with the expansion of the circle of God's people. And in Christian reading, this becomes part of the biblical line that reaches to the Messiah, Son of David, in whom the promises of the kingdom and recovery are fulfilled in a way broader than the boundaries of the ancient kingdom.
يحمل السفر تحذيرًا مهمًا للكنيسة المعاصر: The book carries an important warning for the contemporary church: the abundance of religious activity is not sufficient evidence of God's pleasure. Meetings, hymns, and services can increase while there are systems of oppression or partiality or exploitation or neglect of the poor. Therefore, Amos calls the believer to make righteousness, mercy, and truth part of the church's witness, because the Gospel that we proclaim must also appear in how we treat humans.
46. الحركة الكبرى لسفر عاموس: 46. The Great Movement of the Book of Amos
يمكن تلخيص السفر في هذا المسار:: The book can be summarized in this path:
The tabernacle of David that is fallen.
وبذلك فإن عاموس يأخذ القارئ من القصور إل: And thus Amos takes the reader from the palaces to the altar, and from the altar to the street, and from the street to God's court, and from the court to the promise of recovery.

«سفر عاموس يعلن أن الله لا يمكن أن يُخدع: «The Book of Amos proclaims that God cannot be deceived by a beautiful religious appearance while the oppressed cry out under the feet of the oppressor; the God who sees the sacrifice also sees the scales, and the one who hears the song hears the cry of the poor, and the one who looks at the temple looks at the heart and conduct, and therefore declares that worship which does not result in justice and righteousness becomes empty noise before Him, and the Day of the Lord which the religious expect to be their day of triumph can become their day of judgment, and yet the story does not end in destruction, for the God who reveals Israel's fall declares in the end: «In that day I will raise up the tent of David that has fallen,» to declare that behind judgment is a greater purpose: to raise up what has fallen, to restore what has been destroyed, and to display the kingdom of God in justice and righteousness.»
ملاحظة منهجية: أخبار الأيام الأول والثان: Methodological Note: First Chronicles and Second Chronicles were originally a single work, then divided into two books. In the Hebrew Bible the work is known as דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים — Divrê Hayyāmîm, that is, «matters of the days» or «events of the days,» while it carried in the Greek translation the name Paraleipomena, that is, «omitted/overlooked matters,» because the translators saw in it additional material to the history of Samuel and Kings. But this description does not give the book its due; it is not merely a repetition of what came before, but a theological rereading of the history of Israel after the exile, with the aim of restoring identity, worship, and hope in God's covenant with David.
أولًا: سفر أخبار الأيام الأول: First: The Book of First Chronicles
1. اسم السفر ومعناه: 1. The Name of the Book and Its Meaning
الاسم العبري דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים — Divrê: The Hebrew name דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים — Divrê Hayyāmîm literally means «matters of the days» or «events of the days,» and it is an expression close in meaning to historical records or royal annals and events. As for the name that has come to us in modern languages, «Chronicles,» it is connected to the title by which the book became known in the Latin tradition.
وهذا الاسم مهم لأن السفر لا يريد فقط أن: This name is important because the book does not just want to tell us what happened, but wants to ask: What does what happened mean before God?
فالكاتب يعود إلى الماضي، لكنه يخاطب شعبً: The writer goes back to the past, but he addresses a people living after the catastrophe of exile, and therefore the study of history becomes a means of rebuilding faith, identity, and hope.
The book does not explicitly mention the name of the author.
ويُطلق الباحثون عادة على المؤلف اسم «الم: Scholars generally call the author «the Chronicler» or «the writer of Chronicles» — The Chronicler, and it is understood from the nature of the work that he was a writer with extensive knowledge of genealogies, the temple, the Levites, systems of worship, and historical records. Some studies suggest that he was a priest or Levite with scriptural training and a connection to the service of the temple in the Persian period.
أما التقليد اليهودي القديم فقد نسب السفر: As for the ancient Jewish tradition, it attributed the book to Ezra the Scribe, and there are literary and historical reasons that led some scholars to support this view, especially the similarity between the end of Second Chronicles and the beginning of the Book of Ezra. But from a scientific standpoint we cannot say that Ezra is the author with certainty, because the text itself does not explicitly state this.
3. زمن كتابة السفر: 3. The Time of Writing of the Book
يرتبط تاريخ الكتابة بوضوح بالعصر الذي أع: The date of writing is clearly connected to the period following the Babylonian exile.
فالسفر ينتهي بمرسوم كورش ملك فارس سنة 53: The book ends with the decree of Cyrus king of Persia in the year 538 B.C., which allowed the Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the house of the Lord, and the genealogy of David in 1 Chronicles 3 extends to generations after Zerubbabel. For this reason many scholars place the final composition in the second half of the fifth century before the common era, approximately 450–400 B.C., with variations in determining the precise date.
This period is very important for understanding the book.
فالقارئ الأصلي ليس إسرائيليًا يعيش في أي: The original reader is not an Israelite living in the days of David, but a person who has returned from exile and sees Jerusalem partly rebuilt, and asks:
من نحن؟ وهل ما زالت وعود الله لنا قائمة؟: Who are we? And do God's promises to us still stand? And do we still have a place in the story of the covenant?
4. لمن كتب السفر؟: 4. For Whom Was the Book Written?
كُتب أساسًا للجماعة اليهودية التي عادت م: It was written essentially for the Jewish community that returned from exile and settled in the land of Judah around Jerusalem.
وكانت هذه الجماعة تواجه أزمة هوية عميقة؛: And this community faced a deep crisis of identity; the ancient kingdom had ended, the Davidic throne was no longer standing as it was, the temple built by Solomon was destroyed and then rebuilt, and the people came to live under Persian rule.
لذلك يقدم السفر لهم إجابة قوية:: Therefore the book presents to them a powerful answer:
أنتم لستم شعبًا بلا تاريخ، ولستم شعبًا ب: You are not a people without history, and you are not a people without promise, and you are not a people whose story ended with exile.
5. سبب كتابة أخبار الأيام الأول: 5. The Reason for Writing First Chronicles
أولها إعادة تثبيت هوية إسرائيل من خلال ا: First is the reestablishment of Israel's identity through genealogy.
Second is the affirmation of the continuation of God's covenant with David.
وثالثها إعادة مركزية الهيكل والعبادة وال: Third is the recentering of the temple, worship, priesthood, and the Levites.
ورابعها إعطاء الشعب العائد من السبي رجاء: Fourth is to give the people returning from exile hope for the future.
فالكاتب لا يروي الماضي لمجرد الحنين، بل: The writer does not narrate the past merely for nostalgia, but wants to say:

تبدأ كولوسي بالصلاة والشكر من أجل الإيما: Colossians begins with prayer and thanksgiving for faith, love, and hope, then moves directly to the center of the letter: Christ; his image is the image of the invisible God, and through him all things were created, and he is before all things, and in him all things hold together, and he is the head of the church, and the firstborn from the dead, and in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead. From this truth Paul moves to the salvific work of Christ, since he made reconciliation through the blood of his cross, and transferred man from enmity to fellowship, and declared that Christ dwelling in the believer is the hope of glory. Then he warns against philosophy and tradition and asceticism and practices that try to add something to Christ, asserting that believers are filled in him and that all treasures of wisdom and knowledge are stored in him. After that he moves from doctrine to life: if you have been raised with Christ, seek what is above, put to death the members of sin, put off the old self and put on the new self, then let the love of Christ and his peace and his word rule your life. And finally this new life enters into the home and work and service and prayer, so that everything becomes in the name of the Lord Jesus. Thus Colossians moves from the greatness of Christ, to the sufficiency of the cross, to the fullness of the believer in Christ, to the rejection of alternatives, then to a new life governed by Christ in all things.
رسالة كولوسي هي رسالة سمو المسيح وكفايته: The letter to the Colossians is a message of the supremacy of Christ and his absolute sufficiency. It does not present Christ as one of the spiritual means, but as the center of creation, salvation, the church, and the new life. He is the image of the invisible God, the creator prior to all things, the head of the church, the firstborn of the resurrection, and in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily. Through the cross of Christ reconciliation is accomplished and victory over the powers of evil is announced, and Christ in the believer becomes the hope of glory. Therefore Paul warns against every philosophy or tradition or religious practice that separates man from the sufficiency of Christ, and affirms that the believer is filled in him. Then comes the practical life as a direct consequence of this truth: whoever has been raised with Christ seeks what is above, puts to death sin, puts off the old self, puts on the new self, and lives in love, peace, word, and prayer. Thus Colossians summarizes its message in one declaration: Christ is all, in him is sufficiency, from him comes life, and for his sake all things ought to live.

الفكرة المركزية للسفر: سفر دانيال هو سفر: The central idea of the book: The Book of Daniel is a book of God's sovereignty over kingdoms, human faithfulness in the midst of a pagan world, the sanctity of life in captivity, the revealing of mysteries of the future, and the triumph of God's kingdom over all earthly kingdoms. The book uniquely combines historical narratives in chapters 1–6 and prophetic visions in chapters 7–12, and therefore does not separate between faith and daily life on the one hand, and between history and prophecy on the other. Daniel and his companions live in the heart of the Babylonian Empire, but they refuse to allow the political and cultural environment surrounding them to reshape their identity, and at the same time the book declares that kingdoms that appear eternal in human sight are not eternal before God, because 'the Most High is sovereign over the kingdoms of men.' From here the book moves from captivity to faithfulness, from trial to revelation, from kingdoms of men to the kingdom of God, and from earthly history to eternal hope.
اسم السفر هو دانيال، والاسم العبري דָּנִ: The name of the book is Daniel, and the Hebrew name is דָּנִיֵּאל—Dāniyyēl, and it consists of the element dān—דִּין connected to judgment or ruling, and the element ēl—אֵל which means God. Therefore the name carries a meaning close to 'God the judge' or 'God is the judge.' And this meaning fits deeply with the content of the book, because Daniel lives before earthly kings who possess power and strength, but the events reveal that the final judgment is not in the hand of Nebuchadnezzar or Darius or any other king, but in the hand of God who raises up kings and removes them and determines the times of kingdoms and their endings.
كان دانيال شابًا يهوديًا أُخذ إلى بابل ض: Daniel was a young Jewish man who was taken to Babylon among the captives in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, and was chosen along with a group of young men to study in the king's palace. It appears from the book that he was endowed with intelligence and wisdom and ability to understand languages and sciences, but he did not allow these abilities to separate him from his faith in God. His character is distinguished by the fact that his faithfulness was not connected to his presence in Jerusalem or to the presence of a believing community around him, but he was able to maintain his relationship with God while living in the heart of a pagan global system.
3. سنة ميلاد دانيال ووفاته: 3. The year of Daniel's birth and death
لا يقدم الكتاب المقدس تاريخ ميلاد دانيال: The Holy Bible does not provide the date of Daniel's birth or the date of his death, and therefore they cannot be determined precisely. But he was a young man when he was taken to Babylon, and his professional and prophetic life continued during the reign of several kings, from Nebuchadnezzar to Belshazzar then Darius, and perhaps his service extended to the beginning of the reign of Cyrus the Persian. This means that Daniel lived through a long period of major political transformations, and witnessed the transfer of power from Babylon to Media and Persia, and yet remained steadfast in his testimony to God.
يرتبط الإطار التاريخي للسفر بالقرن الساد: The historical framework of the book is related to the sixth century before Christ, beginning from the captivity of Judah to Babylon and continuing through the transformation from the Babylonian Empire to the Median-Persian Empire. The narrative places the beginning of events in the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim, while some visions extend to later years of Daniel's life. As for the question of the date of the final composition of the book, scholars have discussed it at length, the Jewish and Christian tradition attributes the book to Daniel himself in the sixth century before Christ, while some critical scholars see a later date for the formulation, especially because of the nature of the prophecies related to kingdoms. Therefore it is important in academic study to distinguish between the history that the book presents of events and visions and between the critical debate over the date of its final composition.
5. لمن كتب السفر؟: 5. For whom was the book written?
يخاطب السفر شعب الله الذي يعيش في بيئة س: The book addresses God's people who live in a hostile or oppressive political and cultural environment, and therefore carries a direct message to the believer who finds himself far from his homeland or surrounded by a culture that does not share his faith. It also addresses every generation living under the authority of human empires and needs to remember that the power of the state is not the ultimate power in history. From here Daniel can be read as a book that presents to the people a fundamental question: Can you be faithful to God when circumstances change around you?
السبب الأول هو تقديم نموذج عملي للأمانة: The first reason is to present a practical model of faithfulness to God in the midst of captivity and cultural pressure, but the book goes beyond that to declare that God is the Lord of history. He is the one who gave Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, he is the one who revealed the king's dream, he is the one who rescued the young men from the fire, he is the one who shut the lions' mouths, he is the one who announced the fall of Babylon, and he is the one who revealed to Daniel the succession of coming kingdoms. Therefore the book does not only want to say to the believer: be faithful, but adds to it a greater truth: be faithful because God is the owner of history, and the kingdoms that frighten you today are only a temporary phase in his story.
7. التقسيم العام للسفر: 7. The general division of the book
ينقسم السفر بصورة أساسية إلى قسمين كبيري: The book is essentially divided into two major sections. Chapters 1–6 present historical narratives about Daniel and his companions in the royal court, and include the food, the golden image, the fiery furnace, the dream of the tree, the writing on the wall, and the lions' den. Meanwhile chapters 7–12 present prophetic visions related to successive kingdoms and historical conflict and persecution and judgment and hope and resurrection. The general structure can be summarized thus: faith in history, then the interpretation of history in the light of God's revelation.
تبدأ قصة دانيال في موقف يبدو صغيرًا لكنه: Daniel's story begins in a situation that appears small but reveals a great principle, as Daniel decided not to defile himself with the royal food and wine. The problem here is not merely a difference in diet, but a matter of identity and loyalty and holiness, because Daniel found himself within an integrated program to reshape the identity of young Jewish men in Babylon. Therefore Daniel's first victory was not over a lion or a king, but an internal victory: to remain with God while living in a culture that wants to redefine him.
9. تغيير أسماء دانيال ورفقائه: 9. The changing of names of Daniel and his companions
أُعطيت لدانيال ورفقائه أسماء بابلية جديد: New Babylonian names were given to Daniel and his companions, and this step has clear cultural significance, because the name in the ancient world was connected to identity and belonging. The empire wanted to reshape these young men through language and education and names and food, but the changing of the name did not change the reality of their belonging to God. And here the book presents a very important principle: the environment can change what surrounds a person, but it cannot change his internal identity unless he allows it to.
هذه العبارة من أهم مفاتيح السفر:: This phrase is one of the most important keys to the book:
«أما دانيال فجعل في قلبه أنه لا يتنجس بأ: 'But Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king's food, or with the wine that he drank.'
لم ينتظر دانيال حتى تبدأ الأزمة لكي يقرر: Daniel did not wait until the crisis began to decide his stance, but made the decision beforehand. This reveals that faithfulness in a moment of great trial is often built from previous small decisions, because when a person determines his loyalty before pressure comes, he becomes more able to stand firm when the pressure arrives. Therefore the Book of Daniel begins from a decision of the heart before it begins from a miracle of God.
يحلم نبوخذنصر بتمثال عظيم رأسه من ذهب، و: Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great image whose head was of gold, and its chest and arms of silver, and its belly and thighs of bronze, and its legs of iron, and its feet of iron and clay. Then stones come and cut out without hands and strike the image, and crush the kingdoms that it represents, and the stone becomes a great mountain that fills the earth. This vision presents one of the greatest biblical images of the weakness of earthly kingdoms before God's kingdom.
يعلن دانيال أن الذهب يمثل مملكة نبوخذنصر: Daniel declares that the gold represents the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar, and then other kingdoms come after it, and the vision ends with the stone which symbolizes a kingdom established by the God of heaven. Scholars have disagreed in determining the details of the subsequent kingdoms, especially in some different historical readings, but the basic axis of the text is firm: history is not a random series of empires, but falls under the authority of God, and in the end God's kingdom triumphs over the kingdoms of men.
13. الحجر الذي صار جبلًا: 13. The stone that became a mountain
الحجر الذي يقطع بغير يدين هو من أكثر الص: The stone that is cut out without hands is one of the most theologically important images in the book, because it does not come as a result of human military power or a political revolution led by a man. It is a divine work that strikes the system that appears solid before men, then transforms into a mountain that fills the earth. In the Christian reading this text became an important part of the study of God's kingdom and Christ, because the New Testament declares that God's kingdom entered history decisively through Christ, and will reach its fullness in the end.
يرفض شدرخ وميشخ وعبدنغو أن يسجدوا لتمثال: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to bow down to the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar set up, so the king issues an order to throw them into the fire. This story presents a powerful image of the conflict between worship of the state and worship of God, because what was asked of them was not merely to respect the king but to offer religious worship to an image made by man. And here the question becomes: does a person preserve his life at any cost, or does he remain faithful to God even when the cost is death?
15. «إلهنا الذي نعبده يستطيع أن ينجينا»: 15. 'Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us'
يجيب الثلاثة الملك:: The three reply to the king:
«هوذا يوجد إلهنا الذي نعبده يستطيع أن ين: 'Behold, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king.'
لكنهم يضيفون معنى أعظم عندما يعلنون أنهم: But they add a greater meaning when they declare that they will not bow down even if God does not deliver them. This is one of the deepest images of faith in the book, because their faith does not rest on a bargain with God, but on God's faithfulness even when they do not understand how he works. Therefore biblical faith does not only say: 'God will deliver me,' but can also say: 'And if he does not, I will not forsake him.'
16. الرابع الشبيه بابن الآلهة: 16. The fourth one like a son of the gods
يرى نبوخذنصر داخل الأتون أربعة رجال بدل: Nebuchadnezzar sees inside the furnace four men instead of three, and describes the fourth in an exceptional way. Interpreters have differed in identifying this fourth figure: some have seen him as an angelic appearance, and others have seen in him a divine appearance or a later messianic reading. Therefore one should not be dogmatic about what the text does not explicitly state, but the core message is clear: God did not necessarily prevent the trial, but he entered with his servants into the midst of the trial and did not leave them alone.
يحلم نبوخذنصر بشجرة عظيمة تمتد إلى السما: Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a great tree that extends to the sky and from which everyone eats, then the command comes to cut it down. Daniel interprets the dream as a warning to the king about his pride, and then the word is fulfilled when Nebuchadnezzar speaks boastfully of his greatness and his kingdom. Here one of the most important principles of the book appears: whoever raises himself above the bounds of humanity discovers that his authority is limited before God.
18. «لكي يعلم الأحياء أن العلي متسلط»: 18. "That the living may know that the Most High rules"
هذه العبارة تختصر لاهوت السفر السياسي:: This phrase sums up the political theology of the book:
«لكي يعلم الأحياء أن العلي متسلط في مملك: "That the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he wills, and sets over it whomever he wills."
الله لا ينافس الملوك على مستوى سياسي متس: God does not compete with kings on an equal political level; rather, he is the possessor of the supreme authority who permits kingdoms to rise and fall. Therefore, the book of Daniel presents an entirely different perspective on history: what appears in earthly news as a struggle between kings and empires appears in heaven under the sovereignty of the true King of kings.
19. دانيال 5 — الكتابة على الحائط: 19. Daniel 5 — The Writing on the Wall
في وليمة بيلشاصر تظهر يد وتكتب على الحائ: At Belshazzar's feast a hand appears and writes on the wall:
يعلن دانيال أن أيام المملكة قد عُدت، وأن: Daniel declares that the days of the kingdom have been numbered, that the king has been weighed in the balances and found wanting, and that his kingdom will be given to the Medes and Persians. That very night Belshazzar falls, and thus the writing on the wall becomes a powerful symbol of the truth that political power cannot postpone the hour of judgment that God has determined.
سقوط بابل في السفر ليس مجرد حدث عسكري، ب: The fall of Babylon in the book is not merely a military event; it carries a clear theological meaning, for Babylon, which seemed so very powerful, was not outside God's authority. This links Daniel to the broader biblical message that sees Babylon as a symbol of human pride and of the system that resists God. Therefore, the story of its fall becomes a testimony that every empire, however great its power, has an end when its time comes before God's authority.
في عهد داريوس يرفض دانيال أن يتوقف عن ال: In the reign of Darius, Daniel refuses to stop praying despite the issuance of a decree forbidding it. He continues to pray three times a day as was his custom, and so he is thrown into the lions' den. But God sends his angel and shuts the lions' mouths, and Daniel comes out unharmed. This story confirms that Daniel's faithfulness was not a temporary stance that appeared before Nebuchadnezzar, but a way of life that continued through the changing of kings and empires.
22. لماذا صلى دانيال رغم المرسوم؟: 22. Why did Daniel pray despite the decree?
لم يكن دانيال يحاول صناعة بطولة شخصية، ب: Daniel was not trying to create a personal act of heroism; rather, he was maintaining a steady spiritual practice that preceded the crisis. Therefore, Daniel's strength in chapter six did not begin when he entered the lions' den, but began in the room where he prayed daily. This teaches that the secret life with God is what produces public steadfastness before the world.
ينتقل السفر من القصص إلى الرؤى، ويرى دان: The book moves from narratives to visions, and Daniel sees four beasts rising from the sea. The vision represents human kingdoms that appear in a beastly form, in contrast to the Son of Man who comes to the Ancient of Days and is given authority, glory, and a kingdom. This is among the most important visions in the whole book, because it moves from the image of the beasts representing earthly kingdoms to the image of the man who is associated with the eternal kingdom.
«وإذا مع سحب السماء مثل ابن إنسان أتى وج: "And behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he came to the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before him. And to him was given authority, glory, and a kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His authority is an everlasting authority which shall not pass away, and his kingdom is one that shall not be destroyed."
هذا النص أصبح من أهم النصوص المسيانية في: This text has become one of the most important messianic texts in the Bible, because Christ repeatedly used the expression "Son of Man" of himself in the Gospels. Therefore, Daniel 7 forms an important bridge between the expectation of the kingdom in the Old Testament and Christ's proclamation of his kingdom in the New Testament.
25. الفرق بين الوحوش وابن الإنسان: 25. The Difference Between the Beasts and the Son of Man
الوحوش تمثل قوى سياسية تملك القوة لكنها: The beasts represent political powers that possess strength but appear in animal form, while the kingdom associated with the Son of Man comes in human form. The contrast is most likely intentional: human kingdoms, when separated from God, turn into a predatory power, while the kingdom that comes from God appears in the form of the man who receives the everlasting authority. Here the book presents a profound theological critique of authority when it turns into predation and tyranny.
26. دانيال 8 — الكبش والتيس: 26. Daniel 8 — The Ram and the Goat
يرى دانيال كبشًا له قرنان وتيسًا له قرن: Daniel sees a ram with two horns and a goat with a great horn, and the vision presents details connected to specific kingdoms and historical events. The traditional interpretation of the vision connects it with the Medo-Persian and Greek empires, and then with the conflicts that came in the Hellenistic era. This vision reveals that God foreknows the course of great events, and that history, which seems to humans full of surprises, falls within the scope of God's knowledge and sovereignty.
من أعظم صلوات السفر صلاة دانيال في الأصح: Among the greatest prayers of the book is Daniel's prayer in chapter nine, where the prophet does not stand before God merely accusing his people, but enters with them into confession and says:
«قد أخطأنا وأثمنا وعملنا الشر وتمردنا وح: "We have sinned and committed iniquity and done wickedly and rebelled, even turning aside from your commandments and from your judgments."
وهذا مهم جدًا، لأن دانيال نفسه كان من ال: This is very important, because Daniel himself was among the figures against whom the book records no clear sin, and yet he does not stand outside the sins of his nation. He prays as one who is part of a people who need mercy, and this is a magnificent picture of intercession and confession of sin before God.
بعد صلاة دانيال تأتي النبوة المتعلقة بـ: After Daniel's prayer comes the prophecy concerning the seventy weeks, which is among the most discussed prophetic texts in biblical studies. Interpreters have differed on how to calculate them and determine their points of beginning and ending and the details of their connection to Christ, Jerusalem, and the final events. But the center of the text is that God has set a divine framework for history, and that sin, judgment, restoration, Christ, and the final events all fall within God's timeline.
29. دانيال 10–12 — الصراع الروحي والتاري: 29. Daniel 10–12 — The Spiritual and Historical Struggle
في الأصحاحات الأخيرة يدخل السفر إلى مستو: In the final chapters, the book enters a more complex level of visions, where a struggle connected with kings and nations appears, and the spiritual dimension behind political events also appears. This reveals that earthly history is not the whole story, and that behind visible struggles lie spiritual dimensions that man does not see directly. Nevertheless, the book does not give man a call to obsess over hidden details, but always returns him to steadfastness, faithfulness, and awaiting God's end.
30. القيامة في سفر دانيال: 30. The Resurrection in the Book of Daniel
يحتوي السفر على أحد أوضح نصوص العهد القد: The book contains one of the clearest Old Testament texts about the resurrection:
«وكثيرون من الراقدين في تراب الأرض يستيق: "And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt."
وهنا ينتقل السفر من التاريخ إلى الأبدية،: Here the book moves from history to eternity, and from the question of kingdoms to the question of man's ultimate destiny. For even if empires prevail for a time, and even if believers die under persecution, the end is not death, for God will raise the dead and declare judgment and eternal life.
يختم السفر بصورة رائعة عن المؤمنين الأمن: The book concludes with a wonderful picture of the faithful believers:
«والفاهمون يضيئون كضياء الجلد، والذين رد: "And those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament, and those who turn many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever."
وهذه الصورة تكشف أن قيمة الخدمة لا تقاس: This image reveals that the value of service is not measured only by what the eye sees in the present, for Daniel lived in a time when evil seemed stronger than good, and yet the book declares that the faithfulness of those who serve God will have eternal glory. Therefore, Daniel's message is not only: do not bow down to the idol, but also: continue to turn others to righteousness even if you do not see the full result now.
32. الأشخاص الرئيسية في السفر: 32. The Main Characters in the Book
النبي والحكيم الذي بقي أمينًا لله خلال ا: The prophet and sage who remained faithful to God through the exile and the changing of empires, and through whose life God used to reveal his sovereignty over history.
رفقاء دانيال الثلاثة الذين رفضوا السجود: Daniel's three companions who refused to bow down to Nebuchadnezzar's statue, and entered the furnace trusting in God.
ملك بابل العظيم، الذي يكشف السفر أن قوته: The great king of Babylon, whom the book reveals that however great his power, it remains subject to God's authority.
الملك الذي ظهرت في وليمة عهده الكتابة عل: The king in whose reign, at his feast, the writing on the wall appeared, and in whose days Babylon fell.
الملك الذي ارتبطت فترة حكمه بقصة جب الأس: The king whose reign was linked to the story of the lions' den and Daniel's deliverance.
الملك الفارسي الذي يظهر في الإطار الزمني: The Persian king who appears in the final time-frame of the book, and represents the transition to a new stage of imperial history.
الملاك والرؤى السماوية: The Angel and the Heavenly Visions
تظهر الكائنات الملائكية في بعض مشاهد الس: Angelic beings appear in some scenes of the book as servants in the declaration of divine messages, without worship being directed to them.
33. أهم الأحداث في السفر: 33. The Most Important Events in the Book
سبي دانيال ورفقائه إلى بابل، ورفض دانيال: The exile of Daniel and his companions to Babylon, Daniel's refusal to be defiled by the king's delicacies, the young men's success in wisdom, the interpretation of the dream of the statue, the three men's refusal to bow down to the golden statue, their deliverance from the furnace, the dream of the tree and Nebuchadnezzar's fall because of pride, the writing on the wall and the fall of Babylon, Daniel's being thrown into the lions' den and his deliverance, the visions of the four beasts, the vision of the Son of Man, the vision of the ram and the goat, Daniel's prayer for the people, the prophecy of the seventy weeks, the final visions, and the declaration of resurrection and eternal life.
34. أهم رسالة يقدمها السفر: 34. The Most Important Message the Book Presents
الله هو السيد الحقيقي للتاريخ، والممالك: God is the true Lord of history, and earthly kingdoms, however great their power, are not eternal; therefore the believer can live faithfully to God within a society, culture, and politics that do not share his faith. For true success is not that a person leave the world, but that he remain God's while living in it, and that he trust that God's kingdom will in the end overcome all human kingdoms, and that those who stand firm in righteousness will shine "like the stars forever and ever."
35. ماذا يشير لنا سفر دانيال؟: 35. What Does the Book of Daniel Point Us To?
يشير السفر أولًا إلى أن الهوية الروحية ي: The book points first to the fact that spiritual identity must be stronger than the pressure of culture, for Daniel lived in Babylon without Babylon becoming the final point of reference for his life. It points second to the fact that political authority is limited, for Nebuchadnezzar, Belshazzar, Darius, and all the kingdoms appear under God's authority. It points third to the fact that prayer is not a marginal habit, but a source of steadfastness in the believer's life, as clearly appears in Daniel's life. It points finally to the fact that history is moving toward an eternal kingdom, eternal life, and a final judgment, and therefore the believer's faithfulness today has a value that transcends the bounds of history.
يحتل سفر دانيال مكانة مركزية في دراسة ال: The book of Daniel occupies a central place in the study of Christ in the Old Testament, especially in the vision of the Son of Man in chapter seven. Christ repeatedly used this title of himself, and linked his appearing with judgment, the kingdom, and authority. Therefore, Daniel 7 is not merely a text about a vague future figure, but is one of the most important biblical backgrounds for understanding Christ's declaration of himself as the Son of Man, possessor of authority and the everlasting kingdom.
37. دانيال وملكوت الله: 37. Daniel and the Kingdom of God
الملكوت هو أحد أهم المحاور التي تربط أجز: The kingdom is one of the most important threads that link the parts of the book together: in the dream of the statue we see a stone that the God of heaven sets up and that becomes a kingdom that shall not be destroyed, and in the vision of the Son of Man we see an everlasting authority and a kingdom that shall not pass away. Thus the book declares that history does not end with the victory of the strongest empire, but with the victory of God's kingdom. This makes Daniel one of the most important books for understanding the relationship between the present kingdom and the coming kingdom.
يمتلك السفر مكانة خاصة في دراسة عقيدة ال: The book holds a special place in the study of the doctrine of the resurrection in the Old Testament, for Daniel 12 clearly declares the awakening of those who sleep to eternal life or to eternal shame. This makes clear that man's destiny does not end at death, and that God will raise the dead and carry out judgment. In light of the New Testament, this text becomes an important part of the background that illuminates the declaration of Christ and the apostles concerning the resurrection, eternal life, and the final judgment.
ربما تكون أهم رسالة عملية في السفر أن ال: Perhaps the most important practical message in the book is that place does not determine a person's faithfulness to God. Daniel could have said that the exile excused him from responsibility, but he did not, and he did not say that the pagan environment forced him to compromise. Rather, he lived in Babylon, learned the language and culture of the court, and served in the administration, but he did not allow Babylon to possess his heart. Here the book presents a highly important model for the believer who lives within an intellectually and culturally diverse society: participation in society does not mean dissolving into it.
40. الحركة الكبرى لسفر دانيال: 40. The Great Movement of the Book of Daniel
The disclosure of the kings' secrets.
The appearance of the Son of Man.
وهكذا يتحرك السفر من أرض السبي إلى ملكوت: Thus the book moves from the land of captivity to the Kingdom of God, from the palace of the king to the throne of God, from the power of the beasts to the authority of the Son of Man, and from death to eternal life.
41. خلاصة سفر دانيال: 41. Summary of the Book of Daniel
معنى الاسم الله ديّان / الله هو القاضي: Meaning of the name: God is Judge / God is the Judge
الخلفية يهودي في السبي البابلي: Background: a Jew in the Babylonian captivity
مكان الخدمة بابل ثم البيئة المادية الفار: Place of ministry: Babylon, then the Persian material environment
Time of events: the sixth century BC
الموضوع المركزي سيادة الله على التاريخ: Central theme: the sovereignty of God over history
أشهر معجزة النجاة من جب الأسود: Most famous miracle: deliverance from the lions' den
أشهر اختبار رفض السجود لتمثال الذهب: Most famous test: refusal to bow down to the golden statue
أشهر رؤية ابن الإنسان: Most famous vision: the Son of Man
أهم وعد أخروي القيامة والحياة الأبدية: Most important eschatological promise: resurrection and eternal life
المحور المسياني ابن الإنسان والملكوت الأ: Messianic focus: the Son of Man and the eternal kingdom
الرسالة العملية الأمانة لله وسط عالم متغ: Practical message: faithfulness to God amid a changing world
النهاية قيامة وحياة أبدية ومجد للأمناء: The ending: resurrection, eternal life, and glory for the faithful
النصوص الكتابية الأساسية: سفر دانيال 1–1: Core biblical texts: the Book of Daniel 1–12, together with a study of 2 Kings 24–25, 2 Chronicles 36, and Jeremiah 25, 29, and 52 to understand the Babylonian captivity, then Ezra 1 to understand the beginning of the return in the reign of Cyrus. For Messianic study, a special connection should be made between Daniel 7:13–14 and Matthew 24–26, Mark 13–14, and Luke 21, and the study of Daniel 12 together with John 5, Acts 24, 1 Corinthians 15, and Revelation 20–22 is also helpful in tracing the theme of the resurrection, the judgment, and the kingdom.
🔑 الجملة التي تختصر سفر دانيال: 🔑 The sentence that summarizes the Book of Daniel
«سفر دانيال يضع المؤمن داخل قلب الإمبراط: "The Book of Daniel places the believer within the heart of empires to teach him that Babylon may change its name but cannot change its identity, that the king may change the laws but cannot change the authority of God, and that the fire may blaze and the lions may surround him, yet the faithfulness of God does not change; at the same time, the book lifts the reader's eyes above kingdoms that seem great, so that he sees the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven, given authority and glory and an eternal kingdom, then hears at the end of the book the promise of resurrection and eternal life, and discovers that all of history moves from the changing kingdoms of men to the Kingdom of God that never passes away, and that those who stood firm in faith and righteousness will not lose their faithfulness, but rather 'shall shine like the stars forever and ever.'"
الاسم العبري لسفر التثنية هو דְּבָרִים —: The Hebrew name of the Book of Deuteronomy is דְּבָרִים — Devarim, meaning "words" or "sayings," taken from the opening of the book: "These are the words which Moses spoke to all Israel." This Hebrew name is very important because it reveals that the book is, in essence, Moses' final address to his people, not merely a mechanical repetition of what was already stated in Exodus, Leviticus, and Numbers.
أما الاسم اليوناني Δευτερονόμιον — Deute: As for the Greek name Δευτερονόμιον — Deuteronomion, from which the English name Deuteronomy is derived, it is connected to the meaning "the second law" or "repetition of the law." However, this expression needs to be understood precisely, because Deuteronomy does not present a law different from the law of Moses, but rather re-presents the covenant and the commandments before the new generation under new circumstances.
فالجيل الذي خرج من مصر مات معظمه في البر: The generation that came out of Egypt mostly died in the wilderness, and the generation now standing in the plains of Moab did not itself experience all the events of the exodus. Therefore Moses gathers together the history of the past, the commandments of the covenant, and the warning about the future, then sets the people before a clear choice: life and blessing through obedience, or death and curse through disobedience.
2. الكاتب ومعنى اسمه: 2. The author and the meaning of his name
ينسب التقليد اليهودي والمسيحي سفر التثني: Jewish and Christian tradition ascribes the Book of Deuteronomy to Moses, who appears in the book as the main speaker addressing Israel before its entry into the promised land. The beginning of the book affirms that Moses spoke to all Israel, while the life of Moses concludes in the final chapter with his death on Mount Nebo.
واسم موسى بالعبرية מֹשֶׁה — Mosheh، وهو: The name of Moses in Hebrew is מֹשֶׁה — Mosheh, the name associated in the Book of Exodus with his being drawn out of the water. By the end of his life, Moses had become more than merely the leader of the exodus; he became the mediator of the covenant, the lawgiver, the prophet, and the teacher who prepares the new generation for life in the land.
ومع ذلك، فإن السفر يوضح أن موسى نفسه لن: Nevertheless, the book makes clear that Moses himself will not enter the land. This paradox is of great significance: the man who led Israel from Egypt to the borders of Canaan will not cross over with them into it, but the word of God and His covenant continue after his departure.
3. ميلاد موسى ووفاته: 3. The birth and death of Moses
لا يقدم الكتاب المقدس تاريخًا تقويميًا م: Scripture does not provide a specific calendar date for the birth of Moses, so no certain year of birth can be given. 40. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 40. The Grand Movement of the Epistle
تبدأ أفسس من قصد الله الأبدي في المسيح،: Ephesians begins from God’s eternal purpose in Christ, declaring election, adoption, redemption, the forgiveness of sins, inheritance, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit. It then moves to the power of Christ’s resurrection and His authority above every principality and power, and reveals that this power is also at work in believers. After that, it moves from the individual to the Church, declaring that salvation by grace creates a new man, and that Christ broke down the wall of hostility and made Jews and Gentiles one body and a dwelling place for God. The epistle then reveals the mystery of Christ, as the Church becomes a declaration of the manifold wisdom of God, and Paul prays that Christ may dwell by faith in hearts and that believers may be filled with all the fullness of God. From the fourth chapter, the practical movement begins: from who we are in Christ to how we walk in Christ; the preservation of unity, growth into Christ, putting off the old man and putting on the new man, walking in love and light, and being filled with the Spirit are required. Then the new life appears in marriage, family, and relationships. Finally, the epistle moves from daily life to the spiritual battle, calling the believer to stand firm in the Lord, put on the whole armor of God, and pray continually. Thus Ephesians moves from God’s eternal purpose, to the work of Christ, to the Church, to the new life, to holiness, and then to steadfastness in spiritual warfare.
رسالة أفسس تقدم رؤية شاملة للإنسان والكن: The Epistle to the Ephesians presents a comprehensive vision of humanity and the Church in Christ; salvation begins with the grace of God, is accomplished through the redemption wrought by Christ, is sealed by the Holy Spirit, and then is transformed into a new life within the body of Christ. In this vision, the Church is not a human gathering, but the body of Christ, the place where the wisdom of God is declared, and the testimony of reconciliation between Jews and Gentiles. Therefore the epistle does not separate theology from life: whoever has received grace is called to holiness; whoever has become a member of the body is called to unity; whoever has known the love of Christ is called to love; whoever has been filled with the Spirit is called to walk by the Spirit; and whoever stands in Christ is called to stand firm against evil. Thus Ephesians summarizes its calling in a clear movement from identity to conduct, from grace to holiness, from unity to service, and from knowing Christ to standing firm in Him.
