وهذا النص يحتاج إلى فهمه في سياق رعاية ا: This text needs to be understood in the context of the church’s care for the sick person and prayer on his behalf, not as a mechanical formula that guarantees a particular outcome in every case.
«اعْتَرِفُوا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ بِالزَّ: “Confess your trespasses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The effective, fervent prayer of a righteous person avails much.”
الصلاة هنا مرتبطة بالمجتمع الروحي والشفا: Prayer here is connected with the spiritual community and mutual intercession.
يقدم يعقوب إيليا نموذجًا للصلاة:: James presents Elijah as a model of prayer:
«كَانَ إِيلِيَّا إِنْسَانًا تَحْتَ الآلا: “Elijah was a man with sufferings like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain.”
وهكذا يشجع المؤمن على الصلاة، موضحًا أن: Thus he encourages the believer to pray, making clear that Elijah was not a supernatural human being, but a person like us who depended on God.
54. رد الضال: 54. Restoring the One Who Has Gone Astray
تختم الرسالة بخدمة إنقاذ الإنسان الذي ضل: The epistle concludes with the ministry of rescuing the person who has gone astray:
«لِيَعْلَمْ أَنَّ مَنْ رَدَّ خَاطِئًا عَ: “Let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.”
فالرسالة التي بدأت بالنضج الروحي تنتهي ب: Thus the epistle that began with spiritual maturity ends with the restoration of the person who has gone astray.
55. المسيح في رسالة يعقوب: 55. Christ in the Epistle of James
لا تقدم الرسالة عرضًا مطولًا عن شخص المس: The epistle does not present an extended treatment of the person of Christ as John or Hebrews does, but it places Jesus at the center of the Christian life.
«عبد الله والرب يسوع المسيح»،: “a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,”
ويتحدث عن مجيء الرب، وعن «الإيمان بربنا: and speaks of the coming of the Lord, and of “faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory,” and places the whole life of the believer under the sovereignty of Christ.
وهذا مهم جدًا: يعقوب لا يفصل السلوك المس: This is very important: James does not separate Christian conduct from faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.
رسالة يعقوب غنية بالخلفية العهدية، وتظهر: The Epistle of James is rich in Old Testament background, and clear echoes appear in it from:
الأمثال: الحكمة، وضبط اللسان، والغنى، وا: Proverbs: wisdom, control of the tongue, wealth, and humility.
Leviticus: love of neighbor and the royal law.
Abraham in the Book of Genesis.
Job in the Book of Job.
Elijah in the Books of Kings.
تعاليم الأنبياء حول العدل ورعاية الفقراء: The teachings of the prophets concerning justice and care for the poor.
تقليد الحكمة اليهودية في الحديث عن الحكم: The tradition of Jewish wisdom in speaking about wisdom from above and earthly wisdom.
كما أن تعليم يعقوب عن الإيمان العامل ينس: James’s teaching about active faith is also consistent with the general trajectory of the Bible, which connects the knowledge of God with obedience.
57. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 57. The Major Movement of the Epistle
تبدأ رسالة يعقوب بالتجربة التي تختبر الإ: The Epistle of James begins with the trial that tests faith and produces patience, then moves to wisdom, the word of God, and practical obedience, and reveals that a person should not be a hearer only but a doer of the word. It then moves to the church community, warning against partiality and calling for mercy, and explaining that faith that does not appear in works is dead faith. After that, the epistle enters the sphere of the tongue, wisdom, conflicts, and love of the world, and calls the believer to humility, submission to God, and drawing near to him. It then confronts the danger of wealth, injustice, and reliance on the future, and calls for patience until the coming of the Lord. Finally, it reaches prayer, intercession, confession, the endurance of suffering, and the restoration of the person who has gone astray. Thus the epistle moves from the testing of faith to the maturity of faith, from hearing the word to doing it, from faith to mercy, from self-control to control of the tongue, from humility to prayer, and from prayer to the restoration of the one who has gone astray.
رسالة يعقوب هي رسالة الإيمان الحي الذي ي: The Epistle of James is the epistle of living faith that is manifested in life. It does not allow the believer to hide behind a doctrinal confession that does not change his conduct, but rather tests the reality of faith through patience in trials, asking for wisdom, hearing the word of God and doing it, caring for the poor, rejecting favoritism, controlling the tongue, keeping away from love of the world, humility before God, prayer, and patience until the coming of the Lord. James’s teaching about works does not mean that works are the price of justification or a substitute for grace; rather, true faith cannot remain dead without fruit. Therefore he uses Abraham and Rahab to show that faith which trusts God moves in obedience. In the end, the vision expands from the life of the individual to the life of the community: prayer for the sick, confession, intercession, and the restoration of the one who has gone astray. The epistle may be summarized in this movement: faith tested → faith maturing → faith working → faith loving and showing mercy → faith controlling the tongue → faith submitting to God → faith praying and waiting for the coming of the Lord.

الفكرة المركزية للسفر: سفر إرميا هو سفر: The central idea of the book: The Book of Jeremiah is the book of warning about judgment, exposing the corruption of the heart, proclaiming the new covenant, and hope amid ruin. Jeremiah stands in one of the most turbulent stages of Judah’s history, when Jerusalem was threatened by Babylon, and the people practiced worship while their hearts were far from God. Therefore the book does not merely present a prediction of the fall of a city, but reveals how a people who bear God’s name can reach collapse when worship becomes an external form and faith is separated from obedience. Nevertheless, the book does not end with judgment, because amid tears and ruin God declares a new promise: “I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.”
الاسم العربي هو إرميا، والاسم العبري هو: The Arabic name is Jeremiah, and the Hebrew name is יִרְמְיָהוּ — Yirmeyahu. It is a name connected with the name of the Lord in its latter part, while the first part is connected with the Hebrew root that bears the meaning of raising, appointing, or establishing, according to the proposed linguistic analysis. Therefore there is more than one interpretive formulation of the meaning of the name, among the most common of which is a meaning close to “the Lord raises” or “the Lord establishes,” with linguistic disagreement among scholars in determining the precise derivation. More important theologically is that the name Jeremiah itself is connected with the name of the Lord, which accords with the nature of his ministry, which was not based on his personal opinion, but on the word of God that he carried to a generation that was fiercely resistant.
إرميا هو «إرميا بن حلقيا من الكهنة الذين: Jeremiah is “Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin”; that is, he came from a priestly background and from the region of Anathoth near Jerusalem. This is very important for understanding his character, because he had close knowledge of the system of worship and the temple. Therefore his criticisms of religious corruption came from within a genuine knowledge of worship, not from outside it. Nevertheless, Jeremiah did not become a comfortable prophet for the religious institution; rather, he became a voice confronting the priests, prophets, kings, and people when worship was separated from obedience.
كانت عناثوث مدينة كهنوتية في أرض بنيامين: Anathoth was a priestly city in the land of Benjamin and was geographically connected with the region of Jerusalem. Therefore Jeremiah was close to the religious and political center of the kingdom. This location made him close to the events taking place around the temple, the palace, and the religious leadership, but at the same time he came from an environment outside the immediate center of Jerusalem. It is striking that Anathoth itself will appear later in the book when Jeremiah buys the field there, so that the place is transformed from merely the prophet’s homeland into a symbol of hope in the restoration of the land after the exile.
تتميز دعوة إرميا بأنها جاءت في سن مبكرة،: Jeremiah’s calling is distinguished by the fact that it came at an early age. Therefore he said to the Lord: “Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child.” But God’s answer was decisive: “Do not say, ‘I am a child,’ for you shall go to all to whom I send you, and whatever I command you, you shall speak.” Here we see that the basis of prophecy is not the human being’s natural ability in oratory, but the authority of the divine word that God places in the mouth of his servant. Therefore Jeremiah’s own life became part of his message, for he had to live through suffering, rejection, and loneliness in order to bear witness to the truth with which he was sent.
5. سنة ميلاد إرميا ووفاته: 5. The Year of Jeremiah’s Birth and Death
لا يقدم الكتاب المقدس سنة دقيقة لميلاد إ: The Bible does not provide a precise year for Jeremiah’s birth; therefore the year of his birth or death cannot be determined with certainty. Since his calling came in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah, around 627 B.C. according to traditional chronology, it is likely that he was a young man at that time, and his ministry continued through the reigns of Josiah, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah. As for the end of his life, it is most likely connected with the events that followed the fall of Jerusalem, but the book does not give us a reliable date for his death. Therefore this point must remain within the realm of probability, not certainty.
بدأت خدمة إرميا في السنة الثالثة عشرة من: Jeremiah’s ministry began in the thirteenth year of Josiah and continued through the turbulent years before and after the fall of Jerusalem. This means that Jeremiah lived through the collapse of the southern kingdom almost before his eyes, witnessed the transfer of world power from Assyria to Babylon, and also witnessed the fall of Jerusalem and the temple around 586 B.C. Therefore the book carries prophetic testimony from within the crisis itself, not merely a historical interpretation that came after the events had ended.
كان الخطاب الأساسي موجهًا إلى يهوذا وأور: The primary address was directed to Judah and Jerusalem, but the book also expands to include many kings, peoples, and nations. Jeremiah addresses the people, the king, the priests, the prophets, the elders, the army, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and he also announces judgments on nations such as Egypt, Moab, Ammon, Edom, Philistia, and Babylon. Therefore the book carries a clear national dimension, but at the same time it presents a broader vision affirming that the Lord is not only the God of Judah, but the sovereign Lord of history and of all nations.
كتب إرميا ليعلن أن خطية يهوذا وصلت إلى م: Jeremiah wrote to declare that Judah’s sin had reached a stage that required judgment, and to warn the people against false reliance on the temple, political alliances, or misleading prophecies. He also declared that Babylon would be the instrument of divine discipline, and that resistance to this decree would not lead to salvation but to further ruin. Nevertheless, the aim of the message was not merely to announce death, because Jeremiah also carried the promise that God would gather his people, restore them, and establish a new covenant with them.
يمكن تقسيم سفر إرميا إلى وحدات كبرى تساع: The Book of Jeremiah may be divided into major units that help in understanding its theological and historical movement, while noting that the arrangement of the book is not a simple chronological arrangement in all its parts. Jeremiah 1–25 focuses to a large degree on the calling of the prophet, the sins of Judah, and the warning of judgment, while Jeremiah 26–45 deals with the prophet’s conflicts with the leadership and the people, and the historical events that the crisis led toward collapse. Then Jeremiah 46–51 comes to present prophecies against the nations, while Jeremiah 52 provides a historical conclusion to the fall of Jerusalem and the exile. The major movement of the book may be seen in this form: calling → warning → rejection → judgment → fall → hope → new covenant.
من أعمق عبارات السفر قول الرب لإرميا: «ق: Among the deepest statements in the book is the Lord’s saying to Jeremiah: “Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; and before you came out of the womb, I sanctified you. I appointed you a prophet to the nations.” This text reveals that Jeremiah’s calling did not begin at the moment he stood before the people, but was connected with God’s prior purpose for his ministry. The text does not mean that Jeremiah knew all the details of his life beforehand, but it declares that prophecy is not a personal project begun by a human being, but a divine calling that has its origin in the purpose of God.
11. رؤيتا اللوز والقدر: 11. The Two Visions of the Almond and the Pot
أعطى الرب إرميا رؤيتين في بداية خدمته، ا: The Lord gave Jeremiah two visions at the beginning of his ministry: the first was the rod of an almond tree, and the second was a boiling pot from the north. The vision of the almond is connected with the word of the Lord, meaning that he is watching over his word to perform it, while the tilted pot from the north points to the danger coming upon Jerusalem and Judah. Thus the book begins with a very important teaching: God does not send a warning without execution, because the word spoken by the Lord is transformed in history into an event.
12. إرميا 2 — ترك ينبوع المياه الحية: 12. Jeremiah 2 — Forsaking the Fountain of Living Waters
يعاتب الرب شعبه بقوله: «لأن شعبي عمل شري: The Lord reproaches his people by saying: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, to hew for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns that can hold no water.” The image here is very profound, because the problem was not merely adding a sin to a good life, but replacing the true source of life with human sources that cannot give life. Thus idolatry, political alliances, and confidence in human abilities all become different forms of forsaking God, and the result is that a person possesses a cistern yet remains thirsty.
يستخدم إرميا لغة الزواج ليصف علاقة إسرائ: Jeremiah uses the language of marriage to describe Israel’s relationship with God, prophetic language that has strong roots in Hosea and Isaiah. Sin is not merely a legal violation, but a betrayal of the covenant, as though the people had left a faithful husband and gone after others. This connects Jeremiah directly with the prophetic tradition that sees the relationship between God and his people as a relationship of covenant, love, and faithfulness. Therefore idolatry becomes spiritual betrayal, not merely a ritual error.
14. إرميا 7 — عظة باب الهيكل: 14. Jeremiah 7 — The Sermon at the Temple Gate
من أشهر مقاطع السفر عظة باب الهيكل، حيث: One of the most famous passages in the book is the sermon at the temple gate, where Jeremiah stands at the entrance of the house of the Lord and warns the people against false trust in the building. They were saying: “The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord are these,” as though the existence of the temple guaranteed them protection regardless of what they did. But Jeremiah declares that God wants the amendment of ways and deeds, and that the temple cannot be turned into a fortress protecting a people who insist on disobedience.
15. لماذا كانت عظة الهيكل خطيرة؟: 15. Why Was the Temple Sermon Dangerous?
كان كلام إرميا صادمًا لأن الهيكل كان رمز: Jeremiah’s words were shocking because the temple was a central symbol of God’s presence in Jerusalem. Therefore the announcement of the possibility of its fall was extremely dangerous politically and religiously. But Jeremiah was not diminishing the holiness of the temple; rather, he was defending the true meaning of holiness, because a holy place cannot make a person holy if he continues in evil. This is a very important principle in every age: the building, the rite, or religious affiliation cannot be used as a substitute for repentance and obedience.
في إرميا 18 يأخذ الله النبي إلى بيت الفخ: In Jeremiah 18, God takes the prophet to the potter’s house, and there he sees the potter working the clay in his hand. Then the Lord uses the scene to declare his sovereignty over peoples and nations, and that he can announce judgment and then turn back from it if the people repent, or announce good and then bring judgment if the people turn to evil. This image does not mean that the human being is without responsibility; rather, it affirms at the same time God’s sovereignty and God’s moral response to human repentance and rebellion.
إرميا ليس نبيًا باردًا يعلن الأحكام دون: Jeremiah is not a cold prophet who announces judgments without feeling their pain; rather, he reveals to us an intense inner struggle. He was subjected to beating, imprisonment, mockery, and rejection, and therefore he cried out to God and expressed his bitterness over bearing the message. Nevertheless, he says elsewhere that the word of God was in his heart like a burning fire that he tried to hold in but could not. This is one of the deepest images of prophetic ministry: suffering does not cancel the calling, and the calling does not cancel suffering.
كان أحد أكبر صراعات إرميا مع الأنبياء ال: One of Jeremiah’s greatest conflicts was with the prophets who announced false peace to the people while judgment was drawing near. They said that Jerusalem would not fall and that the yoke of Babylon would be broken quickly, while Jeremiah declared that the people must submit to God’s discipline. Here the difference between the true prophet and the false prophet appears: the true prophet does not measure his message by the extent to which people accept it, but by the extent of his faithfulness to the word of God.
ينتقد الرب الرعاة الذين أهلكوا الشعب وبد: The Lord criticizes the shepherds who destroyed the people and scattered them, then declares that he will raise up good shepherds. After that comes the famous prophecy:
«ها أيام تأتي يقول الرب وأقيم لداود غصنً: “Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch; he shall reign as king and prosper, and shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.”
وهنا يظهر ارتباط إرميا أيضًا بالرجاء الد: Here Jeremiah’s connection with the Davidic hope also appears. Political ruin does not mean that God’s promise to the house of David has ended; rather, God will raise up a king connected with righteousness and justice.
«وهذا هو الاسم الذي يدعونه به: الرب برنا: “And this is the name by which they will call him: The Lord Our Righteousness.”
وهذه عبارة لاهوتية شديدة العمق لأنها ترب: This is an extremely profound theological phrase because it connects the Davidic king with the righteousness that comes from the Lord. In Christian reading, this text became an important part of the study of Christ as the righteous king, while in the original study we must first place the text in the context of Israel’s hope in the just Davidic king, and then see how the New Testament reads it in light of Christ.
21. إرميا 29 — الرسالة إلى المسبيين: 21. Jeremiah 29 — The Letter to the Exiles
من أشهر نصوص السفر الرسالة التي أرسلها إ: Among the most famous texts in the book is the letter that Jeremiah sent to the exiles in Babylon, where he tells them that they will not return after a few days as the false prophets were saying, but that they must build houses, plant, live, and seek the peace of the city to which they had been taken. Then comes the famous promise: “For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says the Lord, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you an end and a hope.” This text must not be separated from its context. It is a promise to a people living under the discipline of exile; therefore hope here does not mean the absence of suffering, but means that suffering is not the final word.
هنا يصل السفر إلى واحدة من أعظم قممه الل: Here the book reaches one of its greatest theological peaks:
«ها أيام تأتي يقول الرب وأقطع مع بيت إسر: “Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.”
«أجعل شريعتي في داخلهم وأكتبها على قلوبه: “I will put my law within them and write it on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.”
المشكلة الأساسية لم تكن نقصًا في وجود ال: The fundamental problem was not a lack of the existence of the law, but the disobedience of the heart. Therefore the solution comes from within: God writes his law on the heart, so the covenant is transformed from merely an external sign into a true inward relationship.
23. غفران الخطية في العهد الجديد: 23. Forgiveness of Sin in the New Covenant
«لأني أصفح عن إثمهم ولا أذكر خطيتهم بعد»: “For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.”
وهنا ترتبط ثلاثة عناصر معًا:: Here three elements are linked together:
وهذه العناصر تصبح أساسية جدًا في اللاهوت: These elements become very foundational in Christian theology of the New Testament. Therefore the author of the Epistle to the Hebrews quoted the text of Jeremiah 31 in his discussion of the new covenant established by Christ.
24. إرميا 32 — شراء الحقل: 24. Jeremiah 32 — The Purchase of the Field
أثناء حصار أورشليم، بينما المدينة تتجه إ: During the siege of Jerusalem, while the city was heading toward collapse, God commands Jeremiah to buy a field in Anathoth. At that moment the matter may seem completely illogical, because the land was about to fall under Babylon’s control. But the purchase of the field becomes an act of prophetic faith, because Jeremiah says that God will restore the people to the land, and the field will be bought again. Thus the field becomes a practical testimony that judgment is temporary with respect to the people of God, but the promise of restoration is eternal in the purpose of God.
تصل القصة التاريخية إلى ذروتها في إرميا: The historical story reaches its climax in Jeremiah 39 and 52, where Jerusalem falls before the Babylonians. Zedekiah’s sons are killed before his eyes, then his eyes are put out and he is taken to Babylon, and the temple, the palace, and the houses of Jerusalem are burned. This is one of the most painful scenes of the Old Testament, because it represents the collapse of the political and religious order under whose shadow the people had lived for centuries.
26. لماذا سمح الله بسقوط أورشليم؟: 26. Why did God allow Jerusalem to fall?
إرميا يرفض تفسير السقوط باعتباره مجرد تف: Jeremiah rejects interpreting the fall as merely Babylon’s military superiority, because for him the fundamental issue is theological before it is political. Babylon was an instrument in God’s hand to discipline Judah because of repeated disobedience, but this does not mean that Babylon itself would remain unaccountable; therefore, Jeremiah’s prophecies against Babylon also appear. Thus, the book maintains an important balance: God uses history to discipline His people, yet He remains the Lord of history and also judges the instrument He used.
الأصحاحات 46–51 تركز على الأمم، ومن بينه: Chapters 46–51 focus on the nations, including:
وهذا يؤكد أن الله ليس إله أورشليم فقط، ب: This confirms that God is not only the God of Jerusalem, but the Lord of all peoples, and that divine justice does not stop at Israel’s borders. Just as Judah could not escape judgment because of its covenant relationship, the nations too are not outside God’s authority.
28. بابل في سفر إرميا: 28. Babylon in the Book of Jeremiah
المفارقة اللاهوتية الكبرى أن بابل التي ا: The great theological paradox is that Babylon, which God used to discipline Judah, itself becomes the object of judgment. This reveals that God does not justify human evil simply because He used it to accomplish a particular purpose. Babylon acted according to its ambition and violence, and therefore judgment comes upon it. This principle gives us a profound picture of God’s sovereignty: God works in history without turning moral evil into good in itself.
إرميا من أكثر شخصيات الكتاب المقدس كشفًا: Jeremiah is one of the biblical figures whose inner feelings are most fully revealed, because the book allows us to see the prophet praying, crying out, weeping, questioning, and complaining. Therefore, some of his texts are sometimes called “Jeremiah’s Confessions,” passages in which the conflict between personal pain and faithfulness to the message appears. This feature makes the book very close to the Psalms, but with an important difference: Jeremiah lives through the crisis while at the same time bearing God’s word to the nation.
30. الأشخاص الرئيسية في السفر: 30. The Main Persons in the Book
النبي الذي حمل رسالة الدينونة والرجاء خل: The prophet who bore the message of judgment and hope during Judah’s fall.
Jeremiah’s father, who was one of the priests in Anathoth.
الملك الذي بدأت في أيامه خدمة إرميا، وشه: The king during whose days Jeremiah’s ministry began, and whose reign witnessed an important religious reform.
ملك ارتبط عهده بمقاومة إرميا واضطهاد رسا: A king whose reign was associated with resistance to Jeremiah and persecution of his message.
The king of Judah who was taken into Babylonian exile.
آخر ملوك يهوذا قبل سقوط أورشليم، وكان في: The last king of Judah before Jerusalem’s fall, who was in a highly unstable political and religious situation.
كاتب إرميا ومساعده، وكان له دور مهم في ك: Jeremiah’s scribe and assistant, who played an important role in writing and recording the prophetic messages.
ملك بابل الذي قاد الإمبراطورية التي حاصر: The king of Babylon who led the empire that besieged and overthrew Jerusalem.
النبي الكاذب الذي أعلن أن نير بابل سينكس: The false prophet who proclaimed that Babylon’s yoke would soon be broken; Jeremiah confronted him with God’s message.
31. أهم الأحداث في السفر: 31. The Major Events in the Book
The vision of the almond branch and the pot.
The conflict with the false prophets.
The purchase of the field of Anathoth.
The exile of the people to Babylon.
The promise of the new covenant.
Prophecies of judgment upon the nations.

الفكرة المركزية للسفر: سفر يوئيل هو سفر: The central idea of the book: The Book of Joel is the book of the day of the Lord, judgment, repentance, mercy, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, the restoration of what affliction destroyed, and finally the judgment of the nations. The book begins with a devastating natural disaster in the form of swarms of locusts that overran the land, but it does not allow the reader to stop at the disaster itself. Rather, it turns it into a spiritual question: What happens when a warning becomes a call to return to God? From there, the book moves from locusts to the day of the Lord, from devastation to fasting and repentance, and from repentance to God's promise: ‘And it shall come to pass afterward that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh,’ and it ends with the proclamation of the Lord's presence among his people and the judgment of the nations. Thus, the book's major movement is: disaster → warning → repentance → mercy → the Holy Spirit → restoration → final judgment → the presence of God.
اسم السفر هو يوئيل، والاسم العبري יוֹאֵל: The name of the book is Joel, and the Hebrew name is יוֹאֵל — Yôʾēl. It consists of the element Yo/Yahu — יוֹ, associated with the name of the Lord, and the element El — אֵל, meaning God. Thus, the name means “the Lord is God” or “Yahweh is God.” This meaning corresponds remarkably well with the book's content, because the crisis facing the people reveals their need to return to acknowledging that the Lord alone is God, and that the disaster is not explained solely through natural circumstances but must lead a person to examine his relationship with God.
يقدم السفر النبي باسم «يوئيل بن فثوئيل»،: The book introduces the prophet as “Joel son of Pethuel,” but it does not provide much information about his personal life, family, or occupation. Therefore, our knowledge of Joel's character comes primarily from the message he carried and from the way he understood the events of his era in light of God's work. This brevity regarding personal information makes the book more focused on God's message than on the prophet's own biography.
3. سنة ميلاد يوئيل ووفاته: 3. Joel's Year of Birth and Death
لا يسجل الكتاب المقدس سنة ميلاد يوئيل أو: The Bible does not record the year of Joel's birth or death, nor does it provide a specific date for his ministry. The book also does not mention the name of the king who ruled Judah when the prophecy was written; therefore, scholars have differed greatly in determining Joel's era. We must therefore be precise: the prophet's date is uncertain, while the content of the prophecy itself is clear, and the various estimates should not be turned into definitive dates.
يختلف الباحثون في تأريخ سفر يوئيل، فهناك: Scholars differ in dating the Book of Joel. Some place it in an early period after the division of the kingdom, while others regard it as one of the postexilic books. The disagreement results from the absence of the king's name and of direct historical references that would help determine the period precisely. Yet regardless of the proposed date, the central axis remains constant: God's people face a crisis, and God uses it as a call to repentance, then announces a greater promise concerning the Spirit, restoration, and the day of the Lord.
يتوجه يوئيل أساسًا إلى يهودا وأورشليم، و: Joel addresses Judah and Jerusalem primarily, speaking to the elders, the priests, and the people, because the crisis affected the land, society, and worship together. The prophet does not treat the crisis as merely an economic problem, although the locusts destroyed the crops; rather, he sees it as an opportunity for the people to gather before God in fasting and prayer. Therefore, the book's true audience is the covenant community that needs to return to the God of the covenant.
يهدف يوئيل إلى تفسير كارثة الجراد باعتبا: Joel aims to interpret the locust disaster as a warning calling the people to awaken and return to God. Then the prophet lifts the people's eyes from the present disaster to “the day of the Lord,” so that they may realize that what is happening before them can be a miniature representation of a greater judgment. But the book does not use fear to end in despair; instead, it opens the way to mercy, repentance, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and the restoration of what the disaster destroyed.
7. تقسيم سفر يوئيل: 7. The Structure of the Book of Joel
The book can be divided into four main sections. Joel 1 describes the locust disaster and the devastation that struck the land; then Joel 2:1–17 moves to the warning of the day of the Lord and the call for the people to fast and repent; Joel 2:18–32 presents God's response through mercy and restoration and the promise of the outpouring of the Spirit; finally, Joel 3 announces the judgment of the nations and the Lord's dwelling in Zion. Thus, the book progresses from an earthly disaster to an eschatological event, from repentance to the Holy Spirit, and from restoration to final judgment.
يفتتح السفر بصورة مروعة لأسراب الجراد ال: The book opens with a terrifying picture of swarms of locusts that consumed what was in the land, leaving the crops, vineyards, and trees in a state of ruin. The locusts were not merely a minor agricultural problem but a disaster threatening food, the economy, and worship, because the absence of crops meant the absence of some of the materials used in offerings and sacrifices. Joel therefore connects the economic crisis with worship and spiritual life, making the disaster a call to return to God.
يبدأ النبي بدعوة الشيوخ والشعب إلى الإصغ: The prophet begins by calling the elders and the people to listen, because what happened is not something that should pass without interpretation. He then asks whether anything like this had occurred in the days of their ancestors, as though he wanted to make the disaster an event that had to be preserved in memory. Here the importance of spiritual memory emerges: the people who learn to interpret their events before God can turn a crisis into a lesson for future generations.
الجراد يظهر في الكتاب المقدس أحيانًا كجز: Locusts sometimes appear in the Bible as part of creation, but they also appear in the context of judgment, as in the plagues of Egypt in the Book of Exodus and in the covenant warnings in the Book of Deuteronomy. Joel's use of locusts therefore evokes an entire biblical memory and causes the reader to ask: Are we facing only a natural disaster, or a divine warning? The prophet does not leave the matter at a natural explanation but uses the disaster to lead the people to return and pray.

This is a very important theological point, because the disaster affected not only the economy but also disrupted the worship system. Thus, the book shows that daily life and worship are not separate spheres, and that the ruin of the land can become a spiritual crisis when the people are unable to offer to God what they had customarily offered.
يدعو النبي الكهنة إلى التقديس والصوم وجم: The prophet calls the priests to consecrate themselves, fast, and gather the people, because the crisis requires a communal response. Repentance here is not merely an individual decision within the heart but a collective movement of the people before God. 29. الحركة الكبرى لإنجيل يوحنا: 29. The Great Movement of John's Gospel
يبدأ إنجيل يوحنا من الأزل، وليس من بيت ل: John's Gospel begins in eternity, not in Bethlehem, declaring that the Word was in the beginning with God and was God, and then became flesh and dwelt among human beings, so that the glory of God appeared in the person of Jesus Christ. From there, Christ begins to reveal himself to the world through signs, teaching, and dialogue: he turns water into wine, gives life, heals the sick, feeds the crowds, opens the eyes of the blind, and raises Lazarus. Each sign leads to the greatest question concerning his identity. Then the “I am” declarations unfold, proclaiming that Christ is the bread of life, the light of the world, the good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, the way, the truth, and the life, and the true vine, while division over his person increases between those who believe in him and those who reject him. After the raising of Lazarus, events move forcefully toward Jerusalem. There Christ enters the hour of his glorification, washes his disciples' feet, and gives them the commandment of love. He then speaks about the Holy Spirit, abiding in him, and going to the Father, and prays for his disciples and for all who will believe in him. Then comes the cross, but John does not present it as a tragic conclusion; rather, he presents it as the hour of glorification and the completion of the work. Christ says, “It is finished,” and gives up his spirit. After this come the empty tomb and the appearances of the risen Christ. إنجيل يوحنا هو الإنجيل الذي يقود القارئ: John's Gospel is the Gospel that leads the reader into the depths of Christ's identity: he is the eternal Word, the Son of God, the light of the world, the bread of life, the good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, and the way, the truth, and the life. From the preexistence of the Word to the incarnation, from the signs to the “I am” declarations, from the raising of Lazarus to the washing of the disciples' feet, and from the final discourses to the cross and resurrection, the entire Gospel moves toward one purpose: that people may know who Jesus is, believe in him, and receive life in his name.
📖 مقدمة سفر يونان: 📖 Introduction to the Book of Jonah
الفكرة المركزية للسفر: سفر يونان ليس مجر: The central idea of the book: The Book of Jonah is not merely a story about a prophet swallowed by a great fish, but a profound book about God's mercy, his sovereignty, the prophet's obedience, humanity's hatred of the enemy, and the breadth of God's purpose of salvation to the nations. The great irony of the book is that the prophet sent to warn a pagan city of judgment was himself the one who needed to learn the meaning of mercy more than the people of the city whom he went to warn. Therefore, the book moves from commission → flight → divine judgment → repentance → mercy → the prophet's anger → the revelation of the breadth of God's heart, and it ends with an open question that God places before the reader: If God has mercy on an entire city, does a person have the right to be angry about God's mercy?
اسم السفر هو يونان — יוֹנָה — Yônāh، ومع: The name of the book is Jonah — יוֹנָה — Yônāh, meaning “dove” in Hebrew. In the Bible, the dove may sometimes be associated with an image of gentleness or a message, but Jonah's name here carries a clear literary irony, because the prophet whose name is associated with the bird does not move freely toward God's call at the beginning of the book, but flees in the opposite direction. Thus, the prophet's name becomes part of the irony on which the book builds its story.
يقدم السفر يونان بأنه «يونان بن أمتاي»،: The book presents Jonah as “Jonah son of Amittai,” and the Second Book of Kings confirms that Jonah was a prophet from Gath-hepher and that he prophesied during the days of Jeroboam II, king of Israel. Therefore, Jonah is not a fictional character detached from biblical history, but appears within the context of the prophets who served in the northern kingdom. This makes the story of Nineveh even more striking, because the Israelite prophet is sent to one of the greatest cities associated with the power of Assyria.
3. سنة ميلاد يونان ووفاته: 3. The Year of Jonah's Birth and Death
لا يسجل الكتاب المقدس سنة ميلاد يونان أو: The Bible does not record the year of Jonah's birth or the year of his death, and therefore they cannot be determined precisely. However, the approximate period of his ministry can be identified through 2 Kings 14:25, where his ministry is associated with the reign of Jeroboam II in the eighth century BC. Historically, this places Jonah in approximately the same period in which the ministries of prophets such as Amos and Hosea appeared.
يجب التمييز بين زمن الأحداث التي يرويها: A distinction must be made between the time of the events narrated by the book and the time when the book was written in its final form, because the date of composition is not settled among scholars. The events themselves take place in the eighth century BC, during the era of the northern kingdom and Assyria. The precise date of the book's composition remains debated, and it is therefore best not to present a single date as an absolute fact.
يحمل السفر رسالة واضحة لشعب الله، وبخاصة: The book carries a clear message for God's people, especially for anyone who believes that God's mercy should be confined to his own group. The story uses pagan Nineveh to expose the attitude of the prophet's and the people's hearts toward the nations. Therefore, the true audience is not only the people of Nineveh, but every reader who knows God's mercy yet may not want that mercy to reach those whom they regard as enemies.
الهدف الأساسي هو الكشف عن رحمة الله وسيا: The primary purpose is to reveal God's mercy and sovereignty over salvation and judgment, while exposing the narrowness of the human heart before God's mercy. Jonah knows that God is merciful, and therefore he flees; the irony is that his correct knowledge of God becomes the reason for his unwillingness to go to Nineveh. Thus, the book reveals that the problem may not be our ignorance of God's attributes, but sometimes that we know his mercy well and yet do not want it to reach others.
7. تقسيم سفر يونان: 7. The Structure of the Book of Jonah
يمكن تقسيم السفر إلى أربعة أقسام واضحة،: The book can be divided into four clear sections, each corresponding approximately to one of the chapters. Chapter one discusses Jonah's commission, his flight, the storm, and his being thrown into the sea. Chapter two then presents Jonah's prayer from inside the great fish. Chapter three describes Jonah's journey to Nineveh, its repentance, and the removal of judgment from it. Finally, chapter four reveals Jonah's anger at God's mercy and places before him the lesson of the plant, the worm, and the wind.

من أكثر المفارقات أهمية أن الوثنيين يظهر: One of the most important ironies is that pagans appear positively in the book in several places. Therefore, the book challenges every narrow conception that makes response to God dependent on national identity rather than faith and repentance.

35. يونان وسيادة الله: 35. Jonah and the Sovereignty of God
من أول السفر إلى آخره، يظهر الله سيدًا ع: From the beginning of the book to its end, God appears as Lord over the sea, the wind, the fish, the plant, the worm, the king, the city, and the prophet. Jonah cannot escape his calling, the sea cannot resist God's command, and Nineveh cannot prevent God's word from reaching it. Thus the great message is that God is sovereign over nature, history, nations, and salvation.
36. يونان ويوم الدينونة: 36. Jonah and the Day of Judgment
يعلن يونان أن نينوى ستنقلب بعد أربعين يو: Jonah declares that Nineveh will be overthrown after forty days, but the prophecy contains within itself an opportunity for repentance. This reveals an important characteristic of prophetic warning: the purpose of warning is not always to carry out punishment, but to prevent it when repentance occurs. Therefore, God's mercy does not conflict with His justice; rather, His mercy is displayed when He uses warning to lead a person to repentance.
سفر يونان يحتل مكانة خاصة جدًا في تعليم: The Book of Jonah occupies a very special place in Christ's teaching, because the Lord Jesus used “the sign of Jonah” in Matthew 12:38–41, Matthew 16:4, and Luke 11:29–32. Christ referred to Jonah and the people of Nineveh, explaining that the people of Nineveh rose in judgment because they repented at Jonah's preaching, whereas before the generation hearing Christ stood One greater than Jonah.
يربط العهد الجديد بين بقاء يونان في جوف: The New Testament connects Jonah's remaining in the belly of the fish with Christ's death and resurrection in its interpretation of “the sign of Jonah.” This does not mean that the Book of Jonah is merely a passing analogy; rather, Christ Himself placed the story within a broader theological framework concerning His death, resurrection, and response to divine revelation. Therefore, Jonah becomes one of the books that helps us understand the passage from death to life in Christian interpretation.
39. يونان والخلاص للأمم: 39. Jonah and Salvation for the Nations
أحد أهم أبعاد السفر هو أن مدينة وثنية بأ: One of the book's most important dimensions is that an entire pagan city comes within the scope of God's mercy when it repents. This accords with the Abrahamic promise that all the families of the earth will be blessed in Abraham, and also with the New Testament's movement toward proclaiming the gospel to the nations. Therefore, the Book of Jonah may be seen as an early picture of the breadth of God's saving purpose beyond Israel's national boundaries.
يحمل السفر تحذيرًا قويًا لكل جماعة دينية: The book carries a powerful warning for every religious community: we may possess the truth and carry the message while still needing our hearts to be changed. Jonah knows God, hears His voice, and proclaims His message, yet he needs to learn mercy. Therefore, the question the book poses to the church is not only, “Do we preach?” but also, “Do we truly want those with whom we differ to be saved?”
41. ماذا نتعلم من البحارة؟: 41. What do we learn from the sailors?
البحارة يعلموننا أن الإنسان يمكن أن يستج: The sailors teach us that a person can respond to God when he sees His authority, even if he did not begin with complete knowledge. They tried to save Jonah before throwing him into the sea; then they feared the LORD and offered vows to Him. This makes them part of the irony the book uses to expose the hardness of the prophet’s heart.
42. ماذا نتعلم من نينوى؟: 42. What do we learn from Nineveh?
تعلمنا نينوى أن الإنذار يمكن أن ينتج توب: Nineveh teaches us that a warning can produce genuine repentance. The city did not say that its history prevented it from changing, nor did it hide behind its military power; instead, it fasted, humbled itself, and turned from its evil. Therefore, in Christ’s teaching, Nineveh became an example of the proper response to divine revelation.
43. ماذا نتعلم من يونان؟: 43. What do we learn from Jonah?
يونان يعلمنا أن الإنسان قد يطيع الله خار: Jonah teaches us that a person may obey God outwardly while his heart remains resistant to His mercy. A servant may succeed in his mission yet fail to share God’s feelings toward people. Therefore, the book is concerned not only with what the servant does, but also with what happens within the servant’s heart during his service.

46. أهم رسالة يقدمها السفر: 46. The Most Important Message Presented by the Book

Therefore, the Book of Jonah reveals that the problem is not always the evil of the outside world; it may also be in the heart of the servant who wants God’s mercy for himself and refuses to let it reach his enemy. كان يشوع من سبط أفرايم، وخدم موسى منذ زم: Joshua was from the tribe of Ephraim and served Moses from an early period. والآن وصلنا إلى نقطة مهمة جدًا في تاريخ: And now we have reached a very important point in the history of the Bible:
لكن السؤال لم يعد: هل يستطيع الله أن يعط: But the question was no longer: Can God give the land?
He had proved that he could.

وهنا تبدأ مرحلة مختلفة تمامًا في تاريخ إ: Here a completely different stage begins in Israel’s history, and the Book of Judges introduces a painful and recurring cycle:

ومن هنا تبدأ واحدة من أكثر المراحل عمقًا: From this point begins one of the most profound stages in the study of human nature and God’s faithfulness.
تُعرف باسم رسالة يهوذا، وهي رسالة قصيرة: The Epistle of Jude is a very short letter, yet it is one of the New Testament’s most forceful books in defending the apostolic faith and warning against corrupt teachers. The name “Jude” is the Arabic form of the Greek name Judas, a common name in the Jewish environment of the first century, and in the New Testament it is associated with more than one person. The author introduces himself as “Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James,” thereby defining his identity through his service to Christ and his relationship to James.
يقدم الكاتب نفسه بقوله: «يَهُوذَا عَبْدُ: The author introduces himself by saying: “Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James” (Jude 1: 1). Christian tradition understands this to refer to Jude, the brother of the Lord Jesus and the brother of James, who appears in the Gospel lists of Christ’s brothers. It is noteworthy that Jude does not introduce himself as “the brother of Jesus,” but as “a servant of Jesus Christ”; this choice carries spiritual and theological significance, since his relationship with Christ had come to rest on faith and submission to him as Lord and Savior, not merely on physical kinship.
كتب يهوذا إلى المؤمنين الذين يصفهم بأنهم: Jude wrote to believers whom he describes as “those who are called, beloved in God the Father and kept for Jesus Christ” (Jude 1: 1). He does not identify a particular group or city, which suggests that the letter had a broader character and could be read in more than one Christian community. These believers needed a serious warning about people who had entered their midst and attempted to turn grace into a license for sin and to deny the lordship of Christ.
كان يهوذا يريد في البداية أن يكتب عن الخ: Jude initially wanted to write about the common salvation, but he found it urgently necessary to warn against the danger of false teaching, saying: “I found it necessary to write appealing to you to contend for the faith that was once for all delivered to the saints” (Jude 1: 3). Therefore, the letter becomes a call to defend the apostolic faith entrusted to the church and not to allow doctrinal and moral corruption to infiltrate the community.
لا يقدم النص تاريخًا صريحًا لكتابته، ولذ: The text does not provide an explicit date of composition, and therefore scholars differ in determining its date. Some scholars associate the letter with the second half of the first century AD, while others place it closer to the end of the first century. A specific year should not be treated as a biblical fact, but as an estimate based on the possible relationship between the letter and the developments faced by the early church.
الموضوع المركزي في رسالة يهوذا هو الدفاع: The central theme of the Epistle of Jude is the defense of the faith and the warning against the spiritual and moral corruption that enters the church under the guise of grace. The letter powerfully combines doctrine and ethics, because Jude sees no possibility of separating sound teaching from holy living. Consequently, deviation from the truth about God leads to deviation in conduct, and the church is called to resist both together.
7. الإيمان المسلَّم مرة للقديسين: 7. The Faith Once Delivered to the Saints
يستخدم يهوذا تعبيرًا بالغ الأهمية: «الإِ: Jude uses a highly significant expression: “the faith that was once for all delivered to the saints” (Jude 1: 3). This does not refer merely to the personal faith of each believer, but to the content of the Christian faith that the church received from the apostles. Therefore, defending the faith does not mean inventing a new doctrine, but preserving and faithfully transmitting the apostolic revelation.
يحذر يهوذا من أشخاص «يَحَوِّلُونَ نِعْمَ: Jude warns about people who “pervert the grace of our God into sensuality” (Jude 1: 4). Here one of the most dangerous distortions confronting the church appears: using God’s grace as an excuse to persist in sin. Biblical grace does not give a person permission to rebel; rather, it frees him from sin’s dominion and leads him into a life of holiness.
يكمل يهوذا وصف هؤلاء بقوله إنهم «يُنْكِر: Jude continues describing these people, saying that they “deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ” (Jude 1: 4). The connection between moral deviation and denial of Christ’s lordship is extremely important: when Christ loses his place as Lord and Master, grace becomes an excuse for justifying conduct that rejects his commands.
10. أمثلة الدينونة في العهد القديم: 10. Examples of Judgment in the Old Testament
يستند يهوذا إلى أحداث تاريخية معروفة في: Jude draws on well-known historical events in Scripture to affirm that God does not overlook rebellion. He mentions the people whom the Lord saved from the land of Egypt and then destroyed because of unbelief, the angels who did not keep their own domain, and Sodom and Gomorrah, which were made an example of judgment. In this way, he uses salvation history itself to warn the church against believing that belonging to God’s community prevents judgment if a person continues in rebellion.
11. الشعب الخارج من مصر: 11. The People Who Came Out of Egypt
يقول يهوذا: «وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أُذَكِّرَكُم: Jude says: “I want to remind you, although you once fully knew it, that Jesus, who saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe” (Jude 1: 5).
وهذا المثال يضع أمام الكنيسة مبدأ واضحًا: This example places a clear principle before the church: previous experience of God’s gifts does not replace continuing faith and obedience. The exodus from Egypt was a great work of salvation, but unbelief led to falling in the wilderness.
يذكر يهوذا أيضًا: «وَالْمَلاَئِكَةَ الَّ: Jude also mentions: “And the angels who did not stay within their own position of authority, but left their proper dwelling, he has kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness until the judgment of the great day” (Jude 1: 6). This example affirms that rebellion against the order established by God is not a trivial matter, and that even spiritual beings are not above God’s authority and judgment.
يقدم يهوذا سدوم وعمورة مثالًا ثالثًا للد: Jude presents Sodom and Gomorrah as a third example of judgment, saying that they “serve as an example by undergoing a punishment of eternal fire” (Jude 1: 7). He connects sexual deviation with rebellion against God’s purpose. He uses the story to affirm that moral sin is not separate from faith, but is part of a person’s attitude toward God’s authority.
يذكر يهوذا حادثة فريدة: «وَمِيكَائِيلُ ر: Jude mentions a unique incident: “But when the archangel Michael, contending with the devil, was disputing about the body of Moses, he did not presume to pronounce a blasphemous judgment, but said, ‘The Lord rebuke you’” (Jude 1: 9). This is one of the letter’s most debated passages because of its connection with a Jewish tradition outside the canonical books of the Old Testament. In Jude’s context, the important point is that Michael himself does not deal with the devil independently of God’s authority, but leaves final judgment to the Lord.
يقارن يهوذا المضللين بثلاث شخصيات من تار: Jude compares the deceivers with three figures from biblical history: Cain, Balaam, and Korah. Cain represents the way of jealousy and hostility; Balaam represents using spiritual matters to obtain gain; and Korah represents rebellion against the authority established by God. Jude brings these images together to reveal that the problem is not merely an intellectual error, but a spirit of rebellion, corruption, lust, and self-interest.
يصف يهوذا هؤلاء بأنهم «صُخُورٌ فِي وَلَا: Jude describes these people as “hidden reefs at your love feasts” (Jude 1: 12). Love feasts were associated with the communal life of the early church, so the presence of these people within them reveals the danger of corruption infiltrating the heart of Christian fellowship. Jude portrays them as dangerous elements that do not nourish the community but threaten it.
يستخدم يهوذا سلسلة قوية من الصور الطبيعي: Jude uses a powerful series of natural images to describe these people: “waterless clouds, swept along by winds; fruitless trees in late autumn, twice dead, uprooted” (Jude 1: 12). The central image is appearance without fruit; a teacher may appear spiritual, but if he bears no fruit of holiness and truth, he is inwardly empty.
يصفهم أيضًا بأنهم «نُجُومٌ تَائِهَةٌ مَح: He also describes them as “wandering stars, for whom the gloom of utter darkness has been reserved forever” (Jude 1: 13). The image points to a loss of direction; instead of leading others along the way of truth, the teacher himself becomes a source of error. This is a grave warning about the danger of spiritual leadership when it becomes detached from truth and holiness.
يستشهد يهوذا بنبوة منسوبة إلى أخنوخ: «هُ: Jude cites a prophecy attributed to Enoch: “Behold, the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones, to execute judgment on all and to convict all the ungodly of all their deeds of ungodliness that they have committed in such an ungodly way, and of all the harsh things that ungodly sinners have spoken against him” (Jude 1: 14–15).
والنقطة المهمة هنا أن يهوذا يستخدم مادة: The important point here is that Jude uses material known in the Jewish environment to affirm a basic biblical truth: God’s judgment on evil. His mere quotation from a literary tradition does not mean that everything contained in that source became part of biblical revelation.
يصف يهوذا المضللين بأنهم «مُتَذَمِّرُونَ: Jude describes the deceivers as “grumblers, malcontents, following their own sinful desires” (Jude 1: 16). This reveals that corrupt teaching ultimately manifests itself in corruption of the heart and conduct; the person who makes his desires the standard of truth will end up reinterpreting the faith to suit his cravings.
ينقل يهوذا المؤمنين من التحذير إلى تذكر: Jude moves believers from warning to remembering apostolic teaching: “But you must remember, beloved, the predictions of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ” (Jude 1: 17). Here once again the centrality of apostolic testimony appears as the criterion for distinguishing sound teaching from distorted teaching.
يذكر يهوذا أن الرسل حذروا من «مُسْتَهْزِ: Jude says that the apostles warned of “scoffers, following their own ungodly passions” (Jude 1: 18). This image connects mocking the truth with the desire to escape God’s authority; a person may mock judgment in order to justify continuing on his own path.
يقول: «هؤُلاَءِ هُمُ الْمُعْتَزِلُونَ بِ: He says: “It is these who cause divisions, worldly people, devoid of the Spirit” (Jude 1: 19). The problem is not merely intellectual disagreement, but the creation of divisions within the body of Christ. False teaching does not remain at the level of ideas; it produces factionalism, division, and the weakening of fellowship.
24. ابنوا أنفسكم على الإيمان: 24. Build Yourselves Up in the Faith
بعد مساحة التحذير الطويلة، ينتقل يهوذا إ: After the lengthy section of warning, Jude turns to the responsibility of believers: “But you, beloved, building yourselves up in your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit” (Jude 1: 20).
وهنا يقدم استراتيجية روحية متكاملة لمواج: Here he presents an integrated spiritual strategy for confronting error: building oneself up in the faith, praying, remaining in God’s love, and waiting for Christ’s mercy.
25. احفظوا أنفسكم في محبة الله: 25. Keep Yourselves in the Love of God
يقول: «وَاحْفَظُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ فِي مَحَ: He says: “Keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ that leads to eternal life” (Jude 1: 21). The letter does not end with fear of deceivers, but by returning the believer to God’s love and the hope of eternal life.
يقول يهوذا: «وَارْحَمُوا بَعْضًا مُمَيِّ: Jude says: “And have mercy on those who doubt” (Jude 1: 22). This is very important: rejecting error does not mean rejecting every person who is struggling with uncertainty. There is a difference between the deliberate deceiver and the person who doubts or needs instruction and mercy. Therefore, the church needs discernment, not blind reactions.
يقول: «وَخَلِّصُوا الْبَعْضَ مُخْتَطِفِي: He says: “Save others by snatching them out of the fire; to others show mercy with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh” (Jude 1: 23). Here the evangelistic and pastoral dimension of the letter appears: the church does not merely defend itself, but seeks to rescue those affected by error while maintaining holiness and avoiding participation in sin.
28. التمييز بين الإنسان والخطية: 28. Distinguishing Between the Person and the Sin
تكشف هذه الفقرة توازنًا بالغ الأهمية؛ فا: This passage reveals a profoundly important balance: the church can show mercy to a person and seek to rescue him, while at the same time rejecting sin and false teaching. This establishes an important pastoral principle: love does not mean participating in sin, and discernment does not mean abandoning mercy.
بعد دعوة المؤمنين إلى حفظ أنفسهم، ينتهي: After calling believers to keep themselves, Jude concludes by declaring God’s preserving power: “Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling, and to present you faultless before His glory with exceeding joy” (Jude 1: 24). Thus, the believer’s confidence does not rest only on his own ability, but on God’s ability to preserve and establish.
يختم يهوذا بتسبيح عظيم: «لِلإِلهِ الْحَك: Jude concludes with a great doxology: “To the only wise God our Savior, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen” (Jude 1: 25). After the warning against error and judgment, the book ends with the believer’s eyes fixed on God, not on the danger; because God is the Savior, the Preserver, and the One who possesses final authority.
رسالة يهوذا غنية جدًا بالخلفية الكتابية؛: The Epistle of Jude is very rich in biblical background; it evokes the exodus from Egypt, the rebellion of the people in the wilderness, Sodom and Gomorrah, Cain, Balaam, and Korah, and it is grounded in the concepts of judgment, holiness, and obedience that fill the books of the Old Testament. Thus Jude places the church in continuity with the history of God’s people, showing that the God who judged rebellion in the Old Testament is the same God who demands holiness and steadfastness from the church.
يضع يهوذا الإيمان المسلَّم مرة للقديسين: Jude places the faith once delivered to the saints at the heart of the epistle, then asks believers to remember the words of the apostles. Therefore, the church’s authority in confronting deceptive teaching does not rest on personal opinions or changing cultural trends, but on the apostolic revelation that the church received. This gives the epistle special importance in the matter of preserving doctrine.
33. رسالة يهوذا والرسالة الثانية لبطرس: 33. The Epistle of Jude and the Second Epistle of Peter
توجد تشابهات واضحة بين يهوذا و2 بطرس، خص: There are clear similarities between Jude and 2 Peter, especially in the warning against false teachers, the use of examples of judgment, the description of moral corruption, and the warning against scoffing in the last days. Many scholars hold that there is a literary or traditional relationship between the two epistles, but defining the precise nature of that relationship remains a matter of debate. What is important theologically is that the two epistles testify to the early church’s concern over teaching that uses Christianity to justify corruption.
34. الحركة الكبرى للرسالة: 34. The Major Movement of the Epistle
تبدأ الرسالة بتحية تركز على الدعوة والتق: The epistle begins with a greeting focused on calling, sanctification, and preservation, then quickly moves to the necessity of contending for the faith delivered to the saints. After that, Jude exposes the entry of corrupt people into the community, and demonstrates from the history of the exodus, the angels, and Sodom and Gomorrah the certainty of God’s judgment. He then uses the images of Cain, Balaam, Korah, clouds without water, trees without fruit, and wandering stars to reveal the nature of the deceivers. After that, he returns to the teaching of the apostles and calls believers to build themselves up on the faith, to pray, to remain steadfast in God’s love, and to wait for the mercy of Christ, while practicing mercy and rescue toward those who have been affected by error. In the end, he lifts the church’s gaze from the danger to God, who is able to keep it from falling and to present it before His glory without blemish.
تكشف رسالة يهوذا أن حفظ الإيمان وحفظ الق: The Epistle of Jude reveals that preserving the faith and preserving holiness are inseparable; apostolic faith is not a doctrinal system without moral effect, grace is not a permit for sin, and love is not acceptance of error. The church is called to defend the truth, practice discernment, and warn against corrupt teaching, while at the same time showing mercy to the doubtful and seeking to rescue those who have fallen under the influence of error. All of this ultimately takes place under the authority of God, who is able to preserve His people.
رسالة يهوذا هي رسالة الدفاع عن الإيمان و: The Epistle of Jude is the epistle of defending the faith amid the infiltration of corruption into the Christian community. Jude begins by declaring believers to be called, sanctified, and preserved in Christ, then reveals the necessity of contending for the faith once delivered to the saints, because people had entered the church and turned the grace of God into a license for sin and denied the sovereignty of the Lord Jesus Christ. He draws on the history of Scripture to affirm that God is not lenient toward unbelief, rebellion, and corruption, and he evokes the examples of Israel in the wilderness, the angels, Sodom and Gomorrah, Cain, Balaam, and Korah. He then portrays the deceivers as fruitless, wandering, and dangerous to the community of believers. Yet he does not leave the church in a passive defensive posture, but calls it to build itself up on the faith, to pray in the Holy Spirit, to remain steadfast in the love of God, and to wait for the mercy of Christ, while exercising mercy, discernment, and rescue toward those who have fallen within the sphere of error. The epistle ends with praise to God, who is able to keep believers from stumbling and to present them before His glory without blemish. Thus the epistle moves from danger to discernment, from discernment to steadfastness, from steadfastness to divine preservation, and from preservation to glory to God.

الاسم العبري لسفر القضاة هو שֹׁפְטִים —: The Hebrew name for the Book of Judges is שֹׁפְטִים — Shoftim, and its meaning is “Judges.” It is the plural of the word שֹׁפֵט — Shofet, that is, the judge, ruler, or holder of judicial and leadership authority. But the word “judge” in the biblical concept is not limited to a person who sits to adjudicate disputes, because the judges who appear in this book were generally leaders whom God raised up to save Israel from oppression and to lead the people in a time of crisis.
والاسم نفسه يكشف طبيعة المرحلة التاريخية: The name itself reveals the nature of the historical period; Israel did not have a central king ruling the whole nation, and leadership was not stabilized in a royal dynasty. Rather, the Lord would raise up a leader in a time of crisis, and then that leader’s mission would end. For this reason, the book becomes a record of a transitional period between the possession of the land in Joshua and the establishment of the monarchy in Samuel.
وتظهر في نهاية السفر العبارة التي تلخص ا: At the end of the book appears the phrase that summarizes the political and spiritual condition:
«في تلك الأيام لم يكن ملك في إسرائيل. كا: “In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes.”
وهذه العبارة ليست مجرد ملاحظة سياسية، بل: This phrase is not merely a political observation, but a theological key to the whole book.
لا يذكر السفر اسم كاتبه بصورة مباشرة، ول: The book does not mention the name of its author directly, and therefore no specific person can be identified with certainty as having written all its materials.
يربط التقليد اليهودي القديم السفر بصموئي: Ancient Jewish tradition connects the book with Samuel the prophet, while many scholars hold that the book passed through stages of collection and editing, and that its present form is connected with the historical and interpretive traditions that appeared within the framework of what is called the Deuteronomistic History.
والأهم بالنسبة للدراسة الكتابية هو أن ال: What is most important for biblical study is that the book presents history bearing a clear theological interpretation of events. It does not merely narrate Israel’s victories and defeats, but connects each stage of them with the people’s relationship to the Lord.
3. زمن أحداث السفر: 3. The Time of the Events of the Book
تبدأ أحداث القضاة بعد موت يشوع، عندما أص: The events of Judges begin after the death of Joshua, when a large part of the land had come under Israel’s control, but peoples and regions remained that had not been fully subdued.
وهذه النقطة مهمة جدًا، لأن سفر يشوع انته: This point is very important, because the Book of Joshua ended with the declaration of the possession of the land, while Judges reveals that the possession was neither complete nor final in practical terms.
وهكذا يعيش إسرائيل في وضع جديد: لديه الأ: Thus Israel lives in a new situation: it has the land, but it is surrounded by pagan peoples, and if it mixes with them and adopts their forms of worship, the spiritual crisis begins.
كُتب السفر للأمة الإسرائيلية، وبصورة خاص: The book was written for the Israelite nation, and especially for the generations that came after the generation of Joshua.

الغرض الأساسي من السفر هو تفسير لماذا تك: The basic purpose of the book is to explain why Israel’s defeats were repeated despite the fact that God had given it the land.

يبدأ السفر بتسجيل بقاء الكنعانيين في منا: The book begins by recording the continued presence of the Canaanites in many regions.
