وهذا يجعل الملوك الأول والثاني من أهم ال: This makes First and Second Kings among the most important books for understanding the transition from the glory of the kingdom → its division → its corruption → its fall → the captivity → waiting for the promised King.
الفكرة المركزية للسفر: مراثي إرميا هو سف: The central idea of the book: Lamentations is the book of sacred tears over the ruin of Jerusalem and the fall of the Temple, but at the same time it is the book of hope born from the heart of tragedy. The author does not stand before the ruins as a cold historian recording the number of the dead and the extent of the destruction; rather, he stands as a prophet who sees that the catastrophe carries a profound spiritual dimension because it is the direct result of the people's rebellion against God and their continual rejection of his word. Nevertheless, the book does not allow the ruins to have the final word, because amid the darkness one of the greatest statements of hope in the Old Testament appears: “It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Thus the book moves from tears to confession, from confession to hope, and from hope to supplication before God for mercy and restoration.
الاسم العربي هو مراثي إرميا، بينما يعرف: The Arabic name is Lamentations of Jeremiah, while in the Hebrew tradition the book is known as אֵיכָה — ’Eikhah, a word that means approximately “How?”. This opening word expresses remarkably the condition of a person standing before a catastrophe beyond his ability to comprehend, asking how the great city became a ruin and how Jerusalem, once full of people, came to sit alone. The name Lamentations in Arabic describes the literary nature of the book, because it consists of sad poems mourning the city, the people, and the Temple, combining grief, confession of sin, and supplication to God.
لا يذكر سفر المراثي اسم الكاتب داخل نصه: The book of Lamentations does not directly mention the author's name within its text, but ancient Jewish and Christian tradition attributed it to the prophet Jeremiah. This tradition is strongly connected to the historical setting described by the book, because Jeremiah was present during the fall of Jerusalem and witnessed the warnings that preceded the catastrophe, and he was also one of the prophets who wept most over the city and the people. Nevertheless, in academic study we should distinguish between the traditional attribution to Jeremiah and the fact that the book itself does not place the author's name on its pages. Therefore, it may be said that ancient tradition attributes it to Jeremiah, while the text itself leaves the question of authorship open.
3. لماذا نُسب السفر إلى إرميا؟: 3. Why was the book attributed to Jeremiah?
السبب الرئيسي هو التشابه الكبير بين مراث: The main reason is the strong similarity between Lamentations and the prophetic spirit found in the book of Jeremiah, especially in its depiction of Jerusalem's fall as the result of divine judgment rather than merely a military defeat. Jeremiah also lived through approximately the same events described by the book, so it was natural for tradition to attribute these laments to the prophet who spent years warning the people of the catastrophe and then saw the catastrophe take place before his eyes. There is also a similarity in vocabulary and themes between the two books, especially the themes of sin, judgment, famine, captivity, the Temple, and hope in God's mercy.
يرتبط السفر تاريخيًا بسقوط أورشليم أمام: The book is historically connected with the fall of Jerusalem to the Babylonians in approximately 586 B.C., and therefore the poems probably originated close to the time of the catastrophe. The language of the book suggests that the author is reflecting on a recent devastation, not on a distant event that had become merely a historical memory. This makes Lamentations a highly significant literary and spiritual document for understanding the shock that struck Judah after the fall of the city and the Temple, while requiring a distinction between the time of the events and the precise date of the final composition, which cannot be determined with certainty.
السفر موجه بصورة أساسية إلى جماعة عاشت ك: The book is addressed primarily to a community that experienced the catastrophe of Jerusalem's fall, but at the same time it speaks to every person who passes through a period of collapse, loss, and discipline. It does not merely provide political information about Babylon; it seeks to interpret the tragedy before God. Therefore, the reader finds himself facing a question deeper than “What happened?”, namely, “Why did it happen?”. From this perspective, the book becomes an address to a people who lost their city, sanctuary, and stability, but who above all need to understand how they can return to God amid the ruins.
الهدف الأساسي هو رثاء أورشليم بعد سقوطها: The primary purpose is to lament Jerusalem after its fall, while acknowledging that this ruin came as a result of the people's continual disobedience. But the author does not merely record the grief; he places the pain before God in explicit prayer, as though saying that true faith does not mean denying pain or pretending that everything is fine. Therefore, the book allows a person to weep, cry out, ask questions, and confess, while at the same time holding fast to the truth that God's mercy has not ended. This is a profoundly important spiritual point: faith does not eliminate grief; it gives grief a place before God.
7. نوع السفر الأدبي: 7. The literary genre of the book
مراثي إرميا من الشعر العبري المرثوي، وقد: Lamentations is Hebrew lament poetry, and the author used a highly precise poetic structure. Most of the poems are connected to the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, so that each verse or section begins with successive letters of the alphabet in a number of the poems, while the book reaches a more extensive structure in chapter three. This organized structure is important because it shows that the author is not merely experiencing psychological chaos; he is attempting to place the tragedy within a disciplined poetic order, as though faith were trying to find order amid a world that had become, for the entire people, ruin and chaos.
يتكون السفر من خمسة أصحاحات، ويمكن التعا: The book consists of five chapters, and each chapter may be treated as an independent poetic lament connected to the other laments. Chapter one portrays Jerusalem as a lonely and humiliated city after having been great among the nations, while chapter two focuses more strongly on God's anger and judgment against the city. Chapter three then presents the deepest transition from pain to hope, after which chapter four depicts the horror of famine and ruin and the fall of the leadership, while chapter five ends with a communal prayer asking God to bring the people back to himself and restore the broken relationship.
يفتتح السفر بصورة مؤلمة للغاية:: The book opens with an extremely painful image:
«كيف جلست وحدها المدينة الكثيرة الشعب! ك: “How lonely sits the city that was full of people! How like a widow has she become, she who was great among the nations! She who was a princess among the provinces has become a forced laborer!”
الصورة الأدبية هنا قوية جدًا، لأن المدين: The literary image here is very powerful, because the city that was a political and religious center has become like a widow, having lost protection, glory, and status. This is not merely an image of urban ruin, but of the collapse of the identity of an entire people, because Jerusalem was not merely an ordinary city for Israel; it was the center of kingship, the Temple, worship, and national memory.
10. لماذا استخدم السفر صورة الأرملة؟: 10. Why did the book use the image of a widow?
صورة الأرملة تعبر عن الوحدة والفقدان وال: The image of a widow expresses isolation, loss, and social vulnerability in the ancient world, and therefore it was highly appropriate for describing Jerusalem after its fall. The city that once welcomed the nations became without a protector, and the city that once took pride in its status came to sit in mourning. This style reveals that the author does not want to make Jerusalem merely a destroyed building; he wants the reader to feel that the city itself has become like a broken person in need of comfort.
«قد أخطأت أورشليم خطية، من أجل ذلك صارت: “Jerusalem has grievously sinned; therefore she has become unclean.”
وهنا تظهر نقطة أساسية في تفسير السفر: ال: Here a fundamental point in interpreting the book appears: in the prophetic vision, the ruin is not a meaningless accident but the result of a long history of disobedience. The author does not place all the blame on Babylon, nor does he say that the people were innocent victims; he acknowledges that Judah rejected God's word and turned away from the covenant. Nevertheless, acknowledging sin does not erase the fact that the resulting pain was extremely severe. Thus divine justice and divine mercy come together in the book.
12. مراثي 2 — غضب الرب: 12. Lamentations 2 — The Anger of the LORD
الأصحاح الثاني أكثر حدة في وصف الدينونة،: Chapter two is more intense in its description of judgment, because it focuses on what the LORD did to Jerusalem within the framework of divine judgment. The Temple was no longer able to protect the city, the king had lost his authority, the prophets no longer had a comforting vision, and the people suffered famine and death. This picture takes us back to the warnings of the earlier prophets, because what once appeared to be merely a prophetic warning had now become a visible historical reality.
سقوط الهيكل يمثل صدمة روحية هائلة، لأن ا: The fall of the Temple represents an enormous spiritual shock, because the Temple was the center of worship and the symbolic presence of God among the covenant people. But Lamentations makes clear that the Temple's presence was not an automatic guarantee that the city would remain regardless of its sins, an idea that strongly agrees with Jeremiah's sermon at the Temple gate. Thus it becomes clear that God does not allow sacred symbols to become a substitute for sacred obedience, and attachment to a place without repentance cannot prevent judgment.
من أكثر الصور قسوة في السفر وصف الجوع ال: Among the most horrific images in the book is the description of the famine that struck the city during and after the siege, until the mothers became unable to feed their children. These images are not literary exaggerations without foundation; they reflect the nature of ancient siege warfare, when the city gates were closed and food was prevented from entering. Therefore, Lamentations bears painful witness to the human cost of war, siege, and political collapse, and enables the reader to realize that the word “captivity” did not mean merely geographic relocation but a genuine human tragedy.
15. مراثي 3 — أنا الرجل الذي رأى مذلة: 15. Lamentations 3 — I Am the Man Who Has Seen Affliction
يبدأ الأصحاح الثالث بصوت شخصي:: Chapter three begins with a personal voice:
“I am the man who has seen affliction because of the rod of his wrath.”
وهنا يتحول السفر من الحديث عن المدينة إل: Here the book shifts from speaking about the city to the experience of the individual human being. The speaker appears to bear in his body and soul the effects of the catastrophe that befell the nation, and therefore his voice becomes representative of the voice of the entire people. Nevertheless, this very chapter will become the place where the greatest light of hope in the whole book shines forth.
16. «هذا أذكره فيرجى»: 16. “This I recall to my mind; therefore I have hope”
وسط سلسلة طويلة من الألم يقول:: Amid a long series of sufferings, he says:
«هذا أرده في قلبي من أجل ذلك أرجو: إنه م: “This I recall to my mind, therefore I have hope: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, says my soul; therefore I will hope in him.”
هذه الكلمات من أعظم نصوص الرجاء في العهد: These words are among the greatest texts of hope in the Old Testament, because they do not deny reality or pretend that Jerusalem did not fall. The author sees the ruins with his own eyes, but he declares that God's mercy did not fall with the city. This is the difference between human optimism and biblical hope: optimism says that things will improve, whereas hope says that God is faithful even when circumstances are dark.
هذه العبارة قصيرة لكنها تحمل لاهوتًا عظي: This statement is short, but it carries profound theology:
«نصيبي هو الرب قالت نفسي، من أجل ذلك أرج: “The LORD is my portion, says my soul; therefore I will hope in him.”
لكن الكاتب يصل إلى اكتشاف روحي عميق: إذا: But the author reaches a profound spiritual discovery: if everything can be lost, God himself remains the portion. This idea connects Lamentations with the Psalms, especially the texts that speak of God as one's portion, sufficiency, and refuge.
18. «جيد أن ينتظر الإنسان»: 18. “It is good that a person should wait”
«جيد أن ينتظر الإنسان ويتوقع بسكوت خلاص: “It is good that a person should wait and quietly expect the salvation of the LORD.”
هذه ليست دعوة إلى الاستسلام السلبي، بل إ: This is not a call to passive surrender, but to trust in God's timing after human ability to control events has come to an end. The city had fallen, the king was gone, and the people had been taken captive; there was no longer any quick political solution. Therefore, the author learns that waiting can be an act of faith when a person is unable to change circumstances by his own means.
19. مراثي 4 — الذهب الذي تغير: 19. Lamentations 4 — The Gold That Has Changed
يستخدم الأصحاح الرابع صورًا مأساوية ليصف: Chapter four uses tragic images to describe the change in Jerusalem's condition, so that even the gold seems to have lost its value, and the children who were like precious gold have become abandoned to famine and ruin. This transformation reveals how quickly civilizations collapse when the structure that sustains them breaks down. A city that appeared extremely strong can become a place of death within a short time. Thus the book places before humanity a historical and spiritual truth: earthly glory is not guaranteed forever.
20. سقوط الملوك والقادة: 20. The fall of the kings and leaders
لم يقتصر الخراب على عامة الشعب، بل أصاب: The ruin did not affect only the common people; it also struck the leadership, because the kings, leaders, priests, and prophets were all part of the crisis. This is an important point in the book, because the author does not offer an interpretation that makes one class responsible for everything; instead, he portrays the collapse of an entire society. When the head becomes corrupt and the people continue in disobedience, the collapse becomes comprehensive. Therefore, judgment in Lamentations is connected with both collective and personal responsibility.
21. مراثي 5 — صلاة الشعب: 21. Lamentations 5 — The Prayer of the People
يختلف الأصحاح الخامس عن القصائد السابقة: Chapter five differs from the preceding poems in its tone, because it appears as a communal prayer before God. The people begin with a direct request: “Remember, O LORD, what has happened to us; look and see our disgrace.” Here the people do not speak about God as though he were absent; they address him directly. This means that the relationship has not ended despite the judgment. The cry itself becomes a sign that the people still know that the final path is not to Babylon but to God.
من أعظم الحقائق في خاتمة السفر:: Among the greatest truths in the conclusion of the book is:
«أنت يا رب إلى الأبد تجلس. كرسيك إلى دور: “You, O LORD, reign forever; your throne endures from generation to generation.”
المدينة سقطت، والملك الأرضي انتهى، والهي: The city fell, the earthly king came to an end, and the Temple was destroyed, but God's throne did not fall. This comparison is one of the most important theological messages in the book, because history can destroy human institutions, but God's sovereignty does not depend on the survival of any human institution. Therefore, amid the ruins the people find a foundation for hope: the earthly kingdom has ended, but God's reign remains.
ينتهي السفر بصيحة مؤلمة:: The book ends with a painful cry:
«لماذا تنسانا إلى الأبد؟ تتركنا طول الأي: “Why do you forget us forever? Why do you forsake us for so many days?”
هذه ليست علامة على فقدان الإيمان، بل هي: This is not a sign of loss of faith, but the prayer of a wounded person who still addresses God. The author does not conceal the pain behind artificial religious language, nor does he try to explain everything easily; rather, he allows the question to remain within the prayer. This teaches us that the Bible is not afraid of the questions of the broken person, while at the same time it does not turn the question into a denial of God's existence.
24. أهم الأحداث التي يعرضها السفر: 24. The most important events presented by the book
السفر لا يقدم أحداثًا متسلسلة مثل سفر ال: The book does not present sequential events like the book of Kings; instead, it offers poetic reflection on real historical events. The central event is the siege and fall of Jerusalem, the destruction of the Temple, and the people's captivity in Babylon, after which the poems explain the pain left by these events. Therefore, the most important “event” in the book is Jerusalem's transformation from a great city into a destroyed city, and then the transformation of this ruin into a space for confession, repentance, and hope.
لا يقدم السفر شخصيات كثيرة بالاسم، لأن ا: The book does not present many named figures, because the city itself almost becomes the main character in the poems. Jeremiah is the figure associated with the book's traditional authorship, while the people appear as a collective character suffering judgment and crying out to God. Jerusalem appears metaphorically as a woman or widow, while the LORD appears simultaneously as judge, king, and possessor of mercy. Babylon appears indirectly as the power that carried out the historical fall.
من أجمل خصائص السفر أن أورشليم ليست مجرد: One of the most beautiful features of the book is that Jerusalem is not merely a geographical location, but becomes a character who speaks, grieves, and weeps. It is the city that was filled with people and then became solitary; the city that was honored and then became humiliated; and the city that was the center of worship and then had its temple become a ruin. In this way, the writer makes the reader see not only the stones, but feel the wound of the city as though it were the wound of a living person.
27. العلاقة بين مراثي إرميا وسفر إرميا: 27. The Relationship between Lamentations of Jeremiah and the Book of Jeremiah
هناك ارتباط موضوعي واضح بين السفرين، لأن: There is a clear thematic connection between the two books, because Jeremiah warns of judgment, while Lamentations reflects on the judgment after it has occurred. In the Book of Jeremiah, we hear the prophet telling the people that Jerusalem will fall if it does not repent; in Lamentations, we see the city after its fall and hear its voice as it weeps. Thus, the two books can be read together as though they are two stages of the prophetic message: the warning before the fall, and the lament after the fall.
28. العلاقة بين المراثي والتثنية: 28. The Relationship between Lamentations and Deuteronomy
سفر التثنية أعلن منذ وقت مبكر أن العصيان: The Book of Deuteronomy had declared from an early point that persistent disobedience could lead to the loss of the land and to exile, and Lamentations of Jeremiah presents the tragic historical picture of what happened when the warning was fulfilled. Therefore, Lamentations does not arise from a theological vacuum, but stands within the framework of covenant, blessing, and curse. The writer sees that the fall of Jerusalem confirms the seriousness of the word of God, yet at the same time he holds fast to the truth that God’s faithfulness does not end with judgment.
29. العلاقة مع سفر إشعياء: 29. The Relationship with the Book of Isaiah
إشعياء تحدث عن قداسة الله والدينونة والر: Isaiah spoke about the holiness of God, judgment, and hope, and Lamentations of Jeremiah lives through the painful historical side of this message. Isaiah saw that God could judge Jerusalem, but he also promised the remnant and salvation, whereas Lamentations comes to say that judgment has in fact become a reality; nevertheless, mercy still exists. Thus, the two books meet in the truth that judgment is not the cancellation of God’s promise, but part of the history of salvation that leads to hope.
يشترك مراثي إرميا مع المزامير في لغة:: Lamentations of Jeremiah shares with the Psalms the language of:
لكن المزامير غالبًا تتحدث عن تجربة فردية: But the Psalms often speak about a variety of individual or communal experiences, whereas Lamentations is especially connected with a major national catastrophe. Therefore, the book may be regarded as a kind of sorrowful communal psalm that emerged from the experience of the fall of Jerusalem.
سقوط أورشليم يعلن أن قداسة الله لا تسمح: The fall of Jerusalem declares that the holiness of God does not allow sin to continue without judgment, but judgment does not mean that God has ceased to show mercy or has forgotten his covenant; even amid ruin, a person can say, “The Lord is my portion,” and wait for new mercy every morning.
32. ماذا يشير لنا سفر المراثي؟: 32. What Does the Book of Lamentations Point Out to Us?
يشير إلى أن الله لا يطلب من الإنسان أن ي: It points out that God does not ask human beings to hide their pain, because the Bible itself allows tears, cries, and questions. It points out that true worship includes confession of sin, because the people do not merely complain about the pain, but confess that disobedience lay behind the judgment. It also points out that hope does not depend on circumstances, because the greatest statements of hope in the book came from the heart of a ruined city. Finally, it teaches us that God’s mercy can become clearest when all human sources of reliance have come to an end.
33. المسيح في ضوء سفر المراثي: 33. Christ in Light of the Book of Lamentations
لا يقدم السفر نبوة مسيانية مباشرة بنفس و: The book does not present a direct messianic prophecy with the same clarity as Isaiah 53 or Isaiah 9, but it does provide an important theological background for understanding the work of Christ. Humanity lives under the weight of sin and judgment, and needs mercy, forgiveness, and a covenant that restores the broken relationship with God. In Christ we find the fulfillment of this hope, because the New Testament declares the forgiveness of sins and the restoration of the relationship with God through the redemptive work of Christ.
34. العهد الجديد ومراثي إرميا: 34. The New Testament and Lamentations of Jeremiah
لا توجد في العهد الجديد اقتباسات طويلة م: There are no long quotations from the book in the New Testament with the same density as the quotations from Isaiah or the Psalms, but its themes clearly intersect with the proclamation of the gospel. Grief over Jerusalem appears in a moving way in Christ’s weeping over the city, while in the New Testament we also find a movement from the earthly Jerusalem to the heavenly Jerusalem. Thus, a theological line can be seen that begins with a city broken because of sin and ultimately moves toward a new city in which there is no death, sorrow, crying, or pain.
35. أهم المفاهيم في السفر: 35. The Most Important Concepts in the Book
هذه الكلمات لا تمثل موضوعات منفصلة، بل ت: These words do not represent separate themes, but form the course of the whole book from beginning to end; therefore, understanding the relationship among them is more important than studying each word individually.
36. الحركة الكبرى للسفر: 36. The Major Movement of the Book

«مراثي إرميا هو صوت الإيمان وهو يبكي؛ فه: “Lamentations of Jeremiah is the voice of faith as it weeps; it does not deny that Jerusalem fell because of its sin, nor does it try to soften the horror of hunger, ruin, and exile, but it also refuses to allow the catastrophe to be the end of the story. الاسم العبري لسفر اللاويين هو וַיִּקְרָא: The Hebrew name of the Book of Leviticus is וַיִּקְרָא — Vayyiqrā, and its meaning is “And he called,” which is the first word with which the book begins: “And the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting, saying.” This beginning is highly important because it reveals that the book does not begin with a human initiative or with a proposal from the priests, but begins with God’s call to Moses from within the tabernacle, as though the whole message proceeds from the presence of God himself.
أما الاسم المتداول في اللغات الغربية فهو: As for the name commonly used in Western languages, it is Leviticus, which is derived from the Greek name connected with the Levites, and especially with matters related to worship, priesthood, sacrifices, and purity. But the name “Leviticus” may lead the reader to think that the book is intended for the Levites alone, whereas the truth is that the book addresses the whole congregation of Israel and sets before it the order of life in the presence of God. Therefore, its subject is much broader than the function of the tribe of Levi.
والفكرة الأساسية التي يجمع حولها السفر ك: The central idea around which the book gathers all its themes is this: How can a sinful people live in the midst of the presence of a holy God? Exodus ended with the glory of the Lord dwelling in the tent of meeting, and now Leviticus comes to explain how the people are to deal with this presence, how worship is to take place, how sacrifice is to function, how the priest is to work, how the concept of impurity is to be addressed, and how the people are to live in holiness.
ينسب التقليد اليهودي والمسيحي سفر اللاوي: Jewish and Christian tradition attribute the Book of Leviticus to Moses, the same tradition that attributes the Pentateuch to him. Moses appears in the book as the mediator who receives the word of the Lord and conveys it to the congregation and the priests, and the first chapters begin with phrases confirming that the Lord spoke to Moses and gave him the instructions concerning sacrifices, worship, and holiness.
واسم موسى في العبرية هو מֹשֶׁה — Mosheh،: The name Moses in Hebrew is מֹשֶׁה — Mosheh, and in the Book of Exodus it is connected with the idea of his being drawn out of the water, when Pharaoh’s daughter said, “Because I drew him out of the water.” Although scholars discuss the linguistic origin of the name, the biblical narrative itself gives the name an explanation connected with the story of Moses’ rescue, an explanation that became part of the biblical identity of the character.
ولا يقدم الكتاب تاريخًا تقويميًا دقيقًا: The Bible does not provide a precise calendar date for Moses’ birth or death, and therefore it is not correct to assign a specific year without stating that it is only an estimate. The fixed piece of information is that he died at the age of 120 according to Deuteronomy 34:7, and the Books of Exodus and Leviticus place his ministry in the wilderness period after the exodus from Egypt and before entry into the promised land.
3. لمن كُتب سفر اللاويين؟: 3. For Whom Was the Book of Leviticus Written?
وُجه السفر إلى جماعة إسرائيل التي أصبحت: The book was directed to the congregation of Israel, which had now become connected with the tabernacle, the covenant, and worship; therefore, it is not a book for priests only. It is true that the priests and Levites occupy an important place in its content, but the laws concerning holiness, purity, festivals, food, social relationships, vows, and other matters touch the life of the whole congregation.
ويمكن النظر إلى السفر باعتباره دليلًا لش: The book may be viewed as a guide for a people who had come out of Egypt and been freed from Pharaoh’s authority, but who now stood before an entirely different authority: the authority of the holy God. Exodus gave Israel freedom from slavery, but Leviticus explains that biblical freedom does not mean that a person does whatever he wishes, but that he lives in a right relationship with the God who redeemed him.
إذا كان سفر الخروج يشرح كيف خلّص الله إس: If the Book of Exodus explains how God saved Israel from Egypt, then Leviticus explains how Israel is to live after salvation. Salvation created a covenant relationship, and God’s presence in the midst of the congregation created the necessity of an order that defines how to approach God and how to deal with sin, impurity, and worship.
والسفر يريد أن يرسخ في ذهن إسرائيل أن ال: The book wants to establish firmly in Israel’s mind that God is not an ordinary god who can be approached according to human desires, but is the Holy One. Therefore, sacrifices, priesthood, purity, festivals, and commandments all appear within one framework: the holiness of God and the necessity of the holiness of his people.
والآية التي تلخص قلب السفر هي:: And the verse that summarizes the heart of the book is:
«تكونون قديسين لأني أنا قدوس»: “You shall be holy, for I am holy”
وهنا لا تكون القداسة مجرد مجموعة من القو: Here, holiness is not merely a collection of external rules, but a reflection of God’s own identity.
5. العلاقة بين الخروج واللاويين: 5. The Relationship between Exodus and Leviticus
نهاية سفر الخروج وبداية سفر اللاويين يجب: The end of Exodus and the beginning of Leviticus should not be read separately, because there is a clear theological progression between them. In Exodus, the tabernacle is constructed and the glory of the Lord fills it; then Leviticus begins within this same context, as the Lord calls Moses and speaks to him from the tent of meeting.
وهذا يعني أن السؤال الذي طرحه الخروج هو:: This means that the question posed by Exodus is:
كيف يسكن الله وسط شعبه؟: How does God dwell among his people?
بينما السؤال الذي يجيب عنه اللاويين هو:: Whereas the question answered by Leviticus is:

والعبارة المتكررة في هذا القسم هي أن إسر: The recurring statement in this section is that Israel must be distinct from the nations surrounding it because the God who chose Israel is holy. ومن أجمل الإعلانات الأخلاقية في هذا القس: Among the most beautiful ethical declarations in this section is:
«تحب قريبك كنفسك»: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself”

يعرض الإصحاح الثالث والعشرون قائمة بالمو: Chapter twenty-three presents a list of the sacred seasons and feasts, including the Sabbath, Passover, the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the firstfruits of the harvest, the Feast of Weeks, the Feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and the Feast of Booths.

وهكذا يصبح الزمن نفسه جزءًا من العبادة؛: Thus time itself becomes part of worship; the people remember God not only in the sanctuary, but also remember his deeds on specific days and seasons repeated through the generations.
في لاويين 25 تظهر فكرة السبت للأرض ثم سن: In Leviticus 25, the idea of the Sabbath for the land appears, followed by the year of Jubilee. ويأتي اليوبيل ليضع نظامًا يعيد ترتيب بعض: The Jubilee establishes a system that restores certain conditions of land ownership, servitude, and debt, and prevents exploitation from accumulating without end. This idea reflects the principle that God is the true owner of the land and the people.

18. أهم رسالة يقدمها سفر اللاويين: 18. The Most Important Message Presented by Leviticus
يمكن اختصار الرسالة الأساسية في العبارة:: The central message can be summarized in the statement:
الشعب الذي خلصه الله ودعا إلى العهد يجب: The people whom God redeemed and called into the covenant must live in holiness before the holy God.
وهذه الرسالة تمنعنا من قراءة اللاويين كك: This message prevents us from reading Leviticus as a book of rigid laws. The sacrifices, priesthood, purity, festivals, holiness, and Jubilee are all parts of one question: How can sinful human beings live in the presence of God?
والإجابة التي يقدمها السفر هي أن الاقترا: The answer presented by the book is that approaching God requires atonement, mediation, purity, obedience, and holiness.
سفر اللاويين من أغنى أسفار العهد القديم: Leviticus is one of the richest books of the Old Testament for understanding the work of Christ, not because every detail in it should be turned into a direct symbol, but because the system of sacrifices, priesthood, and atonement establishes the theological framework that the New Testament uses to explain the cross.

تجري أحداث اللاويين في فترة البرية بعد ا: The events of Leviticus take place during the wilderness period after the exodus from Egypt and before entering the land of Canaan, with the tent of meeting in the vicinity of Mount Sinai as their central setting. «لوقا» هو الاسم الذي ارتبط بالكاتب التقل: “Luke” is the name traditionally associated with the author of the third Gospel, and it is a common Greek name in the Roman world. His Gospel is considered the first part of a unified two-part work, followed by the Book of Acts, so that the first begins with what Christ did and taught, while the second continues the extension of his work through the Holy Spirit and the church.
ينسب التقليد المسيحي المبكر الإنجيل إلى: Early Christian tradition attributes the Gospel to Luke, the physician whom Paul mentions in his letters. His association with Paul appears clearly in certain passages of Acts that use the “we” form, indicating that he accompanied Paul on some of his journeys. Luke does not mention his name within the Gospel, but in the preface he presents himself as a researcher who collected reports from the earliest eyewitnesses and arranged them accurately.

10. اهتمام لوقا بالفقراء والمهمشين: 10. Luke’s Concern for the Poor and Marginalized
من السمات البارزة في الإنجيل اهتمامه بمن: One of the Gospel’s prominent features is its concern for those on the margins of social and religious life. This is evident in the stories of the Good Samaritan, the prodigal son, Zacchaeus the tax collector, the sinful woman, Lazarus the poor man, and others. This does not mean that Luke presents a social gospel separate from salvation; rather, he proclaims that God’s grace reaches people where they are and restores their dignity and relationship with God.
يبرز لوقا حياة الصلاة في شخص المسيح بصور: Luke clearly highlights the prayer life of Christ, mentioning his prayer at his baptism, before choosing the Twelve, at the Transfiguration, in Gethsemane, and on the cross. Thus, prayer appears not as a secondary part of Christ’s life, but as an essential element of his relationship with the Father and of his ministry.
ينفرد لوقا أو يتميز في تسجيل عدد من الأم: Luke alone, or with particular distinction, records a number of important parables, such as the Good Samaritan, the Rich Fool, the Prodigal Son, the Rich Man and Lazarus, and the Pharisee and the Tax Collector. These parables reveal the heart of Christ’s message concerning mercy, repentance, forgiveness, love of neighbor, and the danger of relying on self-righteousness and wealth.

The journey does not appear to be merely a geographical movement, but a theological road on which Christ deliberately moves toward the cross while teaching his disciples about the kingdom, discipleship, prayer, and mercy.
يظهر المسيح في لوقا قريبًا من الإنسان بص: In Luke, Christ appears close to people regardless of their background. He interacts with sinners, tax collectors, women, the sick, strangers, the poor, and the rich. This concern reaches its climax in the story of Zacchaeus, where Christ declares: “For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.”
لا يقدم لوقا الصليب باعتباره مأساة غير م: Luke does not present the cross as an unexpected tragedy, but as the fulfillment of God’s revealed purpose. Christ appears on the cross in an image of mercy and forgiveness, saying, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do,” and then entrusting his spirit to the Father in confidence.
تأتي القيامة باعتبارها إعلانًا لانتصار ا: The resurrection comes as a declaration of Christ’s victory and the fulfillment of what he had previously told his disciples. Luke is distinguished by the story of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus, where Christ explains that what happened was not outside God’s purpose, but that “the Christ should suffer these things and enter into his glory.”
17. أهم شخصيات إنجيل لوقا: 17. Major Figures in the Gospel of Luke
تتمحور القصة حول يسوع المسيح، ويبرز إلى: The story centers on Jesus Christ, alongside whom John the Baptist, Mary, Joseph, Zechariah, Elizabeth, Simeon, Anna, and the disciples come into prominence, in addition to figures such as Mary Magdalene, Zacchaeus, Martha, Mary, and others. Luke also gives a clear place to the poor, sinners, the sick, and the Gentiles as part of the scene that reveals the breadth of salvation.
رسالة لوقا هي أن الخلاص الذي أعده الله ف: Luke’s message is that the salvation God prepared in Christ has come into the world, and that Jesus is the Savior who seeks the lost, welcomes the repentant, and opens the way of salvation to all peoples. Therefore, the Gospel brings together individual salvation, God’s mercy, repentance, the cross, and the resurrection, then naturally prepares for the transition to the spread of the Gospel in the Book of Acts.
19. الحركة الكبرى لإنجيل لوقا: 19. The Major Movement of Luke’s Gospel
يبدأ إنجيل لوقا بالإعلان الدقيق عن الأحد: The Gospel of Luke begins with a precise account of the events that led to the appearance of Jesus Christ. John the Baptist appears as the forerunner who prepares the way, and then Christ is born in Bethlehem, declaring that God’s promise of salvation has entered history. After his baptism and temptation, Jesus begins his ministry in the power of the Holy Spirit, proclaiming the kingdom, healing the sick, forgiving sins, and declaring God’s mercy to sinners, the poor, and the marginalized, while it gradually becomes clear that he is the Savior who came to seek and save the lost. Then the decisive journey toward Jerusalem begins, where he teaches his disciples about repentance, prayer, mercy, and discipleship, and reveals that the way to glory passes through the cross. In Jerusalem, Christ is handed over, crucified, and dies, but he rises on the third day and explains to his disciples that his sufferings and resurrection were part of God’s purpose revealed in the Scriptures. The Gospel ends at a new boundary, as the risen Christ moves from being the subject of testimony to being the source of the mission, and the disciples prepare to be his witnesses to all nations. This opens the way directly to the Book of Acts.
يرتبط لوقا بالعهد القديم ارتباطًا واضحًا: Luke is clearly connected with the Old Testament, especially in the birth narratives, the praises of Mary, Zechariah, and Simeon, and the use of images and promises from the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms. He presents Christ as the fulfillment of God’s promises to Israel, but the fulfillment of these promises does not stop with Israel; it extends to the Gentiles, as appears powerfully at the conclusion of the Gospel.

The first focuses on Christ’s ministry, death, and resurrection, while the second focuses on the continuation of his witness and the spread of the Gospel through the apostles and the Holy Spirit. Therefore, the end of Luke is not a closed conclusion, but a transition from Christ’s work in the flesh to the continuation of testimony to the risen Christ through the power of the Holy Spirit.

It presents Jesus Christ as the fulfillment of God’s promises, the one anointed by the Holy Spirit, the physician who came to the sick, the shepherd who seeks the lost, the Savior who welcomes the repentant, and the Lord who deliberately walks toward the cross. Luke emphasizes that salvation is not confined to one group, class, or social background, but extends to everyone who believes in Christ, repents, and returns to God. The story ends with the resurrection and preparation for witness, making the life of Christ in the Gospel the foundation of the worldwide mission that will spread through the Book of Acts.

It addresses a people who had returned from exile, rebuilt the temple, and apparently restored worship, but the problem had become deeper: the heart itself had turned away from God. Therefore, Malachi confronts not so much overt idolatry as spiritual coldness, formal worship, corrupt priesthood, marital unfaithfulness, injustice, doubt concerning God’s justice, and the theft of what belongs to him. The book ends with a twofold promise: the Lord will come to his temple, and before the coming of the great day of the Lord, “Elijah the prophet” will come to prepare the way. سفر ملاخي يكشف أن أخطر حالة روحية ليست أ: The Book of Malachi reveals that the most dangerous spiritual condition is not for a person to abandon religion completely, but to continue practicing worship while losing the fear of God in the heart. Therefore, He confronted the people with a series of questions that reveal that the problem was not the absence of religion but the absence of the heart. He called them to return to Him and to reform worship, leadership, marriage, giving, and justice. Then He declared that the coming of the Lord would reveal everything, that the Lord would come to His temple to purify and refine, and that the day of the Lord would come, bringing judgment upon evil and healing for those who fear Him. Therefore, the book ends not by closing the story but by opening the door of expectation: the messenger will come, the Lord will come, the Sun of Righteousness will rise, and God will finally declare who truly serves Him.

اسم «مرقس» مرتبط بالاسم اللاتيني Marcus،: The name “Mark” is associated with the Latin name Marcus, a Roman name that was common in the ancient world. In the New Testament, a person appears who bears the name “John who was called Mark.” He is associated with the house of Mary, the mother of John, in Jerusalem; he later appeared in ministry with Barnabas and Paul and afterward became especially associated with Peter, so that Peter mentions him in his letter as “Mark, my son.” Early Christian tradition preserved the name Mark as the author of the second Gospel and connected his writing especially with Peter's testimony. This tradition is supported by early ecclesiastical sources, although the author's name does not explicitly appear within the text of the Gospel itself.
ينسب التقليد المسيحي القديم إنجيل مرقس إ: Ancient Christian tradition attributes the Gospel of Mark to John Mark, the person who appears in the Book of Acts and the New Testament epistles. Mark was associated with Barnabas and Paul at the beginning of ministry, then became clearly associated with Peter. At the end of his ministry, Paul refers to Mark's usefulness in ministry after an earlier period of disagreement concerning his accompanying them. Peter mentions Mark affectionately as “Mark, my son,” which led ancient tradition to associate him especially with Peter's testimony. The testimony of Papias, preserved by Eusebius, states that Mark was Peter's interpreter or translator and that he faithfully recorded what he remembered of the sayings and deeds of Christ, even if the order of his narrative was not strictly chronological.
ومن المهم التمييز بين التقليد وبين البره: It is important to distinguish between tradition and internal evidence: the Gospel itself does not name its author, and therefore its attribution to John Mark depends to a great extent on early Christian testimony. Nevertheless, this testimony is sufficiently ancient and early to give the attribution of the Gospel to Mark significant historical weight, even as academic discussion continues concerning the extent of Peter's direct relationship to the material contained in the Gospel.
لا يقدم الكتاب المقدس معلومات عن سنة ميل: The Bible provides no information concerning the year of Mark's birth or the year of his death; therefore, no precise date can be determined for these two events. What can be known from the New Testament is that his name was John, that he was the son of a woman named Mary, that her house in Jerusalem was a place where believers gathered, that he accompanied Barnabas and Paul during a stage of ministry, and that he was later associated with Peter and with Paul's ministry. The multiple references to him reveal that his life was not marginal in the history of the early church; rather, he was part of the network of apostolic ministry that extended between Jerusalem and other regions of the early Christian world.
أما الروايات اللاحقة عن نهاية حياته وخدم: As for later accounts concerning the end of his life and his ministry in particular places, their details cannot be presented as certain biblical facts. They should therefore remain within the framework of ecclesiastical tradition rather than that of established biblical history.
4. لمن كتب الإنجيل؟: 4. For Whom Was the Gospel Written?
يظهر من إنجيل مرقس اهتمام واضح بجمهور غي: The Gospel of Mark shows a clear concern for a Gentile audience, or at least for an audience that needs explanations of certain Jewish customs and terms. When Mark uses Aramaic words such as “Talitha cumi,” “Ephphatha,” and “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani,” he provides the reader with an explanation of their meanings. He also explains certain Jewish customs relating to purity and the washing of hands, as well as some geographical and cultural expressions. This style makes it likely that Mark's audience included a large number of Gentiles and may have been associated with a Roman setting. This is consistent with the ancient tradition that connected the writing of the Gospel with the city of Rome, although identifying the place of writing does not reach the level of historical certainty.
ولا ينبغي اختزال جمهور مرقس في جماعة واح: Mark's audience should not be reduced categorically to a single community, because the Gospel spread among the early churches and its readers likely included Jews, Gentiles, and different social groups. Yet it is clear that Mark writes in a way that makes the message of Christ understandable to the reader who does not live directly within the Jewish setting.
الهدف الأساسي من إنجيل مرقس هو إعلان يسو: The primary purpose of the Gospel of Mark is to proclaim Jesus Christ, the Son of God, through a vivid and rapid account of His life, ministry, suffering, and resurrection. Mark does not begin with the birth narrative or genealogy; instead, he begins directly with the ministry of John the Baptist and then the appearance of Christ, as though the reader is driven from the first sentence to confront the central question: Who is Jesus? The miracles, teaching, casting out of demons, healing, and authority over nature follow as successive testimonies to Christ's authority and identity.
وفي الوقت نفسه لا يسمح مرقس للقارئ أن يف: At the same time, Mark does not allow the reader to understand Christ through miracles alone, because the path gradually moves toward the cross. The Christ who appears as the one possessing authority is Himself the Son of Man who “must suffer many things” and who came “to serve and to give Himself as a ransom for many.” Thus, Mark brings together authority, service, the cross, and the resurrection in one story.
6. زمن كتابة الإنجيل: 6. Date of Writing of the Gospel
لا يحدد إنجيل مرقس تاريخًا صريحًا لكتابت: The Gospel of Mark does not specify an explicit date for its composition; consequently, scholars differ in determining the precise year. The broad academic view places the writing of the Gospel in the sixties or near 70 A.D., while some studies connect the text to the events of the Jewish-Roman War and the destruction of the temple in 70 A.D. The discussion depends especially on the interpretation of chapter thirteen, where Christ speaks about the destruction of the temple, persecution, tribulations, and the coming of the Son of Man.
وتظل المسألة الزمنية محل نقاش، ولذلك لا: The chronological question remains debated; therefore, it is not appropriate to present a single year as an established fact. However, placing Mark in the second half of the first century, especially in the sixties or around 70 A.D., accords with a substantial body of modern scholarship. The tradition that connects the Gospel with Rome and with a period of persecution of believers also provides an important background for understanding Mark's concern with suffering, perseverance, and discipleship.
7. الموضوع الرئيسي للإنجيل: 7. The Main Theme of the Gospel
الموضوع المركزي في إنجيل مرقس هو يسوع ال: The central theme of the Gospel of Mark is Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who came to proclaim the kingdom of God, serve humanity, and give Himself as a ransom for many. Mark presents Christ as possessing authority over disease, demons, nature, and death, yet he also presents this authority within the framework of service, humility, and obedience unto death.
وهنا تظهر إحدى أهم مفارقات الإنجيل: المس: Here one of the Gospel's most important paradoxes appears: Christ is declared to be the Son of God not only in moments of power and miracles, but with exceptional clarity at the cross, when the centurion says after His death, “Truly this man was the Son of God.” Thus, the cross becomes an essential part of the revelation of Christ's identity, rather than merely a tragic end to His life.

Yet Mark does not present the kingdom as an abstract idea; rather, he makes it present in Christ's deeds, teaching, and authority over the powers of evil, disease, nature, and death. The kingdom is at hand because the King Himself has come, and God's authority is manifested concretely in the ministry of Jesus.
وتوضح أمثال الأصحاح الرابع طبيعة هذا الم: The parables of the fourth chapter explain the nature of this kingdom, for they show that the work of God may begin in a way that appears small and unnoticed, yet it grows powerfully until it reaches the goal God desires. Thus Mark brings together the hidden beginning of the kingdom and its final power, and the word of God that is sown and the authority of God that accomplishes His purpose.

10. يوحنا المعمدان وبداية الطريق: 10. John the Baptist and the Beginning of the Way
يبدأ مرقس بخدمة يوحنا المعمدان، فيظهر في: Mark begins with the ministry of John the Baptist, showing him in the wilderness calling for repentance and the baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, fulfilling the prophecy that speaks of preparing the way before the Lord. عندما يعتمد يسوع في الأردن تنفتح السماوا: When Jesus is baptized in the Jordan, the heavens open and the Spirit descends upon Him like a dove, and the voice from heaven says, 'You are My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.' ولا تمثل المعمودية مجرد طقس افتتاحي للخد: The baptism does not represent merely an introductory rite for the ministry, but a moment of divine declaration regarding Jesus' identity before He enters the conflict with Satan and before His ministry begins in Galilee. بعد المعمودية يقود الروح المسيح إلى البر: After the baptism, the Spirit leads Christ into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil, but Mark narrates the account in a highly compressed manner compared with Matthew and Luke. وتكشف التجربة أن طريق المسيح نحو الملكوت: The temptation reveals that the path of Christ toward the kingdom does not pass through the use of power independently of the Father's will, but begins with obedience. يمر المسيح على شاطئ بحر الجليل ويدعو سمع: Jesus passes along the shore of the Sea of Galilee and calls Simon and Andrew, James and John, and the call comes directly: 'Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of people.' The men immediately respond, leaving their nets and their work to follow Him.
وتكشف هذه الدعوة طبيعة التلمذة في مرقس؛: This call reveals the nature of discipleship in Mark: the disciple is not merely a person who receives information from Christ, but a person who leaves his old way and enters the way of Christ. منذ بداية خدمته يظهر يسوع في مرقس صاحب س: From the beginning of His ministry, Jesus appears in Mark as One with unique authority, for He teaches in a way that astonishes people, casts out demons, heals the sick, forgives sins, and commands nature so that it obeys Him. وهكذا يربط مرقس بين كلمة المسيح وسلطانه؛: Thus Mark links the word of Christ with His authority; He does not merely present religious ideas, but speaks and the powers of the spiritual and natural world respond to Him. Yet the authority possessed by Christ does not become a display, but is always directed toward the service of humanity and the proclamation of the kingdom of God.
15. شفاء المفلوج وغفران الخطايا: 15. The Healing of the Paralytic and the Forgiveness of Sins
عندما يأتي الرجال بالمفلوج إلى يسوع، لا: When men bring the paralytic to Jesus, He does not begin by saying that He will heal his body, but says to him, 'Son, your sins are forgiven.' يقدم مرقس في الأصحاح الرابع مجموعة من أم: In chapter four, Mark presents a group of parables of the kingdom, beginning with the parable of the sower.
